# CLAUDE.md — 识字 Zeichentrainer

Working language: **English.** Reply to H in English. Short, direct, no excessive politeness.

## What this is
Chinese character trainer for adults (spaced repetition), a reinterpretation of 悟空识字 without the kids' aesthetic.
**The rule (H, 2026-09-14): "Flash cards are for learning and multi cards are for looking up stuff."** A flashcard is studied — it has a progress row, a due date, a grade, a star, a place in Learn and in the Deck count. A multicard (a page card, v453) and its own texts are looked up — nothing on them is studied, counted, scheduled or graded, and the only thing a multicard text can do is generate a separate flashcard (v487). Every control, label, count and filter is judged against that one sentence; v487, v488, v491, v493, v496, v497 and v498 are its applications, and a later change that puts a learning word or a learning control on a multicard, or a look-up-only surface on a flashcard, is wrong by construction.
User: H, product manager, Beijing, **phone-only (Android/Xiaomi, Chrome, VPN), no computer**.
UI language: English. Learning content: Chinese + pinyin + English meaning.

## Live deployment
- Repo: `henglicam/zeichentrainer` · GitHub Pages, branch `main`, folder `/ (root)`.
- URL: `https://henglicam.github.io/zeichentrainer/`
- Push to `main` → Pages rebuilds automatically (~1–2 min). `index.html` must stay in the repo root.
- The site is **public** (free plan). User data lives exclusively on the device (IndexedDB), never in the repo; the only thing the app sends on its own is the daily anonymous usage row (v170, below), and that can be switched off.

- **The first field round on the write pad, answered as one version (v518, H, 2026-09-18, eight items in one message after v517 landed: "I don't get out of the character locked mode anymore · Vibration there doesn't work · Locked on/off should be more obvious, maybe with a padlock icon? · Completing a row of characters: when automatically jumping to next, pinyin and meaning under the pad don't follow. And they should Always be visible · Cards overview should follow layout. Without drawing pad: edit, star, etc instead · No 'also in other cards' in learn mode. Only on Cards mode. · Swiping cards in learn mode somehow jumps the image … Swiping shouldn't be only possible on the image, all other areas as well, except maybe the pad. · The left and right arrows next to the pad change cards, but that design won't win an award … better ideas?"):** seven built, the eighth answered with three proposals and not built (a design ask waits for a "go"). **(1) The lock's release.** Driven with real touch events through CDP on a v517 root, a *tap* on the locked character released it exactly as v513 says, so the tap path was never broken — what H did is what his own phase-6 prompt says he would do, **press and hold again**, and until v517 a second hold on the locked character re-locked it (`longPress(b,()=>lockChar(...))`, no branch for the locked one) while the hint that says "tap it" is gone after 20 reviews. A hold on the locked character releases now, the tap still does, and the hint and the guide's Learn sentence say both (one key replaced in nine columns, the old one gone — its only other user is `WHATS_NEW[513]`, whose text differs). **(2) The buzz** was `navigator.vibrate(12)` at every site since v354, and 12 ms is under what most phone motors render at all; **no field run has ever confirmed a buzz** — v354's, v513's and v517's are all "not yet field-checked". One helper `buzz(p)`: 40 ms for a hold, `[30,60,30]` for the release, 20 for a finished character. **It cannot be measured here** — the harness stubs `navigator.vibrate` and counts calls — so the phone is the only check, and if 40 ms is still silent the next suspect is MIUI's own haptics switch rather than the app. **(3) A padlock** (`MARK_LOCK`, an inline SVG disc in the button's top-right corner, `.lockmark`, inverted on the current character) on the locked character's button on every card of the walk, gone at the release. **(4) The line under the pad is always there and follows the pad.** v517 showed it only behind the open answer or after a tap, and the lit word was the tapped one (`S.wordCh`) — so when the pad moved on to the next character by itself the line stayed on the old word and the tile stayed lit on it. Both are the pad's now: the lit word is the word of the character the pad is on (`litWi=cur?cur.wi:null`), `padLine(d,cur)` runs on every render, the `hidden` attribute and the tap-off are gone, `S.wordCh` and `wordOn` with them. Measured: on landing the line reads the first word with the answer folded; two characters written by real strokes move the pad to 供 and the line and the light to 供应 without a tap. **And the line has to be in the pad's budget, which the first cut of this version missed and the ratio measurement below caught before the merge:** `fit` still counted v517's `PAD_BELOW` 46 for what sits under the pad, so with the line always there the card ran 121 px under the tab bar at 390 × 844 and 53 on H's folded screen (`cardEnd` 904 against `nav` 783) while the pad-above-the-bar check stayed green — the overflow was below the pad, which that check never looked at. `PAD_BELOW` is **84** (the line at its two-row height plus the helper row's margin) and `.padline` carries `min-height:61px`, so a one-character word does not change the pad; measured under the pad with hints off: line 61, helper row 0, the card ending at 759 against the bar's 783. **What the line costs, named:** at 390 × 844 the pad is **289 px** now and no longer the card's 322 — the v517 symmetry H asked for holds on his own folded screen (393 × 917: pad 325, the width cap) and on the unfolded one, and gives 33 px back to the line on the common phone size; the swipe hint of the first twenty reviews stays outside the budget, as v517 decided, and scrolls the card by 93 px until it goes. **(5) The open card is the study card without the pad** (`detailCardHTML`): the photo in the one 2:1 box, the character row grouped by word, the answer block **open** — this screen is for looking a card up — folded by its own button (`#d-fold`, `S.detailHide` is that fold now; the tap on the picture only swaps crop and whole photo), the line under it for a tapped character (`S.detailCh`, held with the card; the same character again puts it out, since there is no pad here to keep it), and **the six actions inside the card where the pad would stand** (`detailActsHTML`); the schedule line and the linked-photos row stay under the card on the pane. The character row is one helper for all three screens (`chrowHTML`: the study card, its carousel neighbour and the detail), so they cannot drift. Four keys go dead with the old preview's hints ("Tap the character to show / hide the answer", ", or the photo for the whole picture / for the text alone") and leave nine columns (the v403 rule): **474 → 470 a column, ru 503 → 499, en 14**, no duplicate in any of the ten. **(6) No linked-photos row on the study card**; the detail keeps it. **(7) The swipe.** The jump was the neighbour's box: `makePeer` drew it with `frontPic(nd,{page:true})` — no `fixed` — and a page front took the general `.picbox.page{aspect-ratio:var(--ratio)}` rule, since the peer is `.card.peer` and not `.card.study`; a three-line neighbour came in at 4:3 (242 px) and snapped to 2:1 (161). `fixed:true` on the peer and `.card.peer .picbox.page{aspect-ratio:2}`; measured mid-stroke, the neighbour's box is as tall as the card's own (161 == 161) and nothing moves at the snap. And the surface: `wireSwipe` stood down on every button, which on the study card is the whole character row and the fold; it stands down only on the pad, the helper row, the chevrons, fields and chips now, and on **a character row that scrolls** — `.chrow` is `overflow-x:hidden` by default and takes `.scrolls` (`overflow-x:auto`, `touch-action:pan-x pan-y`) only when it is wider than the card (`chrowScrolls`, measured after each render), because a scrolling row owns the horizontal pan and a swipe there would fight it. **What that costs, named:** a card whose row overflows — 骑车勿盯还车勿忘 does at 390 px, six tiles at 428 px against 322 — is swiped from the photo, the fold, the answer or the line, not from its row. **(8) The chevrons: three proposals, not built** — see the report to H; the guide's "or tap the arrows beside the pad" sentence stands until he picks. **(9) A finished card stays folded** (H, minutes later: "Pinyin and meaning open after completing writing a card. Makes card jump, shouldn't."): `cardDone` opened the answer block on the last stroke since v512, and the block appearing above the pad pushed the pad down; with the line under the pad carrying the word's pinyin and meaning since (4), the block has nothing left to say there and stays folded — the fold button opens it, and the release of a locked character (v513) still opens it on purpose. the line on landing with the answer folded and the pad's word lit without a tap, two characters written by real strokes moving line and light to 供应, a tap on 应 reading it inside its word, the second tap leaving both; a card on another photo with no linked row in Learn; the detail as the study card with its 2:1 box, row, open answer with pinyin, no pad, the six actions inside the card, the linked row and no overflow, the fold's button, a tapped character lit and read, the second tap putting it out; the fold button as a swipe surface, the three-line neighbour's box as tall as the card's mid-stroke with nothing moving at the snap, a character button as a swipe surface on a row that fits, the pad never one, an overflowing row scrolling instead; and its "the pad is as wide as the card" retargeted at 289 ≤ 322, the cost named above) and `verify-writepad` (54) ALL OK with four checks retargeted — v517's "the same character tapped again puts the word out" and "the lit word does not survive onto the next card", and v512's "the line under the pad is hidden while the answer is folded" and "the whole card written: the answer block opens", each the contract this version reverses on purpose; - **One geometry on every card, the real Kai outlines as the template, a tap that reads a word, and a star for a finished one (v517, H on the three proposals put to him as screenshots from the real app: "Implement your recommendations", then mid-turn "You also don't need clear and undo at the bottom", then "Implement this only … plus highlight words", then "Misunderstanding. apply the L1 / brush / outlines / praise patch. Plus highlight words"):** phase 5 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, four things in one deploy. **(1) The photo box and the pad are constants, and the reason they were not is arithmetic rather than taste.** Two zones grew with the photo's line count at the same time — v514's picture ratio (2:1 / 3:2 / 4:3) and the character buttons' one row per line — so they compounded and the pad took what was left: **measured at 390 × 844 with the answer folded, photo 161/215/242, buttons 60/128/196, pad 309/200/200, the card running 6/19/114 px past the tab bar**, and the pad narrower than the picture above it (309 against 322), which is the asymmetry H was looking at. Now the study card's box is **`FRONT_RATIO` 2** whatever the text (`frontPic(d,{fixed:true})`, `.card.study .picbox.page{aspect-ratio:2}`) — **the picture is still CUT at v514's per-line ratio and fitted inside with the v232 blurred fill, and the card detail still shows each card's own shape**, which is `verify-recut4`'s own control — and the characters are **one row that scrolls sideways** (`.chrow` row/nowrap/`overflow-x:auto`, each photo line still its own `.chline` group with a hairline between). `fit` then measures the same numbers on every card: it takes the answer block's height back off the top (so **opening the answer no longer shrinks the pad**, 322 → 322 where v516 went 252 → 200) and counts a constant **`PAD_BELOW` 46** instead of whatever actually sits under the pad, so the helper row appearing, the swipe hint and the linked-photos row make the card scroll rather than the pad shrink. **Measured: photo 161 and pad 322 on a one-, two- and three-line card at 390 px, 238 at 360 px, nothing overflowing sideways in either.** **Undo and Clear leave the helper row** (H, mid-session) and are drawn only for a character the stroke set lacks, where the learner really is drawing freehand — both handlers are null-guarded, since the buttons may not exist. **(2) The template is the real Kai outline.** Until v516 a template stroke was a constant-width round-capped polyline through the raw median samples, and those samples wobble — the first stroke of 我 runs y 348, 350, 358, 370, 368, 378 — so every sample showed as a kink; a stroke of even thickness cannot read as writing whatever it follows. **`vendor/outlines.txt.gz` (7.31 MB gzipped, 9,534 characters)** carries the true Arphic Kai outline of every stroke, out of the same `graphics.txt` the medians come from, quantised onto a 256 grid (**measured against the raw paths and the 512 grid: indistinguishable, including the 12,255 paths that carry a negative coordinate**) and stored y-up, flipped at draw time by the transform `translate(off,off) scale(k,-k) translate(0,-OUT_Y0)` — our medians are `900 − y` of the source, verified on 丁 and 我. It is **loaded in the background after the medians and nothing waits for it** (`loadOutlines`, through `vendorFetch`, cached in `zt-ocr-v1`), and it is **deliberately not in `OCR_FILES`** — the v401 trap, where one non-reader entry silently kills `warmReader` for every existing user. Until it lands, and for any character it lacks or whose stroke count disagrees (`outlinesFor`), **`brushPath` draws instead**: the samples smoothed (Chaikin, twice) and given a width along the stroke from its own inferred kind (`strokeKind` — 横/竖/撇/捺/点 and their hooks, from direction, length and the turn at the tail; the median file carries no stroke type, so a wrong guess costs a stroke drawn a little too evenly, never a wrong shape). The learner's own ink is smoothed by the same Chaikin and keeps its even width. "Show me" still animates along the centreline, since a fraction of a filled outline is not a thing. **(3) A tap lights the whole word and reads it** — H's own framing, and it needed no new data model: `padTargets` already returns `wi`/`word`/`wstart` per character and `groupRow` already renders one `.chw` per dictionary word, so the tile only needed lighting (`.chw.on`). The line under the pad carries the word with the tapped character marked, its pinyin and meaning, **and a second row for the single character** when the word has more than one — **its syllable taken out of the word's own pinyin rather than looked up alone**, so 应 in 供应 reads **yìng** and not its isolated yīng. The same character tapped again puts the word out; the tap still picks the character to write, so nothing the pad could do before is lost; the lit word is held with its card (`S.wordCh={c,i}`) and cannot survive onto the next one. **One thing this exposed and fixed:** `bestSense` skipped surnames, variants and abbreviations but not a Taiwan-pronunciation note, so 应 came out meaning "Taiwan pr." — it skips that too now, which also mends the parts row. **(4) A finished word is praised** (§ 12): a star lifts out of the pad and flies an arc into a **counter at the right of the top bar**, which then **stays while the day has points in it** — a counter to watch grow rather than a receipt that fades, so the bar does not jump twice a card — and the praise is proportional: a card written clean sends a **gold** star with a ring spreading out of the pad, a card that needed a Skip sends a plain one. `NEXT_MS` **900 → 1500**, a tap anywhere on the card that is not a control skips straight on, `prefers-reduced-motion` keeps the pause and the number and drops the travel, and the star's origin is **clamped to the visible part of the pad**, since the answer block opening can push the pad below the fold. **Nothing about the schedule, the grade, the points arithmetic or the repeat pass changes** — the counter reads `daily[day].w`, the figure More → Progress already calls "Written today", and no key was needed in any column (the label reuses `"Written today"`, 474 a column, ru 503, en 14, `lang.js` byte-identical). Suite `verify-onewidth` (29 checks: the box and the pad identical across one-, two- and three-line cards with the pad as wide as the card and whole above the tab bar; every photo line still its own group; the answer block leaving the pad alone; no Undo/Clear on a template character and both on a free one; the outlines loading, matching stroke for stroke and being refused when they do not; the tap lighting exactly the word's characters, the two lines, the character's in-word reading, the tap-off, another word taking the light, a one-character word getting one line, and the light not surviving the card; the star, the gold and the ring on a clean card, the counter, the origin on screen, the tap skipping, the dwell, and the counter staying) — **ALL OK on v517; on a v516 root 7 of its first 10 checks fail and the run then dies at the missing `OUTLINE_OF`**, and the 2 that pass on both are labelled controls. `verify-lockwalk` (22), `verify-hdrfilter` (23), `verify-newflag` (27) and `verify-piczoom` (11) ALL OK; **`verify-writepad` (54) ALL OK with three hardcoded waits retargeted** — it slept 1100 ms for the old 900 ms dwell, and a suite that pins a number breaks on every change to it, so it reads `NEXT_MS` from the page (the v413 lesson); **`verify-recut4` (19) ALL OK with one check retargeted**, its "the study card's box of a two-line card measures 3:2" being the v514 contract this version reverses on purpose, with the detail's per-card ratio directly above it as the control. **A harness lesson worth keeping:** a pixel-exact synthetic stroke never registers, because identical coordinates fire no `pointermove` — `verify-writepad`'s own helper has always added jitter, and the new suite must too; and a fixed 0..n-1 stroke run races the pad, whose finished character holds a 300 ms flash before moving on, so the writer follows `S.pad.k` instead. Checked by screenshot in light, German dark and at 360 px: the outline template, mid-write, the lit word with its two lines, the star and ring with the counter. A `WHATS_NEW` line, four `TO_TEST` lines. **What it costs, named:** the characters no longer sit one row per photo line, so a two-line sign is one long row and a long text has to be scrolled to reach its last characters; **7.31 MB** lands on the phone once; every finished card holds 600 ms longer, about 12 s over a twenty-card session, skippable with a tap; and the counter takes 62 px of the top bar, so a long filter name is cut about 50 px sooner than at v516. Not yet field-checked — H's next session is the check: the pad the same size on every card, the template reading as writing rather than wire, a tap on a word he does not know, and the star.

- **A card from a photo is "not yet checked" until the act of checking clears it, and the flag means "wrong" again (v515, H: "go for 3 and 4" — phase 4 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, § 9 —, then, on the first cut that flagged every photo card with the note "new — check text, pinyin and meaning": "Make better suggestion for flagging", and "Go" on the design below; the first cut was pushed and replaced under the same number before anything was deployed):** with every new card flagged the ⚑ meant two things at once — "the app is unsure" (v325) and "H has not looked yet" — so the Flagged filter lost its signal and its count grew by one with every photo until a tap took it off. **The state is its own field, `unchecked:true`**, born on every card `readingCard` builds — the automatic card, Save now (whose card `finishPending` fills from the built card), every label of a split panel and the preview's own Save card — and inherited by a flashcard generated from a multicard text (`makeFlashcard`, the v503 shape); a card typed in the Add form is the learner's own and is born checked; absent = checked, so every card from before v515 is checked and export and import carry the field with no line of their own. **It is cleared by checking, never by a tap on it** (`checkCard`): the first full write in Learn (`cardDone`, with the answer block opening), the card detail opened (`renderCardDetail`, the write landing behind the render), an edit saved or an AI suggestion accepted (`applyCardUpdate`), and the flag set by hand (`setFlag` on — a verdict is a look). A swipe past, a chevron and a tab tap clear nothing. **The ⚑ is v514's again:** the `SIGN` records are born without it, the v143 guard tests `!sg.flag` as before, and the note key of the first cut is gone from nine columns; v245's Save-now note and v325's "the reading looks unsure" stand where they stood. **What H sees:** a row **Not yet checked (N)** in the filter sheet — on Cards in the Status group, an OR beside Flagged (v366), counting the open tab's own (v477: the Cards tab counts the flashcards, the Multicards tab a page once through its texts), shown only while a card is unchecked and dropped by `normaliseFilters` when the last one is checked (the v308 rule); on Learn its own Status group beside Starred (`learnNew`, the star's shape: the session then holds every unchecked card with the eight-new cap lifted, v429, and stands down when none is left) — and **the session puts unchecked cards first inside the due group and the new group** whatever the order (`newFirst` after `byWeight`). On the study card the corner glyph has **three states**: a hollow ⚐ on an unchecked card (`.picflag.new`, one tap flags it and so checks it), the tint ⚑ on a flagged one (one tap clears), and **nothing once the card is checked and clean** — the answer block's Flag button stays for re-flagging. The Cards tile shows a quiet **New** chip where the due chip sits (`cardStatus`: a fresh card has no progress row, so the place is free), and a page whose text is unchecked carries the mark at its foot (`.tm.new`). **Two keys in nine columns** ("Not yet checked" — de Noch nicht geprüft, ru Ещё не проверены, th ยังไม่ได้ตรวจ; "tile:New" with its English in the `en` column, since `"New"` already serves the deck bar's legend in the plural — ru Новая against Новые) **and one guide key replaced in ten** (the "Fix the characters" paragraph: "A new card counts as not yet checked until you have written it in Learn or opened it, and the filter shows those alone; flag a card yourself when something looks wrong." — the v259 rule): **475 → 476 a column, ru 504 → 505, en 14 → 15**, no duplicate in any of the ten (source scan and evaluation agree). Checked by screenshot in light and German dark: the hollow ⚐ on 鸡蛋, the tint ⚑ on the flagged card, the New chips, the sheet with its row, the narrowed list. - **The card's picture follows its text — one line 2:1, two 3:2, three or more 4:3 — the deck is cut again, and the picture can be pinched (v514, H: "go for 3 and 4" — phase 3 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, D1 and § 4):** **(1) The window.** `windowRect(r,ratio)` takes the ratio, `frameRatio(n)` gives it from the line count (2, 1.5, 4/3, never taller), `cardLines(d)` counts a card's photo lines (a sign card's `\n`, a word card's `seg` breaks) and `ratioOf(d)` joins the two; every window site of v329 passes the reading's own ratio — `finishPending`, `saveSign`, `provisionalCard`, the Edit form's hand-off and re-crop, v410's `outsideWindow` — while the Save-now placeholder and Image only take the one-line default and are re-cut when the text lands. `FRAME_RATIO` 16:9 stays for the ink-row **proposal** (`shapeBox`, v207), which is a different thing. **(2) The box.** `.picbox` carries the card's ratio inline (`aspect-ratio`) on the study card, the detail and the camera's finished card; a page front carries it as `--ratio`, read by the study card's cover-fitted box of D5; the shared PNG's box follows it too (`cardImage`); the Cards tile keeps 4:3 with the wider picture fitted. That is the deliberate step off v223's "one shape on every card": the shape is tied to the second row of buttons the learner sees anyway. At 390 × 844 the pad grows from 250 to about 272 px under a one-line card. **(3) The re-cut, `RECUT_V` 4:** `recutCard` now tells which rectangle the stored picture is — the old 16:9 window (cut again at the new ratio), already the new window (nothing to do), a split label's own frame (byte-identical, it never had a window), or none (left alone) — and **the guard compares like with like:** the fresh cut of the OLD window against the picture the card has says whether the frame still describes it (v398's `RC_CORR` 0.8), and only then is the new window written; comparing the new shape against the old picture would have refused every card the pass exists for. Measured on the suite's textured photo: three of eight eligible cards written, five skipped by construction, `recutStat` `{v:4,written:3,skipped:5}`. **(4) Pinch and pan** (`attachPicZoom`, § 4): two pointers pinch around their midpoint up to `ZOOM_MAX` 5, one pointer pans once enlarged, the view clamped so no gap opens that was not there at rest; while enlarged the box carries `touch-action:none` and its pointer events stop at the box, so neither the page's scroll nor the carousel takes the pan; a pan's closing click is eaten so it is not the v55 tap, which still swaps crop and whole photo; the next card resets it, since the DOM is rebuilt. On a page front the `pagewrap` moves as one, so the regions stay on their texts — measured, the region's centre at the same fraction before and after. Suites `verify-recut4` (19 checks: `windowRect` at the three ratios and the default; `cardLines` on a word card, a two-line card and a sign; the pass at v4 with `recutStat` written 3; the one-line card's window 480 × 240, the two-line 405 × 270, the sign 480 × 360, in memory and in IndexedDB; a card without a frame, a split label's frame and a card already at 2:1 all byte-identical; Diagnostics' line; the detail's box ratio per card, the study card's box measuring 3:2 under the pad still square and whole, a fresh `windowCut` at 2:1, the PNG's box taller on a three-line card, the tile at 4:3; no page error) and `verify-piczoom` (11 checks: at rest a drag on the picture is the swipe; a synthetic two-pointer pinch enlarging 2.25× with the transform, the class and `touch-action`; a real drag panning within bounds with no swipe and no peer; the clamp at every edge; the pan's click not swapping; the next card at rest; a page front's region at the same place after a pinch; the tap swapping to the whole photo and back; no page error) — **ALL OK on v514**, `verify-writepad` (54) and `verify-lockwalk` (22) ALL OK beside them. Checked by screenshot: the 2:1 box over the pad. A `WHATS_NEW` line (the learner's cards change under him once more), three `TO_TEST` lines. **What it costs, named:** every card with a window is re-cut once more (the third pass since v398 — about 95 ms a card, spread out, no undo); a one-line sign's window loses about 12 % of its height against 16:9; a card without a frame or a photo keeps its 16:9 picture and shows it fitted in a 2:1 box with fill at the sides, for good. Not yet field-checked — H's Diagnostics after one start is the check ("v4 done … cards cut again"), and a one-line card beside a two-line one in Learn: 2:1 over 3:2.
- **Press and hold a character to walk through every card that has it (v513, H: "Go for phase 2" — § 7 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`):** the v354 long press (`longPress`, `LP_MS` 500, `LP_MOVE` 10, its own buzz) on a character button **locks** it — `S.lockChar` — and Learn's list becomes **the walk**: every card of the current Learn filter that carries the character, **due or not** (v429's argument: a locked character is a hand-picked list like the star), in the session's order first — every occurrence, so a card's repeat pass (§ 8.1) rides in the walk too — and the rest of the deck after it (`walkOf`), starting at the card the press was on (`S.walk`, `S.walkIdx`). **One list, one place:** `curList()`/`curIdx()`/`setCurIdx()` stand in for `S.queue`/`S.idx` in the study screen, the chevrons, the swipe, `isRepeat`, `padState`'s key and the pad's `cardDone`, so writing works on every card of the walk exactly as in the session (the review, Done, the points, the repeat entry — inserted into the walk while it stands) and **a walk never runs out:** its last card stays. The Due capsule showed the walk's count until v516 took the capsule off the bar; the chevrons say it since. - **Learn is a write pad: the card is written stroke by stroke, and nothing is graded by a button (v512, H's "Go" on phase 1 of `SPEC-flashcard-layout.md`, draft 4 — the whole design is in that file and every decision in its § 13):** the study card is five zones top to bottom — the photo with the **review flag in its corner** (`.picflag`, one tap toggles), the **character buttons grouped by word** (`padTargets`: one button per character in the text's order with its repeats, the buttons of one dictionary word on one tile `.chw`, one row per photo line; a number with its unit is one button and not writable; a traditional card shows its traditional glyphs, which are also the templates), the **folded answer block** ("Pinyin and meaning ⌄" — `backHTML` without the parts row, the flag note, the AI box, and the ☆ Star / ⚑ Flag row; folded on every card, opened by a tap or by the finished write, `S.ansOpen`), the **square pad** (`mountPad`: a 720 px canvas sized by `fit` to what is left above the tab bar, never under `PAD_MIN` 200, then the card scrolls; a stroke that fits **snaps** into ink and the next lights, one that does not **shakes** and the expected path animates once. **The test is the forward distance alone** (`traceDist`, eight points each, never `strokeDist`'s forgiven reverse) under `TRACE_OK` 0.18 of the pad side — **tightened for a short stroke** (`bar=min(0.18, 0.07+len/2)`, or a dot could land anywhere within 18 % of the pad) **and refused when the stroke fits the template better backwards than forwards**, which is how the suite's own backwards case caught the first cut: a short stroke drawn backwards was inside the bar either way. The order is strict (Q9). Two misses offer **Show me**, four offer **Skip**, which draws the stroke and marks the character *helped*. **Three levels** (§ 8.1): trace, faint template with no lit stroke (a miss lights it), recall on an empty pad (a miss shows the faint template) — the level from `charWrites[ch]` (0–1 / 2–4 / 5+), a repeat pass one level up, a helped character the same level again. **The grade is the writing:** the last stroke of the last character opens the block, writes `recordGrade(c,"good")` — or `"again"` when a Skip helped (Q10: due today, `fails` +1, so the v82 leech flag still fires from Learn) —, counts Done once, adds the points (one per clean character, the count again for a clean card with at most one miss per stroke; `daily[day]={r,w}` with `dayOf` reading the old plain number, `usage.written`, the daily row's `written`, a fifth Progress tile **Written today**), bumps `charWrites` (+1, −2 for a helped character, floor 0, `WRITES_MAX` 3000, in `RESET_KEYS`), **queues the card once more `REP_GAP` 3 cards on** — the same id later in the queue, `isRepeat()` — with an "Again" pill, no second grade and no second Done, and slides to the next card after `NEXT_MS` 900. The guide's Learn section is rewritten in ten columns (the v259 rule). Now every token is looked up in **`PY_SYLLABLES`**, the 419 syllables of Mandarin without their tones (the standard table plus the interjections m, n, ng, hm, hng and biáng), through `pySyllableCounts(tok)`: tone marks are stripped (NFD, the combining marks off, the diaeresis kept so ü survives), tone numbers and apostrophes go, `v` and `u:` read as ü, and the token is split into syllables every way it can be — "xiao" one, "xian" one or two (xi an), "gōngyìngshāng" three, "xio" none as one and two as xi + o, a lone "l" none. A line is kept when its tokens' counts can add up to the line's character count (a number with its unit stands aside, v323); else the app's own pinyin replaces the line as before. So "xio" for 小 is two syllables against one character and is replaced by xiǎo, "xio chéng xù" for 小程序 the same, "xiěn" for 显 and a vowel soup are replaced — and the v187 case (b for 吧), the joined word, the ambiguous join xī'ān, the number with its unit, two lines, capitals and tone numbers are all kept exactly as they were. **One thing this also mends without being asked for it:** v506's vowel regex had no `v`, so a model writing ü as `lv` or `lu:4` had its whole line thrown away for a "vowelless" token — both are kept now, and the suite labels that check as a flip too. **The ambiguity is settled by the count and nothing else:** a wrong token that happens to split into real syllables — "xiom" as xi o m — is caught only when the counts disagree, which they do whenever one character got a broken syllable; a joined answer whose split fits by chance is the price of allowing joins at all. The three callers (`aiAsk`, the picture answer's `p` and every label's `p`) are untouched. So each reading is its own row **`read:<shot>`** (`readRow`: the record trimmed to `NUMS_MAX`, its steps, its passes, `at` and a `seq` that breaks a same-millisecond tie — the first cut sorted by `at` alone and a batch logged in one millisecond came back in the rows' alphabetical key order) with its own 0.8 s debounce (`saveReadLog(N)` takes the record; a record the ring has pushed out or a reset has taken writes nothing), and each exchange its own row **`ailog:<t>:<n>`**, written at once. `ringAdd` deletes the row it pushes out; `numsReset` keeps a re-read photo on its one row (v405's in-place replacement, the key being the shot). **The rows never enter `S.settings`** (`putRow`/`delRow` write past `setSetting`, and boot lifts them out of the settings map into the ring and `AILOG`), or a hundred records would sit in memory twice — the v214 shape one store along. **A phone still holding the v504 single rows is migrated once at boot**: `readlog` and `ailog` are read as before, written out as rows and deleted, so the three readings and three exchanges already on the phone survive the update. **Start over** deletes every `read:`/`ailog:` row through the ring and `AILOG` and then sweeps the store for any prefixed row the ring no longer names. Press the button twice and it reads **Open the flashcard** instead of making a second one (`madeFrom` derives that from the deck rather than storing it on the item, so deleting the flashcard offers Generate again by itself). **WHAT WENT WITH v478, and it went whole:** `derived`, the two unfitted thresholds (`DERIVE_PAGES` 2, `DERIVE_LOOKS` 3), the `lookups` counter in settings with its `LOOK_MAX` cap and its `RESET_KEYS` entry, `promote`/`promoteCheck`/`afterPromote`, `sourcesOf`, `pagesOf`, `carouselHTML`, `isDerived`, `srcLabel`, `ICON_MULTI` and its tile chip, and `groupPages` — there are no page items in a queue to group. **Nothing automatic is left: you press the button or nothing happens.** **THE ONE MIGRATION, and it is why nothing of H's is lost:** the cards v478 promoted carry `derived` and still sit inside their page, so without it they would simply vanish from the deck the day this ships. `migrateDerived` runs once at boot, 2.2 s in (where the T1 pass used to), turns each into the flashcard the button would have made and **copies its progress row onto the new id**, then clears `derived` and leaves the text in its multicard. **A generated flashcard survives its multicard's deletion** — it is a separate card, its `from` dangles and the copied title stays; The reading proper then ended **weak** (`eff` 149.8, the best pass read 玛墨家), so the picture path ran, and **Qwen answered the same three characters** — `zh:"玛黑家"`, box `[348,256,570,361]` of the 800×450 picture, i.e. `0.435–0.7125` across, **`0.5689–0.8022` down**, where the characters actually stand at about 0.36–0.63 across and **0.297–0.438** down: the box is **0.27 of the picture too low**, the vertical drift this file has recorded on 邪不压正 and on the street sign. **`snapBox` could not save it and the record says why:** the characters sit at 267–394 of the copy and the box at 512–722 — **zero overlap** —, so its "at least half of the blob inside the AI's box" test (v297) dropped every one of them and it returned **null** (`"snap":null` in his dump; `SNAP_ROOM`'s one text height, `Hb` 210, cannot close a 118 px gap under that test). With no snap the raw box was used, `{"by":"AI","rect":[633,449,1203,785],"took":true}` overrode the reader's measurement, and `cardFrame` came out `{x:0.3956,y:0.5621,w:0.3563,h:0.28}` — **56 % down the photo**, which is his screenshot exactly. **The fix, and it is a narrowing of v319 rather than a new rule:** `placedText` records the text a reader placement came from, and `placeFromPicture` skips `frameOnText` when the AI's `zh` **is that same text** — CJK characters only (`cjkOnly`), so punctuation, spaces and line breaks cannot decide it. **THE BOUNDARY, stated rather than assumed, because v319 exists for a reason:** v319's own case is 绿皮书, where the quick look read **绿友书一** and the AI answered 绿皮书 — a *different* text —, so the AI's box still wins there and everywhere else the reader was wrong about **what** it read. Where the two agree, the reader has per-character boxes measured on the real pixels at 98 % and the model has only confirmed the characters; the pixels win. **Deliberately exact equality, not a similarity score:** the harness's own reader reads a synthetic 面包店 as 面包**后**, one character out, and there the guard correctly stands down — the AI may be right about that character and is then the only evidence about it. A "same length, mostly the same characters" rule was considered and **not built**: it would need field evidence this file does not have (the v386 rule), and on H's own sign exact equality is what fired. **Two further guards:** only a placement from **one definite reading** counts — the quick look and the winning pass, both `rectOfLines` — while the close look's `textBandOf` is a quartile band over several *disagreeing* passes and has no single text, so it records none; and only while `picSeen.base` stands, so a v314/v318/v348/v393 re-ask, which deliberately threw the reader's frame away to ask again about the whole photo, is untouched. `N.agreed` carries the text (the v399 rule) and the log says *"the reader placed the frame on 坚果供应 and the AI read the same text back — the reader measured the characters, the AI only confirmed them: the frame stays"*. Suite `verify-aibox` (a sign in the top third of a photo over plain glass, the proposal the whole photo, `effScore` forced weak, **`textLike` left real so the quick look must read the sign itself**, and Qwen answering with a box in the glass: the reader's own reading asserted, the frame placed by the reader, no AI placement, `N.agreed`, the log line, **the card's picture on the sign** (`cardFrame.y+h` 0.306 against 0.945 on v485), one picture call; and a **control** where the AI answers a *different* text, where the box still places the frame on both trees) — **ALL OK on v486, 4 of its 16 checks fail on v485** with the card's picture at `y` 0.4956 there, the field defect reproduced. Proven as a predicate rather than argued: the old test matches **0 of 2** of the new rows, the new one 2 of 2. `report.sql` sums over `u.install = <id> OR u.install LIKE <id> || ':%'` — the bare id still matched, for the rows written before that day — and returns `relay_qwen` and `relay_deepseek` beside the total, which is what the warning needs. **H must run it once in the SQL Editor**; until he does, `relay_today` reads 0 and the near-cap section is simply empty, which is the safe way for it to fail. **Then the warning itself, and what "notify" can honestly mean here: there is no push channel and there will not be one.** The app has no service-worker push handler, no VAPID keys and no subscription store, and web push on Android in China goes through FCM, which is blocked — so a real notification would be a large build that then does not arrive. **The unlock is the moment H is actually looking at the owner's rows**, so `relayWatch()` fetches the report once there and puts a line above the tab bar: "One phone is near today's relay cap: qwen 72 of 80.", or "2 phones are near today's relay cap — see All users." It is accepted because the copy cannot refuse a call or change what a phone may do; the worst drift is a warning at the wrong number in a report only H reads, and both places carry a comment naming the other. Rendered in the real bar at H's own 390 px, the card gives the row **358 px**, and with both labels spelled out the content wants **448 px in English, 538 in Russian, 554 in German and 615 in Spanish** — so v480's `flex-wrap` was not a stylistic choice, it was the only thing keeping the bar inside the card. **Seven layouts were measured over all ten languages before one was picked**, and six of them fail: the count sentence with two pills (max 615), with two pills at 14 px and tighter padding (590), with a pill and a text link (587), with *Accept*/*Dismiss* instead of *Accept all*/*Dismiss all* (510), with one pill and one icon button (495), and the count reduced to the bare number with two pills (381, still over in de, es and id). **The only layout that fits every language at both widths is a shortened count phrase with two 44 px icon buttons — measured 310 px at its widest**, and that is what ships: `4 AI suggestions` at the left, a filled green **tick** and a neutral **cross** at the right, both 44 px circles, the words carried on `title`/`aria-label` from the same `"Accept all"`/`"Dismiss all"` keys v480 added. The glyphs are `MARK_TICK`/`MARK_CROSS`, the pair v461 already uses for known and not-yet-known — the app's own visual language for yes and no, not a new one. **The count phrase is a key swap, not an addition:** `"AI suggestion waiting"`/`"AI suggestions waiting"` are gone from all nine columns and `"bar:AI suggestion"`/`"bar:AI suggestions"` replace them, prefixed because a bare `"AI suggestion"` is already the suggestion box's own label (the v371 collision, avoided by construction); English lives in the `en` column as the `capsule:Done` pattern does, Russian keeps its three forms. **465 keys a column and ru 494, byte-identical to v480**; en 12 → 14. **Measured over 10 languages × 390 and 360 px: 20 of 20 one line, the bar 60 px tall everywhere, both aria-labels present, nothing overflowing.** **Two defects the measurement caught that reading would not have.** The two buttons sat **12 px apart vertically** — a flex row aligns its items by their own baselines when they carry inline content, and the tick's path sits lower in its viewBox than the cross's; `align-items:center` on the group settles it. And the accept button was first given the class `ok`, which the page has carried as a **bare `.ok` rule since v82** (`font-size:14px; color:var(--ok); margin-top:12px`) — so it inherited a 12 px top margin from a rule written for a completely different thing; it is `.prim` now, and the comment says why. That is the v421 lesson (a class written for one shape borrowed by another) in its collision form. **What it costs, named and not dressed up:** two bare glyphs carry a thirty-card bulk action, so a mis-tap on the tick accepts everything — which is why both actions write the v369 undo store and More → Check-up offers **Undo last run**. `verify-dismissall` reads the labels from `aria-label` since and asserts the bar is one line (all centres within 2 px and no overflow), so a longer label or a second row fails rather than quietly wrapping — **ALL OK on v481**. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — the v412 precedent exactly: a layout polish of a control shipped one version earlier. the whole batch is **one IndexedDB transaction** (`idbPutMany`, where Accept all still writes card by card through `applyCardUpdate`, since each of those is a text change with its own line-recutting); and it writes the **v369 undo store** exactly as Accept all does (`saveLastRun("dismiss","*",before,n)`), so More → Check-up carries **Undo last run** and one tap puts all thirty suggestions back — memory and IndexedDB, asserted both ways. **Dismissing is not accepting, and that is the check that matters:** the cards' text, pinyin and meaning are byte-identical afterwards and `mt.verified` does not move — the only thing that changes besides `ai` is a `mt.suspect` reason, which goes because a human has now seen it (the v82 single-Dismiss rule, unchanged). **The button is the sheet's own neutral Cancel look** (`.btn.plain` scoped to `.aibar`), not the tint: `.btn` is tint-soft on tint, so beside a filled red *Accept all* a tinted *Dismiss all* reads as a second red button and invites the wrong tap — the v475 lesson (a control that looks like the control beside it) in its button form. **And the bar had to be allowed to wrap, which the measurement forced rather than taste:** three items on one flex row overflowed at **390 px in German and Russian** and at 360 px in German, Spanish and Indonesian; `.aibar` is `flex-wrap:wrap` with the two buttons in their own `.aiacts2` group (`margin-left:auto`, itself wrapping), so the pair moves as a unit and stays right-aligned — measured over **10 languages × 390 and 360 px: 0 overflowing, 0 labels broken inside a button** (the v427 fit rule: ask whether the text broke, not whether the box overflowed), at the cost of the bar being two lines in every language now and three in de/es/id at 360. **Two keys in nine columns** ("Dismiss all" against each column's own word for Dismiss — de Alle verwerfen, ja すべて閉じる against its 閉じる, ru Отклонить все —, and "Dismissed the AI's suggestions on {0} at {1}." mirroring each column's own *Accepted* line, agreement-free by construction since the verb agrees with the suggestions inside the key, not with `{0}` — the v412 rule), **463 → 465 a column, ru 492 → 494, en 12**, no duplicate in any of the ten (source scan and evaluation agree). Suite `verify-dismissall` (19 checks: the bar carrying both actions with its count; one tap clearing every suggestion in memory and in IndexedDB with the bar gone, the cards' own text and `mt.verified` untouched and the suspect reason cleared; the undo store naming the run; More's row with its line, and Undo putting all four back with the bar; Accept all still applying them and writing its own store — the regression guard; no bar at all on a deck with no suggestion, the v308 rule; the German button and the German undo line) — **ALL OK on v480, and on v479 the run dies at the missing button after its first check**, which is the flip stated plainly. The derived and cardstabs suites pass. Checked by screenshot in light, German dark and Russian at 360 px. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **What it costs, named:** once the next run replaces the undo store the suggestions are gone for good — the way back is another Check-up, about six relay calls for thirty cards. Not yet field-checked — H's own thirty waiting suggestions are the check: one tap, and the Undo row where he can find it.
- **The reading log belongs to a photo (v479, H after the Diagnostics dump of 2026-09-13: "Fix the interleaved reading log"):** his dump had **"the AI could not check the photo and the reading is weak — no card" standing at step 12 of 16**, before two further `recognizing` steps — one photo's line sitting in the middle of another photo's reading. `READLOG` was **one global 40-line list**, and `cropSign` **wiped it at its start**, so a reading that began while an earlier one was still finishing — v411's album batch, where the next photo starts as soon as the last has its cards while that one's AI check and `finishPending` are still running — **erased its predecessor's steps and then collected its predecessor's tail among its own**. v406 named it ("the per-photo `numbers:` records carried everything that mattered, so it waits for its own PR") and left it. **The fix is not a second store: the steps move onto the record that is already keyed by the photo.** `NUMSOF[id]` has existed since v399 and the ring of three since v405, so `logRead(id,text)` files the line on `N.log` and the misfiling is impossible by construction — `logRead` cannot be called without naming a photo. **57 call sites take the id and every one of them already had it in scope** (`aiReadPicture` through its own `rec`, the rest through their first parameter); only `findFrame` had none and gained one. **Two things it buys beyond attribution, each a defect in its own right.** (1) **The two earlier readings carry their steps at last** — until now `Earlier readings` printed `numbers:` alone, which is exactly the half a human cannot read; they are trimmed head 5 / tail 10 with "… N steps left out", keeping the frame's proposal and the quick look at one end and the outcome at the other. (2) **The progress line overwrites its own photo's line** — `readingStatus` compared against whatever was logged last by anyone, so two photos read close together overwrote each other's "recognizing … N%"; measured on the v478 tree, photo X ends with **no progress line at all** while photo Y's block carries **five**, X's 10 % and 30 % among them. **Three smaller things the rebuild forced, each with its reason.** `LAST_READ.nums` is gone — a second copy of the ring's last entry that had to be kept in step by hand, where `lastRead()` reads it from the one place. **A record joins the ring once and never rejoins** (`N.ringed`): `NUMSOF` keeps six records and the ring three, so without the flag a late line from a reading already pushed out would put it back at the head as the newest — the misattribution in its last hiding place; its steps are still filed under it, they are simply not printed. And **`numsReset` replaces the photo's ring entry in place** and carries the trailing `pre` lines (the frame's proposal, the old crop found) into the new record — v285's rule without the global wipe — so a photo proposed, located and read takes one ring slot and not three. **The numbers' own budget is untouched, which is why the two are kept apart:** `numsTrim` strips `log`, `passes` and `ringed` before it measures, and the steps ride beside the trimmed ring in the setting (`readlog.logs`, matched back by shot id at boot); steps inside that JSON would push the numbers out, which is the v395 fault (the reply cut mid-word) one store along. The passes are stored and printed for the newest reading only, as before. **Measured:** the shared text grows **5 058 → 6 048 characters** on three panel-sized readings of 18 steps each, and buys the two earlier readings their steps where they had none. **A defect found on the way and fixed:** `picOnBad`'s own `aiReadPicture` call passed no record, so that path's answer-shape lines had no photo to file under **and its prompt fingerprint was never written at all** — the v399 rule, one path further on. Suite `verify-readlog` (19 checks: a photo read end to end with its own steps, the frame's proposal first, passes and numbers under it and not inside the numbers JSON; a second photo read after it with the first still listed and its steps intact; two readings overlapping, driven through the app's own `readingStatus` — the late line in its own photo's block and not in the newer one's, each photo keeping its own progress line; every reading coming back with its steps after a restart; a phone still holding a v478 setting; Start over) — **ALL OK on v479, 9 of its 19 checks fail on v478**, and the seven that pass on both are named in the file as controls (the card is made either way, the numbers JSON never carried the steps on either tree, and "the second photo's block carries no line of the first" is vacuous on v478, which prints no shot id anywhere). Eight suites that read `READLOG` are retargeted at the ring's own logs (`LAST_READ.ring.flatMap(N=>N.log)` in place of the global list), and of those the two that drive a whole photo through the pipeline pass: `verify-quota` ALL OK — 14 checks and `verify-shared` ALL OK; `verify-page` and `verify-derived` (25) pass too. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — Diagnostics sits behind the owner's password and a learner never sees it (the v408 rule). One `TO_TEST` line. Not yet field-checked — H's next dump after two photos in a row is the check: two blocks, each with its own steps, and no line under the wrong photo.

Vanilla JS, no frameworks, no build step. `app.js` in reading order: helpers and state → IndexedDB → online AI → study screen → cards, detail, edit form → More → camera and inbox → reading pipeline (`readPass`, `readPassTra`/`traWorker`/`t2s`, `secondLook`, `readingScore`, `deskewBlob`, `textRowExtent`, `toBW`/`chromaCanvas`/`toChroma`/`inkHeight`) → character picker and drawing sheet → sign editor and save → service worker, mirror, shell check and the shared screenshots (`takeShared`). The usage counters and the owner's gate sit with More. Small shared helpers: `askSheet` (a question as the app's own sheet, v222), `putCard`, `pySpaced`, `eachLine`, `slineHTML`/`wireSlines`, `urlOf`, `fullPhoto`, `pageVersion`, `median`, `readingStatus`, `logErr`/`diagText`/`shareDiag`, `busyHTML`, `apiErrText` (the error text from a provider's or the relay's JSON body).
- **A multicard is a reference, and what Learn studies is a text that has EARNED a card (v478, H across five messages, all of `SPEC-derived-cards.md`'s core built: "please analyze whether certain buttons or certain fields appear again and again in multicards and then make flashcards for learning out of them" · "either a text appears again and again on a multicard or I tap a certain text again and again on a multicard. both cases become a flashcard" · "When I select a word on a multicard, I think I should also instantly get the option to make it a flashcard" · "I think multi cards don't really need the got it or learn again buttons" · "flash cards generated from multi cards should be somehow marked as such.", and his "Go as per your recommendation" on D1–D4):** **ONE FIELD, and nothing is deleted or merged.** A page's texts are still the split's own cards with their progress row, star, flag, tags and AI check exactly as v453 made them; what changes is that Learn studies only the ones carrying **`derived:true`**, and the lookup sheet grades nothing. The sources are **not stored**: `sourcesOf(d)` derives them from the deck, so a page photographed tomorrow joins a card's carousel by itself and there is no second copy of the truth to drift (the v401 lesson) — that is the one place this departs from the spec's `d.from`. **Three ways to earn it.** **R9, the manual one, and it is the reason the other two are allowed to be guesses:** the sheet's three grade tiles are replaced by **Make this a flashcard**, one tap, and by **Already a flashcard** once it is one; a wrong threshold then costs patience and never a card H wanted and could not have. **T1, recurrence:** the same text on `DERIVE_PAGES` 2 multicards or more — checked once at boot, so a deck that already holds its multicards earns its first cards with no tap. **T2, repetition:** `DERIVE_LOOKS` 3 look-ups of one text on one multicard, and **the third look-up IS the promotion** — the sheet shows the state at once and the write lands behind it. **Where the counter may live was decided by the spec's own measurements, not by convenience:** not keyed by card id (`cardId` recycles a freed text as the next card's id, v118, so a count would transfer between unrelated cards), not in the progress row (`importData` drops every row without a numeric `due`, which is exactly an un-promoted item's shape) and not as a field on the item (`putCard` rewrites the whole record including its crop Blob on every tap) — so it is `settings.lookups`, keyed **page + text**, which forces two things it now does: it is in **`RESET_KEYS`** (it holds the photos' own characters — the v458 leak) and its debounced writer is in `resetAll`'s `clearTimeout` line, and it is capped at `LOOK_MAX` 2000 keys, least-looked-at first. **Q5, T2's dirty signal, answered by cleaning rather than by absorbing:** a tap on the same region while its own sheet already stands no longer counts a second time; a tap that misses a small region and lands on the nearest one (v448's 44 px rule) still does, because it is a look-up either way. **THE COST, and H approved it (D3): a text that has not qualified leaves Learn AT ONCE** — his ~20 washing-machine texts drop out of the due deck the day this ships and come back one at a time. Nothing is lost: the progress rows stay, so a promoted text returns with its whole history, and **a card made on purpose joins TODAY's session** (appended at the end, which is what an `again` grade already does, v428 — without it the reward for tapping the button would be a card that appears after the next reload; the suite caught that). **The carousel (R6, R7):** a derived card whose text stands on several multicards shows them **all**, side by side, snapping, most looked-at first (D2: "order of use" is look-ups of THIS text on that multicard, the number T2 already counts, so the sort is free) — and each slide carries its own `me`, the sibling text on that photo, so the frame is drawn around this card's text wherever it stands. One source is exactly v452's page front and renders through the same `pageHTML`, so there is one way of drawing a page. **The mark (R8, D4), in both places:** a quiet pill beside Traditional on the card ("From a multicard" / "From 2 multicards") and a small two-plate chip on the Cards tile beside the flag and the AI mark. **Two keys rather than a count word, deliberately:** «Из {0} мультикарточек» wants the genitive plural after a numeral and a fixed phrase at one, which no plural table of this app gets right by itself — the v412 rule that no agreement may cross a key boundary. **v461's cross and check are NOT taken away; where they show is narrowed:** only a text that has earned a card carries one, because an unpromoted text has no learning state and a red cross meaning "you cannot do this yet" would be false about a text nobody is being asked to learn. H fought four rounds over those marks and the spec's reading was that he now wants them gone; narrowing is the smaller move and **whether they should go entirely is his call, named here rather than taken.** **And the grades stay on a marked photo that is NOT a multicard** — v448's own screen, which every photo from before v453 still is and whose texts are ordinary flashcards already; H's "multi cards don't really need the got it or learn again buttons" is about multicards, so that is the only place the grades went. `verify-photomode`'s "three grades" assertion is what guards it. **Five keys in nine columns** (the action, the state, the two pill forms and the guide's sentence), **458 → 463 a column, ru 487 → 492, en 12**, no duplicate in any of the ten, the static key check reporting the same five standing hits; the guide's Cards section gains its own paragraph in all ten (the v259 rule), and `privacy.html`'s usage list names the new counter (`regionCards` beside `regionTaps` and `regionGrades`). Suite `verify-derived` (25 checks: the clean break — the plain card alone in the queue, the Deck capsule counting the page once; the sheet with no grade tiles and the one action; the tap writing `derived` to memory AND IndexedDB, the sheet swapping in place, Learn studying it, the Cards tile with its chip, the card with its pill, and only that text marked in the page's list; two look-ups promoting nothing and the third promoting by itself; the same region tapped three times while its sheet stands counting once; T1 at boot with the queue holding exactly the plain card and the promoted one; two slides each framing this card's text on its own photo, and one source giving the single page; the counter filled and then wiped by Start over; the German action and the German guide) — **ALL OK on v478, 19 of its 25 checks fail on v477**; the six that pass on both are labelled controls in the file. **Three suites were retargeted rather than left red, each naming the contract that moved:** `verify-page` (its session check now asserts that NO text is studied until one earns a card, its sheet check asserts no grades and the action, and its Learn block promotes a second text because the first was just scheduled 30 days out), `verify-cardtiles` (the page's list starts bare and a mark appears once a text is promoted) and `verify-photomode`, which needed **no** change and is therefore the guard on the narrowing. The cardstabs, pagefront, pageswipe, starfit and aiswitch suites pass untouched. Checked by screenshot in light and German dark: the sheet, the carousel, the back. A `WHATS_NEW` line, two `TO_TEST` lines. **Measured and named, not chased:** the overflow scan over ten languages × 390 and 360 px reports `.picbox.page` and `.cs` **identically on a v477 root** — the first is the blurred fill's deliberate `width:120%` (the v465 measurement bug, named again so it is not chased a third time) and the second the star's 44 px target in a 33 px column at 360 px, both older than this change. **Not built, and named:** the spec's promote-and-merge, which deletes the sibling items — the derived card is simply one of them and the others stay as their page's dots, which is less destructive and reaches the same place; and Q4, a derived card whose only source photo was deleted, where `fullPhoto` falls back to the item's own copy and the carousel drops a slide it cannot draw. - **The thirteenth audit, and the field finding that made it necessary (v472, H, 2026-09-13, with a full Diagnostics dump: "Also, hier hat weder Multicard funktioniert noch, dass die prozessierten Fotos von der Kameraseite verschwinden, wenn sie fertig sind.", then "Du machst jetzt bitte mal ein Komplett Audit, suchst nach Widersprüchen und löst sie auf und polisht komplett drüber."):** **THE OPERATIONAL FINDING FIRST, because no code change touches it: `[picture] relay error 403: Free quota exhausted. To continue accessing the model on a paid basis, please add funds or disable the "use free tier only" mode in the management console.`** Qwen's free tier on the **relay's** key is spent, so **every phone without a Qwen key of its own — H's included, which is what his own record shows — has no picture reading at all**, and that is the whole of "Multicard funktioniert nicht": no picture answer means no `apart`, no `labels`, no split, one card. It is H's Bailian account to settle, and this file's v451 entry, which said his phone reads pictures on its own key, is corrected. **What the code got wrong about it is the audit's first contradiction, and it is the v384/v395/v399/v405 fault one path further on: the app said the opposite of what happened.** `picOnBad` consumed the parked early answer as `(await early.p).pic` and logged **"the picture answer asked at the quick look 21.7 s ago is used"** whatever came back — so H's diagnostics claimed a paid-for answer was used when it had 403'd; `N.picErr` stayed **null**, the error log carried nothing from that path, and `N.early.ok` stayed `null` as if the call were still pending. `picPanel` swallowed a rejected parked promise the same way. Both go through **`noPicture()`** now — one place that writes the failure into the reading's record, into the numbers, into the error log (so the daily row and All users carry it) and into the reading log. **Then the card that should never have been built.** His shot read 自回回回还 | 还一一一 at **effScore 183**, three points over `WEAK_READ`, so v438's gate — which asks for `sg.weak` — did not fire, and the app built the card, `verified`, with the whole screenshot as its picture. Three independent signals had already said the text was worthless: **v441's own per-line test held the provisional back** (94 and 93, under `PLACE_CF`), **DeepSeek answered `bad:true` twice** ("OCR garbage: no plausible sign, menu or product text can be made of these repeated 回/还/一 characters"), and **the picture call that could have settled it was refused**. The gate is `noPic && (sg.weak || (sg.ai.bad && !sg.sureLines))` since: the reader unsure of its own lines, the text model rejecting them, and no picture answer at all. **A reading whose every line IS read surely keeps its card even against a bad verdict** — the v143 rule, and v348's finding that a text-only garbage verdict is weaker evidence than the picture's; that case is the suite's control and still makes its card. **And the row no longer claims the AI "could not be reached" when the AI answered and refused:** one key replaced in nine columns, "The AI could not check this photo, and the reading alone was not good enough for a card." — true of a dead network and of a 403 alike (457 keys a column, ru 486, en 12, no duplicate). **The breaker, and the regression it caused before it worked.** A 4xx that is not 429 is a **refusal** — no funds, a dead key, a forbidden call — and the next photo gets the same answer, so `picRefused` stands the picture path down for `PIC_DOWN` 10 minutes and any answer clears it (`picOk`); a 5xx, a timeout and a dead connection are transient and change nothing; a 429 is deliberately excluded, since a provider's rate limit clears in seconds and the relay's own daily cap has its own sentence. The shape is v189's `ORIGIN_DOWN` one layer up, and it saves H's phone 88–134 KB and twenty-odd seconds **per photo** while the quota is out. **The first cut put `pictureUp()` in `picOnBad`'s own guard and the suite caught it at once: the parked 403 then left no `picErr` at all, the no-card gate went quiet, and the garbage card came straight back.** The breaker belongs at the dial, not at the earpiece — it stops a **new** call and never the consumption of one already paid for; the weak path sets `picErr` from the stand-down for the same reason. Suite `verify-quota` (H's own shape, forced: `effScore` 183, `sureLines` false, `textLike` false, Qwen answering 403 with Bailian's own body, DeepSeek answering `bad` — the record carrying the provider's words, `N.early.ok` false, the log NOT claiming the answer was used and saying what happened instead, no card, the gate naming the text check, the photo kept with Crop, the row's new sentence, the error log, a vouching text check still making its card, the German sentence, and **one picture call for three photos**) — **ALL OK on v472, 10 of its 14 checks fail on v471**, where the card comes out as 癌本1本工地，站上 | 示兴牛示人诈吴 | … flagged, with the whole photo. **The audit's own sweeps, and what they found.** **Layout: zero overflowing elements at 390 and 360 px over seven screens × ten languages**, where v432 had left three standing findings. Two were real and both are fixed: **the card detail's six buttons overflowed the card** — `.detailacts` is `1fr 1fr`, which is `minmax(auto,1fr)`, and `.btn{white-space:nowrap}` made each track's min-content its own label, so the grid could not shrink (measured +21 px in Indonesian, +6 German, +1 Spanish at 360); it is `minmax(0,1fr)` with a label that may wrap, which is the v427 fault in its grid form — a class written for one shape borrowed by another. And **the owner's Mirror row** ran 6 px past a 360 px screen because the mirror address is one unbreakable token driving its container's min-content: `min-width:0` on the row's own column and `overflow-wrap:anywhere` on the address. A photo that never made a card is gone."), both in ten columns. **What came back clean:** no unreferenced function or constant (the one hit is `altCharsAt`, used through a spread), no `var`, no `console.warn`/`error` without a `logErr`, no local named `t` in a scope that calls `t()`, no duplicate key in any of the ten columns (source scan and evaluation agree), the static key check reporting only its five standing hits, the SW shell list complete, every path relative, every external host one of the documented seven, and `supabase/`, `vendor/ARPHICPL.TXT` and both workflows present with `CAP_ALL` at the 10000 v409 recorded. **Suites:** quota, camtab, camonly, tiles, shutter, todo, taptoframe, multicard and checkfail pass. **Seven suites carried v470 fixture debt that had gone unseen** — `waitForSelector('#shots')` waits for a *visible* element and v470 hides `#shots` on an empty inbox, so checkfail, multicard, finekeep, page, shared, snapkeep and waiting had been dying at their first tab click on v470 and v471 alike (measured on a v471 root); they wait for `#snap`. - **The words on a photo are framed, and the photo gives nothing away (v461, H on the v448 dots: "Die Punkte in den Multicards gefallen mir überhaupt nicht. Kannst Du nicht was Moderneres machen? zum Beispiel einen richtig modernen, schönen Rahmen, um die Worte, die Du erkannt hast? … Wir brauchen nur zwei Stati. Rot mitm Kreuz drauf zum Beispiel Heißt, kann ich noch nicht. grün mitm Haken drauf Heißt, okay, kann ich abgehakt.", then "Die frames in multicard should be neutral, not have any color.", then "Keine x- beziehungsweise Haken-markierung am Frame bitte.", then the decisive one — "The two states are only living in the cards. That is the entry's real content: the first three rounds were mine to lose. Round 1 offered four frame treatments with a coloured cross/check on the frame's corner; H: neutral. Round 2 made the frames neutral and left the mark — and cost the app the one thing the frame's colour had been carrying, the state of a **16 × 9 px** washing-machine button label where no glyph fits, which round 2 solved by carrying it in the frame's *weight*; H: no mark on the frame at all. Round 3 offered three ways to keep a stateless hint on the picture (identical frames / weight / a veil over the done ones); H's answer was not a preference between them but **an argument**: a flashcard front does not tell you whether you know the word, so neither may the photo. **That is a didactic constraint, not an aesthetic one, and it kills the whole family of "show progress on the picture" ideas — including the two I had recommended in rounds 2 and 3.** What ships is round 4's option A. **On the photo:** every card's frame is drawn permanently as one **neutral outline** — a white core with a dark flank on each side (`inset 0 0 0 1.7px rgba(255,255,255,.95), inset 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,0,0,.38), 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,.45)`, radius 6), so the boundary is carried by the **edge between the runs** and survives a white sign, a black appliance panel and a red shop front without a colour of its own — the failure mode of any single-colour stroke is that some photo matches it. **Every frame is identical**: the state class left the region entirely, so the picture cannot leak the answer even through the DOM. Gone with the dots: the `.dot` element, `REGION_FLASH`, `REGIONS_SHOWN` and the two-second outline flash of v448 (the frame is permanent now, so there is nothing to flash), and the 18 px pulsing dot of v452. **`.ff` is the frame and is its own size container** (`container-type:size` on `.region`, the query on its child — an element cannot be styled by its own container query), so a word only a few pixels tall thins its stroke to 1.3 px and its radius to 3.5 instead of drowning in it; measured on the suite's fixture, a 10 × 5 px label gets the thin frame and an 88 × 23 px one the full frame. **On Learn, a spotlight, and it is still:** one extra shadow on the studied word's own frame (`0 0 0 9999px rgba(0,0,0,.34)`), clipped by `.picbox.page .regions{overflow:hidden}` — the whole photo steps back and the word you are on is the only thing at full brightness. No second element, no clip-path, nothing to keep in sync, and **no animation at all** on a screen whose job is to be read. It says *which* word, never whether you know it. **The two states, where a card is listed or opened:** `stateMark(id)` draws a red disc with a cross for one still to learn and a green disc with a check for one ticked off, as inline SVG (the app ships no icon font and no emoji in the UI), and it replaces the bare `.pdot` in the page detail's list of its own texts. Colour is never the only channel — the glyph is, which is what H asked for. **The Multicard in the Cards list (H, the same hour: "Die Multicards müssen in den Listen auch irgendwie anders angezeigt werden. Man muss sofort sehen, dass das eine Multicard ist und keine normale Flashcard."):** the thumbnail becomes a **stack of three plates** with the number of texts on it — the language iOS Photos uses for an album — and a **bar** under the title says how far through it you are. The three plates are 114 × 60 offset by 5 px twice, so they occupy **exactly** the 124 × 70 the row's first column already reserves: measured, the thumbnail box is still 124 × 70, nothing widens, nothing overflows sideways. The row is 153 px against a plain row's 91 — it was **141 px before this version** (title, count, tags and a preview of its texts), so the bar costs 12 px and the stack nothing. **The tap sheet is untouched:** the two-button *Not yet / Got it* sheet was offered as S2 and H did not pick it, and replacing the three grades changes what the scheduler is told — that is a flow change and waits for his word. **What the four rounds also produced and is NOT built** (do not bring them back unasked): a coloured frame; a cross/check badge on the frame's corner, in any shape (a disc, a notch cut into the border, a seal in an open fourth corner); a corner-bracket frame (offered as B and refused by the "A"); and every way of hinting progress on the picture — the weight difference, the desaturating veil, and the mini-frames on the list thumbnail. A `WHATS_NEW` line, three `TO_TEST` lines. Checked by screenshot in light and dark: the Cards list, the page detail and the Learn front. Multicards lassen sich nicht swipen."):** two faults, and the second is the one that made it look completely dead. **(1) The page detail never wired the gesture.** v445 gave the Cards detail its carousel in `renderCardDetail`, and v453's page card renders through `renderPageDetail` instead — a different function that never called `wireSwipe`. v453's own entry recorded it as "a page reached through the Cards list has no swipe"; H found it. The page's body is `pageBodyHTML(d)` now, factored out so the swipe's peer can draw a page neighbour with it exactly as `detailCardHTML` draws an ordinary one, and both detail screens share one options object (`detailSwipe(list,li,main)`) whose `peer` dispatches on `isPage` — the v445 lesson that two copies drift. `makePeer` takes `{html,cls}` so a page arriving from the side gets its own class. The page's body sits in a `.card.bare`, which is what `wireSwipe` looks for and which takes the card's box back off (`background:none;padding:0;box-shadow:none;border-radius:0;text-align:start;max-width:none`) — **measured: the page detail is pixel-identical to v459 in light and dark, 0 of 1 341 600 pixels different.** A first cut without `text-align:start` centred the title and the count line, 13 000 pixels' worth, which is the kind of unasked look change H approved nothing about. **(2) And the whole card refused the stroke anyway, which is the real bug.** `wireSwipe`'s pointerdown has ignored `button,a,input,textarea,.chip` since v414, so a press that begins on a real control is never hijacked — but **the v448 dots are `<button class="region">` and the v453 text rows are `<button class="crow">`**, and on a page detail those two cover essentially the whole card. Measured on the fixture: a stroke starting 40 px or 120 px down (the photo) produced **no peer at all**, one starting on the title at 260 px swiped perfectly. So the only card kind that holds several texts was the one kind whose entire surface was dead.
