- **"Start over — Delete everything" now deletes everything (v458, H after the contradiction audit: "Go with 1, 2, 4 und 5"):** `resetAll` cleared the three IndexedDB stores and never touched `settings`, and the audit **measured what that left behind on a seeded phone: seven settings still holding Chinese read off the user's photos** — `ailog`, `errlog`, `lastRun`, `readlog`, `recheckRun`, `tagStage`, `translateStage` — **and a Progress dashboard still showing a four-day streak and two busy days over an empty deck.** The sheet has promised "All progress, cards and inbox photos" since v82 and delivered two of the three. `RESET_KEYS` names fourteen keys now, in three groups: **the app's own logs**, which carry the photos' own characters (`ailog` — the last three AI exchanges, the request up to `AI_LOG_REQ` and the raw reply up to `AI_LOG_RES`; `readlog` — the steps and the `numsRing`, which keeps the model's `zh` per reading; `errlog` — **unredacted**, since `noHan` runs only on the way to the daily row); **everything keyed by a card id**, which since v118 **is** the card's text while it is free (`lastRun`, `translateStage`, `tagStage`, `recheckRun`, `translateRun`, `tagRun`, `resumeView`, `autoQueue`); and **the two progress settings More → Progress actually reads** — `days` the streak and `daily` the 30-day strip — plus `lastExport`, which after a wipe should say "never". **What survives, each for its own reason, and an independent design review earned three of these:** the API keys and the provider choice (v172 exists because a key was lost once); **`aiAuto`, `aiPicture` and `aiRelay`, because all three are `!==false` defaults — deleting them would silently switch the AI review and the picture path back ON, and a privacy wipe that re-enables privacy switches is indefensible**; `installId` **and `usage`**, the owner's own continuous series (v220's "one line per browser storage" — a new id forks it; and `usage` carries no card content and has not been read by a learner-facing screen since v274, which the probe confirms: after a reset with `usage` intact, Cards learned and Reviews this week both read 0, and only the streak was wrong); `nmt`, whose 50 MB live in a cache this does not touch, so deleting the flag would make the row lie over files that are still there; `mirror`, the only update path without a VPN; and `brightPass`/`recutPass`/`recutStat`, which hold nothing and whose pass may be running at that moment and would write them straight back. **The defect inside the fix, and it is the interesting half:** deleting the keys was not enough — the first measurement came back with `usage` intact, 310 reviews and all, because `bump`, `bumpModel` and `dailyBump` each **close over the object they are about to write** and fire on a 500 ms debounce, and `saveReadLog`/`saveAiLog` would have re-created their key as an empty husk 800 ms later. All four timers are cleared first. The in-memory side goes with it (`ERRLOG`, `READLOG`, `AILOG`, `AUTOQ`, `LAST_READ`, `NUMSOF`, `TRANSLATE`, `TAGALL`, `RECHECK`), or the next debounced save writes the old arrays back. **And a refused clear no longer paints an empty deck over data that is still there:** the three store clears sat in one empty catch with the in-memory wipe and `render()` unconditional after it, so a clear a second tab blocked left the user looking at an empty app whose data was intact; the failure is caught, named in the error log, and the sheet says "Nothing was deleted — close the app's other tabs and try again." in the owner's English (Reset is behind the admin gate, so this row is H's alone — `openDB` has no `onblocked` handler, which is the likely cause and its own PR). **No `WHATS_NEW` line, and that is the v408 rule doing its job: Reset is inside `${S.admin? … }` — a learner cannot reach it at all**, which also makes `privacy.html`'s "wipe everything under More → Start over" false a second way, for v459 to fix. The sheet's own three strings stay as they are and stay translated, which is a pre-existing inconsistency with the owner-English rule and not this PR's to change. **Measured on a seeded phone (two cards, a progress row, an inbox photo, a four-day streak, two days in the strip, 310 reviews, and all seven leaky settings filled with Chinese): after the reset and a reload, 0 settings hold Chinese, the streak is 0, the strip is gone, and the keys, the installation id, the language and `usage` are still there.** Suite `verify-reset` — **ALL OK on v458, and five of its ten checks fail on v457** with the five that must not move passing on both. The multicard, finekeep, checkfail and page suites pass on v458. One `TO_TEST` line. **Named, not built: `aiRelay` is read at two places and written nowhere — there is no way for anyone to switch the relay off short of hand-editing IndexedDB**, which is why `privacy.html` must not tell a reader to turn it off. Not yet field-checked — H tapping Start over once is the check: Progress at zero afterwards, and Diagnostics with an empty AI log.
- **A "Multikarte" no longer depends on how well the reader read the photo (v457, H after the contradiction audit: "Go with 1, 2, 4 und 5"; his rule, twice: "Immer wenn auf dem Foto mehr als ein zusammenhängender Wortstring auftaucht, wird die Karte als Multikarte behandelt mit den Punkten drauf" and "wenn diese Cluster quasi als getrennte Cluster erkennt werden können, dann ist es eine Multikarte"):** the app could not do that, and the audit measured it. A page card needs `pic.labels`; `labels` come only from a picture answer; a picture answer was asked for only when the quick look's `textLike` failed (v439), the reading ended weak (v173) or the text check said `bad` (v302); and `picPanel` then refused a parked answer whenever `sureLines` was true. **Measured on one synthetic directory board — a big name over four shop plates — driven through the real pipeline three times with the same mocked Qwen answer, changing only the reader's verdict: quick look likes it, reading strong and sure → 0 calls, 1 card, no page; quick look fails, reading strong and sure → 1 call, the answer DISCARDED, 1 card, no page; quick look fails, reading strong but not sure → 1 call, 4 cards and a page.** Two changes, in that order of importance. **(1) A parked panel answer is used even when the reading was read surely — and the guard that replaces `sureLines` is narrower and right.** `sureLines` was doing the v143 rule's job by proxy, but v143 is about the *text* of a card and a panel answer is about its *segmentation*. What the guard actually protects on this path is one thing: `signAskAI` replaces `sg.lines` with the model's `zh` and `splitCards` then builds the cards from `sg.ai.labels` **alone**, so a line the reader read at 99 % that the model did not list is not merged — it is **gone**. `panelCovers(pic,lines)` asks exactly that and nothing else: a multiset of the CJK characters and digits of `pic.zh` and every label's `zh`, and every line of the reading must be covered to `PANEL_COVER` 0.8. A multiset rather than a per-label `hitCore`, since a panel row the reader read as one line (混合快速单脱水) has to match three labels of three characters each and `hitCore` refuses any pair whose lengths differ by more than one; order-free, so reading order cannot cost a card; digits count, since a number belongs to its line (v323). **A first cut compared the counts instead (`labels.length > lines.length`) and an independent design review broke it: a board whose model lists four plates without the headline would have passed that test and lost the headline for good.** The suite carries that case (`uncovered`). **This half costs no extra AI call at all** — it consumes one the quick look already sent and v447 already paid for. **(2) The early call fires on a photo whose text stands in several separated blocks, however cleanly it read.** The signal is the **ink**, not the reader: `textRegion` already walks the photo's text-like rows on a 360 px chromaticity copy and threw the gaps away; it now also returns `blocks`, the number of row runs separated by more than `MULTI_GAP` 1.2 of one line's height, and `several` is `blocks >= MULTI_BLOCKS` 2. **It had to be the ink, and that was measured rather than assumed:** on the board fixture the quick look reads the big name and **misses every plate** (`readB` 1 against `inkB` 5), so the reader's own lines can never answer this question. The reader's blocks are kept as a second route (`Math.max(inkB,readB)`). **v319's rejection of "ask the AI on every photo" stands and is tested:** a one-line sign and a two-line sign both measure **one block and cost no picture call**, on both trees. The v442 reading-stop is explicitly **not** armed on this trigger (`ok` in its guard): there the quick look *liked* the reading, so cutting the passes short would lower `effScore`, turn a good reading weak and hand the card to the model — the opposite of the point. **What it costs, named:** a clean-reading photo whose text stands in two or more blocks — a poster with a separated credit line, a sign with a plate beside it — now spends one picture call whose answer will say `apart:false` and go unused; v439 measured that 33 of 40 photos already send the picture, so the ceiling on this is the other 7, about +21 %. A photo of that kind also now has its framed area leave the device where it did not before, which is the v173 promise widening — **v458 makes the app say so** (task 4 of the same "Go"). And on a surely-read photo the v441 provisional card can now be replaced by a page, which is a flicker H will see. **And `EARLY` is cleared when a reading is abandoned** (`abandonReading`): v439 deleted it only where a finished reading hands it to `SIGN`, so Cancel on the scanning row, the v437 Crop or a frame the hand moved kept the crop and its straightened copy alive for the whole session — and v457 fires that call on more photos. Cancel still cannot un-send: by the time the button is tapped the picture has usually gone. `N.qk` carries `blocks`, `inkB`, `readB` and `several`, `N.prop.blocks` the ink's own count and `N.panel` `{labels,sure,covers,lines,used}` (the v399 rule), and both decisions have their own log line. Suite `verify-multicard` (one board drawn as a name over four plates, one 坚果供应 sign, one two-line sign: a clean-reading board asks the model with the block line and becomes a page of its four plates; a surely-read board uses the parked answer with the coverage line; **a one-line sign and a two-line sign measure one block and ask nothing**; a panel answer that drops a surely-read line is refused with its own line; the ink found blocks the reader could not) — **ALL OK on v457, five of its eight checks fail on v456 and the three that must not move pass on both.** The finekeep, checkfail, page, photomode, shared, waiting, snapkeep and pagefront suites pass on v457. A `WHATS_NEW` line, two `TO_TEST` lines. **The bound, stated: no real photo fixture survives in this scratchpad, so the block count is measured on synthetic boards and signs and on H's recorded answers, never on his own pixels** (the v386 rule — and this is a rule about *whether to ask the model*, where a wrong answer costs one call and never a wrong card, not a placement heuristic). `PANEL_COVER` 0.8 is unfitted for the same reason; `N.panel` is what settles it. Not yet field-checked — H's 798 directory board and his Meituan screen taken again are the check: one page card each, with the dots; and a plain shop sign still making one card with no picture call in its diagnostics.

It drops every line whose box is under `FINE_PRINT` a third of the tallest line's height from `zh`, `p` and `m`, it takes no `apart` argument, and it is called at `aiReadPicture`'s head **before** `apart` is even computed. On H's 龙人居 notice board that rule dropped **five of seven answered lines** (`drop` in his own record). So the prompt and the code were asking for opposite things about the same field, and the code won silently. **What decides now:** `apart` is computed above the filter and `mainLines` takes `keepAll` — `apart===true` (what the prompt already promises: "when \"apart\" is true … none of them counts as fine print"), **or** the model's own `kind` being one of `FINE_KEEP` — **Menu, App, Appliance, Transport, Office**, the five of the nine `KINDS` that *are* the prompt's own list ("a board, a directory, a menu, a panel or a screen"): a menu's dishes, an app screen's rows, an appliance's sub-labels (the v358 长按童锁 rule says so already), a station board's lines, a form's field labels. **Street sign, Shop, Product and Notice keep the filter**, because that is where a poster's credits, a date line and a package's small print live — v312's own case is a poster. `keepAll` returns the lines with their boxes intact and leaves `box` as the model's own union, so the frame spans the whole board, nothing lands in `snapBox`'s skip list (`droppedBoxes` stays empty) and the reader's label search gets the full region; `mainAlt`, the second reading of a box that passes the picture's edge (v340), takes the same flag. The log says "the small lines of this answer are elements, not fine print (kind Menu) — none of them is left out" and `N.pic.keptAll` carries `apart` or `kind Menu` (the v399 rule), so the field can tell which clause fired. **Where it actually changes a card:** on a successful split the cards come from `labels`, which the v312 rule never touched — so this bites exactly where the split *refuses* (`SPLIT_MAX` 30, a drawing whose reader found nothing, a frame the hand drew), and there `zh` **is** the one card's text. That is H's own case: a board of twelve plates that answers `apart:false` used to make one card saying only the mall's name. **What it costs, named:** a poster the model wrongly calls `apart:true`, or wrongly tags Menu, keeps its credits on the card and its frame spans them — the v312 complaint back, for that one answer. Suite `verify-finekeep` (one synthetic board — a 60 px name over four 16 px plates, i.e. plates at 0.27 of the tallest — answered five ways: `kind:"Menu"` keeps all four plates with the log line and `keptAll` "kind Menu" and the one card carrying every plate; `kind:"App"` the same; `apart:true` keeps them whatever the kind; **`kind:"Shop"` still drops all four and a poster still loses its credit line** — the v312 case, unchanged; one picture call in every case; no page error) — **ALL OK on v456, and the five `[flips]` checks fail on v455 with the four controls passing on both** (the v419 rule). The checkfail, page, photomode, waiting, prompt and shared suites pass on v456. A `WHATS_NEW` line, one `TO_TEST` line. **Unmeasurable here, and stated rather than dressed up: the sandbox cannot reach Qwen (the v405 rule), so no harness run can say whether v455 makes H's board answer `apart:true` in the first place** — this version only guarantees that when the model does name the plates, the app keeps them. Not yet field-checked — H's 798 directory board taken again is the check: every plate on the card, and `keptAll` in the diagnostics saying which clause kept them.

Und wenn er funktioniert, dann sind die Punkte oft an der falschen Stelle."):** the ring of v405 held all three readings, so the first half is diagnosed from his own record without the photos, and it is **not** a placement failure — **Qwen answered `apart:false` on all three**, so the split never ran and each photo made one card. What the three answers say, and two of them accuse the prompt in their own words: the **深夜食街 mall directory** — a board of some twelve brand plates under its own big name — came back with `"zh":"深夜食街\n新辰里"`, two lines, and a note reading "A directory sign showing various brands and the name of the shopping complex below": the model **saw** the plates, described them, and left every one of them out; the **蛙厂 poster and sign** came back `apart:false` with the note "The text appears on two separate signs: a grey vertical sign at the top and a large white poster below it" — the note contradicts the flag; and the **龙人居 notice board** answered seven lines of which the app's own v312 fine-print rule then dropped five (`drop` in the record). **The mechanism is the prompt fighting itself.** The `"zh"` clause says, unconditionally, to leave out fine print — "lines whose characters are under a third the height of the largest characters" (v312, for a poster's credits) — and a directory's plates, a menu's dishes and a panel's sub-labels are all exactly that beside their own headline; the model builds `"zh"` first, drops them, and then sees one text and answers `apart:false`. Sonst denkt man, dass sich die App verschluckt hat und gar nix passiert."):** two things, and the second was found by the suite written for the first. **(1) The line.** A photo of the batch still in `AUTOQ` — queued, not yet reading — shows one quiet line in its own row's box, **"Waiting for its turn …"** (`renderShots`, the `.badge` look of the frame's own hint, no bar and no shimmer: nothing is happening to this photo yet, and the `.batchline` above already says how many are to go and that the app has to stay open, v411/v412). Measured on the harness’s synthetic order screen: the ink rows put the band at 13–83 % down with the title above it, on v449 and v450 alike. **The route is the tell, not the pixels:** the share sheet is the screenshot path by design (v163 — the manifest’s `share_target`, the worker’s `shareIn`, the page’s `takeShared`), so a photo that came through it carries `shared:true` on its inbox record (`importPhotos(files,{shared:true})` → `addPhoto(file,shared)`), and `proposeFrame` sets its ink-row proposal aside: the frame is the whole photo, the quick look and the passes run on the whole image, and the picture Qwen gets is the whole screen. Darüber hinaus ist eine Karte in Crop Mode abgeschnitten worden.", "Und die hier hat er total falsch erkannt.", then, on the v448 dots over his Meituan order screen: "Sehr gut, aber auch bitte Überschriften und so weiter abdecken. Alles."):** four things, three of them diagnosed from his own `numbers:` records without the photos, the fourth with no record at all. **(A) The cut-off card, 江苏淮扬菜代表品牌 (shot_1).** Qwen boxed the nine characters `[40,310,760,390]` of 800×600 — in the 1600×1200 copy 1440 × 160 px, **nine squares**, the most character-consistent box a model can draw —, and `snapBox` kept `[364,678,972,760]`: 608 × 82, four characters with their tops sliced, 42 % of the width, 51 % of the height, **21 % of the area, one point past snapBox's own "specks alone" floor of a fifth per axis**, so the AI's box was not kept and the card showed a third of the sign. The same shopfront one minute later (shot_822, 小厨娘淮扬菜, six characters 1440 × 240, six squares) snapped to 1422 × 218 and was right — the A/B pair the fix is measured on, both byte-exact from the phone. **The rule:** a single-line box whose width is its height times its own character count (`|w/h − k| ≤ SNAP_SQUARE` 0.25 k) is a measurement, not a guess — the characters ARE its height —, so when the snap keeps under `SNAP_KEEP` 0.65 of that height it has found something other than the line (fine print under it, a bright patch, a sub-line) and **the AI's box stays**; the log says "the AI's box is 9 characters wide and one character tall, so it was measured, not guessed — the snap kept 51 % of its height: the AI's box stays" and `N.snapKept` carries the ratio. It runs in `cropSign` **after** the v324/v326 `beyond` bands have joined, on the box as it stands. **The two tests are coupled on purpose:** a box taller than one line of k characters fails the first, so the second can only fire where the height is the character height. **The width is deliberately not tested**, and the reason is a field-confirmed case: H's 业主直租 sign (v305) legitimately loses 40 % of its width when the snap drops the QR code standing in the line's own band, and its box (four characters plus a square code, w/h ≈ 5 against k 4) passes the consistency test — a width rule would have put the code back. **The failure mode this accepts is a crop with room around the text, never one that cuts it** (v380's rule). (`regionLine`, one key in ten columns; a marked photo has two cards at least, so the plural is always right). The v358 list "11 cards from this photo" with a card each under a freshly split photo is gone — the photo itself carries them (D2 of the spec). **A photo that made one card is untouched:** the finished card of v325, the switch being the split's own (`REGION_MIN` 2 = `SPLIT_MIN`), so the shop-sign flow H approved does not move. **The tap opens a sheet over the photo** (`openLookup`, `.ask.lookup` + `.sheet.lookup` — the v222 sheet **without the scrim and not modal**: the page keeps scrolling and the next dot can be tapped while it stands, which swaps the content in place; a tap anywhere else, the ×, or Escape closes it, `closeLookup`): the characters in the Hanzi font (the traditional form with its pill when the card has one), the pinyin with the speaker, the meaning with the language pill, the **three grade tiles** of v421 (`data-g` for the colours, `data-lg` for the wiring — a first cut had `data-lg` alone and the screenshot showed three grey tiles), and **More**, the existing key, which opens the card detail with **← Back** (`S.detailFrom="inbox"`, `backToPhoto`, `INBOX_SCROLL`) and Delete card there returns to the photo too; a tab tap clears `detailFrom`. No picture in the sheet — the photo is right there. **The grade is the decision (H):** `gradeRegion` writes the review through **`recordGrade`** — the schedule, the leech flag, the streak's day and the day's count, factored out of Learn's `grade()` so both write the same way — counts it as a review, and the dot takes the card's colour at once; a sheet closed without a grade writes nothing (`regionTaps` and `regionGrades` in `usage` and the daily row say how often a lookup becomes a grade; `privacy.html` names them). In phase 1 every region is a card already, so the grade only grades; in phase 2 it makes the card first. **A tap beside a small region still opens it:** the `.regions` container resolves a tap that missed every region to the nearest one whose box, grown to `REGION_HIT` 44 px around its centre, holds the point (measured: a 7 × 4 px region opens from 14 px beside it). **Regions are derived from the cards at render time and nothing is written to the photo record** — a put of an inbox record rewrites its Blob, and 237 photos at boot would be some 70 MB of writes for data the cards already carry; phase 2 stores the model's own regions on the record, since a text without a card has no other home. What it costs: one Map of cards by photo per inbox render (measured: 200 marked photos with 1 003 regions render in 56 ms, 56 fps after a scroll to the end), and a grade given on the photo does not touch the Learn session's queue — a card graded Easy there that was already in today's queue comes up once more in Learn (named, not fixed). It is measured against the label's own **character** height since (`rowBand[rowIx[j]]`, falling back to the picked run's height); two constants unchanged, one derived value swapped. **And one more fault, older than v396, that `roundGrid` exposed:** the per-label fallback picture at the split's last gate was `PLACED[id]||seenBase` — the *snapped* frame, trimmed by `snapBox` to the ink the search found, which by construction omits exactly the labels the search missed. On `oven-bottom` this is the difference between five cards of **blank oven-door glass** and ①吐司 ②牛排 ③全鸡 ④鸡翅 ⑤大虾. Only H's own dishwasher answer in the AI log can show it firing. **Measured and dropped, do not attempt again without the named test:** the camera hunt's A/B split of the five changes (PR-A green everywhere, PR-B carrying the whole regression, so landing A alone silently arms B); deleting the vertical-overlap line in the free-standing-element block (all three skeptics broke it — shrinking a corridor moves its midpoint toward the label and flips the centring and occupancy tests *reject → accept*, handing 混合 a 29 %-wide slab carrying 快速, 袜子 and 洗衣液); sloped bands in `labelRunsOf` (the estimator fits +0.010 where the truth is −0.052, wrong sign, and with the true slope forced in the result is unchanged — it is contrast, not alignment); lowering `labelRunsOf`'s ink threshold from 0.15 (recovers 蛋糕, loses 烤鱼, regresses the washer 13 → 11).
- **PWA:** installed and verified on the Xiaomi; runs offline (SW cache-first); `navigator.storage.persist()` granted. **Versioning:** SW cache `zt-vN` in `sw.js` and the label `PWA vN` in `index.html` (`.ver` — **hidden since v225**, H's "Go" on the design review: a developer's line, not a user's; it stays in the page because the shell check, the mirror update and About read it, and More → About shows "PWA vN." to the user) move in lockstep — bump both on **every** change to cached files. The app updates itself (update check on load/foreground, auto-reload on `controllerchange` — deferred to the next foreground while the app is in use since v279); the worker's install fetches the shell with `cache:"reload"` — GitHub Pages sends `max-age=600`, and after two deploys within ten minutes a new worker once filled its cache with the previous shell (the phone showed the v70 page with the v69 script: header v70, no drag in the sheet). **Boot self-check** (`shellCheck`): `APP_V` in `app.js` must equal the `PWA vN` label — **bump both, plus `zt-vN`, on every change**; if they differ, the page posts `refresh` to the worker, which refills its cache from the server (`cache:"reload"`) and the page reloads once (through `reloadSoon` since v279, see below; guard: at most once per 10 min, setting `shellFixAt`); it runs after registration and on the first `controllerchange`; the vendor cache `zt-ocr-v1` survives shell updates — bump it only when vendor files change.
- **The reload after an update waits until the app is idle (v279, H after eight builds in two hours: "nach Laden eines neuen Builds flackert die App … Passiert das nach jedem Update auch bei den Usern?" → the answer: one reload per update, two with a mixed shell; the flicker was the pace of the deploys → "Go" on the deferral):** until v278 the page reloaded the moment the new worker took over, in the middle of whatever H was doing. Now `reloadSoon()` decides: within `RELOAD_GRACE` 3 s of the load (the app was just opened, the first screen is up) or while the app is in the background the page reloads at once, as before; later `RELOAD_DUE` is set and the reload comes when the app next comes to the foreground (`visibilitychange`). The same for the shell check's "refreshed" reload and the hourly mirror check's "updated"; a tap on the mirror row's **Check now** still reloads at once (`MIRROR.forced`) — the user asked for it. The old page keeps running meanwhile with the new worker's cache, which is harmless (the vendor cache is separate, the page's own files are already loaded). Suite `verify-reload` (a synthetic `controllerchange` in the first seconds reloads at once, one after the grace leaves the page with `RELOAD_DUE`, a hide changes nothing, the return to the foreground reloads, an update while hidden reloads at once); the shell and english suites pass. **The mirror suite fails in this session on both v278 and v279** with "The mirror is not reachable: Failed to fetch" from the worker's fetch of the suite's fake mirror — a sandbox or harness problem, not the app (the shell suite, which uses the same reload path, passes). Not yet field-checked — the next update after v279 is the check: H should see no reload while using the app, and the new version on the next return to the foreground or the next open. **Never while a photo is on its way from the camera (v316, H right after the v315 update: "Ich habe gerade ein Foto gemacht und bin danach direkt auf der Learn Seite gelandet. Foto ist weg. Warum?" — Diagnostics at v315 with the previous reading's log restored from the setting and no line for the new photo):** the camera app in front is the page hidden, the new worker took over meanwhile, `reloadSoon` reloaded the hidden page at once, and the camera handed its photo to a page that was gone — the file input's change never reached the app, the photo never reached the inbox. (The v279 rule also reloads on the return to the foreground, which comes before the change event; the same loss.) Now `PICKING` is set by the tap on Take photo or From album and cleared by the input's `change` or `cancel` (at most `PICK_MAX` ten minutes), and `reloadBusy()` = `picking()` or a frame standing (`CROP`, the photo open in crop mode, Crop again too): `reloadSoon` only sets `RELOAD_DUE` then, hidden or not, and the return to the foreground reloads only when neither holds — so the reload comes with the next foreground after the photo is saved or cancelled. Suite `verify-reload` (Take photo tapped arms the flag; headless Chromium then fires the input's `cancel` at once, since no dialog opens, so the case arms the flag again by hand — a worker change while hidden: no reload, `RELOAD_DUE` set; the return to the foreground: no reload; the photo landing in crop mode: a hide and return still no reload; the frame gone: the next return reloads); the english suite passes. Not yet field-checked — the next update taken through the camera is the check. What it cannot do: bring the lost photo back, and a page Android discards while the camera runs (memory) reloads all the same and loses the photo as well — that is the system's, not the update's. **The reload comes at the next pause, on the same screen, and the mirror is fresh within minutes (v327, H: "make sure that new software versions always load automatically without the need for manual refresh"):** three faults kept an update from showing by itself. A reload deferred past the 3 s grace waited for the next return to the foreground, so an update that arrived while H used the app (the worker's install takes a few seconds, longer than the grace) showed only after leaving and reopening the app. The mirror was asked at most once an hour. And jsDelivr keeps its own copy of a branch's files for hours, so a phone without a VPN saw a new version late even when it asked. Now: **(1) the idle reload** — once a reload is due, every `RELOAD_POLL` 2 s the page asks `reloadIdle()`: no finger for `IDLE_MS` 4 s (`LAST_TOUCH` from pointerdown, keydown, input, touchstart, wheel), the page visible, no photo on its way and no frame (`reloadBusy`, v316), no Edit or Add form, no reading waiting (`PENDING`, `READING`), no Translate-all run, no sheet or drawing sheet open, nothing typed in the Feedback box — and then `reloadNow()` notes the screen in setting `resumeView` (mode, the open card, the Cards search, the scroll) and reloads; `boot` puts the screen back (within `RESUME_MAX` 3 min; a card that is gone falls back to the list) and drops the setting, so the reload is a flicker on the same screen. The rules of v279 and v316 stay: within the grace or in the background at once, never while a photo is picked or a frame stands; the return to the foreground reloads as before; the mirror row's Check now reloads at once through `reloadNow` too. **(2) The mirror every ten minutes** (`MIRROR_EVERY`, on start, on foreground and on a timer while the app is open; hourly until v326), and `reg.update()` on the same timer. **(3) The mirror's cache purged on every push to main** — `.github/workflows/purge-mirror.yml` calls `purge.jsdelivr.net` for the shell files (index, app, styles, lang, sw, manifest, signs, nmt-model, privacy); the purge API needs no key; the sandbox cannot reach jsDelivr (403 through the proxy), so whether the purge answers is seen in the repo's Actions tab — **seen 2026-09-12** (H: "Bekommen user app updates ohne VPN?", then "Yes" to the check): 112 runs since v327, every one green, and the v437 run's log shows all nine files answered `"status":"finished"`, `"throttled":false`, both providers `CF` and `FY` true, eleven seconds after the merge — so a phone without a VPN sees a new version within one `MIRROR_EVERY` of the merge, not within jsDelivr's own cache life. The workflow itself never fails (a dead curl only echoes), so its green tick alone proves nothing; the job log is what says it. Still VPN-only, unchanged: a first install when github.io is blocked, `sw.js` itself, the 50 MB model, the Claude provider. What it costs: a reload while H reads a card front without touching it for four seconds — the same card comes back, the session's queue is rebuilt from the deck (a card marked "again" earlier in the session may come later than it would have); a mirror fetch of index.html every ten minutes while the app is open. Suite `verify-reload` (the early reload; a due reload held while the finger taps every second on More, then coming within 4 s of the last touch with More restored at the same scroll and the setting gone; the Cards detail with the search restored; the Add form holding the reload with the finger at rest and the reload after leaving it; an update in the background at once; the v316 pick cases, the standing frame holding through 5 s at rest); the english, shell and autocard suites pass. Not yet field-checked — the next update is the check: it should appear within seconds of a pause, on the screen H was on.
- **No VPN needed to use the app (H's requirement):** the installed app runs from its cache, DeepSeek is reachable from China, and updates also arrive through a **mirror** — More → Updates without a VPN (setting `mirror`, default jsDelivr **`fastly.jsdelivr.net/gh/henglicam/zeichentrainer@main/` since v483** — see the next sentence; `cdn.jsdelivr.net` until v482, **field-verified reachable from H's phone without VPN**, which turned out to be one phone's luck rather than a property of the host). **The default is `fastly.`, not `cdn.` (v483, 2026-09-14):** `cdn.jsdelivr.net` is **DNS-hijacked in mainland China** — it resolves to long-blocked Facebook/Twitter addresses or to nothing at all, reported to hit about **two fifths** of users, with measurements from August 2026 putting it at reachable-but-unstable, TTFB 493–1086 ms ([jsDelivr #18392](https://github.com/jsdelivr/jsdelivr/issues/18392), [21cloudbox](https://www.21cloudbox.com/support/jsdelivr-china.html)); jsDelivr lost its China PoPs and its ICP filing, and the issue tracker has been carrying this for years. A phone in that two fifths gets **neither** github.io **nor** the mirror — no updates, and no reader files on a fresh install —, and the app cannot tell, since a hijacked DNS answer is a dead fetch like any other. `fastly.jsdelivr.net` is jsDelivr's own alternative endpoint, the same paths and the same content, and is not hijacked. **Field-confirmed on H's Xiaomi, 2026-09-14, without a VPN:** the Mirror row read "Up to date. The mirror has v482.", which is the whole path — the worker fetched `index.html` from fastly and parsed the version label out of it. Changed in `MIRROR_DEFAULT` (`app.js`) and in the worker's own pre-`tellMirror` fallback (`sw.js`); `purge-mirror.yml` keeps `purge.jsdelivr.net`, which is the purge API's own host and purges the file across jsDelivr's network rather than per endpoint. **It reaches only phones with no stored `mirror` setting** — `mirrorURL()` is `S.settings.mirror||MIRROR_DEFAULT` — so H's own phone keeps what he typed, and so does anyone who ever edited the field. **What is not measured:** whether `fastly.` stays clear (it is one hostname of a service that has been squeezed in China for years, and the next block would be as silent as this one), and whether a second fallback hop is worth building — falling back to `cdn.` would help nobody, and `gcore.jsdelivr.net` is an untested guess. The real answer is the second origin H has already chosen (Cloudflare Pages, below), which makes the mirror a fallback rather than the only path). The page posts `mirror-update` (with its own version label) to the worker on start/foreground (at most hourly) or on "Check now"; the worker reads `PWA vN` from the mirror's index.html and, if newer, fetches the shell assets into the current cache — content types by extension, because jsDelivr hands HTML out as text/plain — and the page reloads (`mirrorUpdate` in `sw.js`, `mirrorCheck` in `app.js`). **Vendor files come from the mirror too** (H: "text recognition does not work without VPN" — the reader's ~12 MB are fetched on first use, and github.io was unreachable): the worker tries the origin, and on failure or a non-OK answer fetches `MIRROR + vendor/…` (all OCR/dictionary files are under jsDelivr's 20 MB cap; types by extension), caching the result in `zt-ocr-v1`; the page tells the worker the mirror setting on start (`tellMirror`). **A silent origin counts as a failure** (v189, H's phone without the VPN: "Reading the text … still at: loading the reader …" for good — github.io behind the wall answers with nothing, and the fallback waited for an error that never came): a vendor fetch from the origin gets `ORIGIN_WAIT` 6 s, then the mirror takes over, and after one such failure the mirror is asked first for `ORIGIN_DOWN` five minutes (`withTimeout`, `originDownUntil` in `sw.js`); measured: the first file 6 s, the rest milliseconds, the whole reader download 6.6 s against a silent origin. **A page no worker controls reads through the mirror all the same, and asks the worker to take it over (v335, H, 2026-09-08, the Xiaomi without the VPN: "Now he really loads forever!" — Diagnostics `SW no`, the reading at "loading the reader …" for minutes, and `Uncaught Error: TypeError: Failed to fetch @tesseract.min.js:2`):** the v189 rule is the worker's, and without a controlling worker every reader file went straight to github.io, which answers with nothing behind the wall; Tesseract's own fetch of the core or the language file then never settled, and nothing ended the reading. Why the worker had stopped controlling the page is not known (earlier diagnostics the same day said `SW yes` with the same user agent; the registration is not dropped by a failed update, and `sw.js` never unregisters) — Diagnostics say more since: `SW no (registration active)` / `(registration failed: …)` / `(registration none)` (`SW_REG`) and `· reader files from the mirror` when the page chose it. Three things now. **(1) The claim:** once `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` resolves and the page has no controller, the page posts `claim` and the worker calls `clients.claim()` — the page is controlled at once, no reload (the first-controller branch of `controllerchange` runs `tellMirror` and the shell check); a worker that is active but not controlling — a hard reload, a worker that activated while the page was open without claiming — is the state this fixes; a page with no worker at all (a first install behind the wall, a failed registration) gets (2). **(2) The page's own origin-then-mirror rule** (`vendorBase`, `vendorFetch`): with no controller the page asks github.io once per session for `vendor/t2s.txt` with `cache:"no-store"` and `ORIGIN_WAIT` 6 s; silent → the mirror (`mirrorURL()+"vendor/"`) for every reader file, the note "no worker controls the page and github.io did not answer within 6 s — the reader's files come from the mirror" in the error log (so the daily row and All users carry it, v271) and in Diagnostics' head line. Every file the page loads itself goes through `vendorFetch` — the scripts (`loadScript` fetches `./vendor/…` and runs it from a blob URL, with or without the worker), the dictionary, the character tables, the strokes, the Text recognition download —, from the reader's cache `zt-ocr-v1` first when the page has no worker (`caches.match`), and a file fetched past the worker is put into that cache under its origin address, so the worker serves it later and a reload without the worker reads it from the phone. Tesseract's worker and core come as blob URLs from `vendorFetch` (`tessPaths`; the core's URL carries `#core.js`, since the worker only checks that the path ends in "js" — measured: the `.wasm.js` is a single-file build, no separate `.wasm` is fetched), the language file Tesseract fetches itself from the base the probe chose — this build's `initialize` step cannot take the data directly (it joins `data` instead of `code` into the language name; `{code,data}` was tried and failed with "Failed loading language '31,139,…'"), so without the worker 1.7 MB come from the network on every start. **(3) A stalled load ends:** `vendorFetch` reads every body chunk by chunk and ticks (`readerTick`), Tesseract's logger ticks, and `withStall` fails the scripts' load and every `makeWorker` when nothing moved for `READER_STALL` 90 s (a `let`, the harness shortens it) — "the reader did not load within 90 s — no answer from github.io or the mirror" as "Reading failed: …" in the box, the auto card's row says the same instead of "Nothing could be read" (`failPending` takes the message), the error log has it, and the next reading tries again (`_ocrLoading` cleared); the dictionary loads outside the stall race, since it is optional and 2.5 MB. What it costs: a phone without the worker fetches the language file on every start and pays the 6 s probe once per session; a connection under about 20 kB/s on the language file is a stall now. Measured in the harness (no `sw.js`, the origin silent on every vendor file, a jsDelivr-like mirror with real content types): the reader reads 坚果 from the mirror 6.8 s after the call — the probe's one request to github.io, six files from the mirror, five of them in the cache for the worker —, a second worker fetches only the language file, a reload reads everything but the language file from the cache; a mirror silent on the language file ends the load at the stall text after 14 s with `READER_STALL` 8 s and the auto card's row names it; a worker that activates without claiming leaves the page uncontrolled (`controller` null, `reg.active` set) and the claim makes it controlled with the page's variables kept. Chromium's hard reload and its service-worker bypass both keep the controller, so the hard-reload case is not reproducible in the harness. Suite `verify-nosw` (those cases, the Diagnostics head line, the error log's vendor line); the english, twopass, vendor-mirror, vendor-hang, diag, reload, shell and savenow suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's next photo without the VPN is the check: Diagnostics should say `SW yes` again after one start, or `SW no (registration …)` with the reader's files from the mirror and the reading ending either way. **The worker helps only while it controls the page:** H's diagnostics of the hanging reading said `SW no` with a desktop user agent (no "Mobile") — Chrome's "Desktop site" switch, ticked for the Bailian key page, was on for the app too, and a page without the worker fetches every vendor file straight from github.io. More → **Text recognition** shows how many of the ten reader files are on the phone and offers **Download** (`OCR_FILES`, `renderOcrRow`). The worker script itself only ever comes from github.io (it just carries the cache name). Still VPN-only: a first install if github.io is blocked, the 50 MB model download (jsDelivr caps files at 20 MB), the Claude provider. **The first install is the one thing the mirror cannot fix, and the way out is a second origin (H, 2026-09-12: "Können wir die VPN Pflicht am Anfang bitte umgehen? Müssen komplett VPN-frei auskommen.", then "Ich werde A machen, aber später."):** jsDelivr serves `index.html` as `text/plain` on purpose, so it can never host the page, and a service worker may only come from its own origin — **no code change can remove the VPN from a first install while the origin is github.io.** Two ways out were offered and **H chose A, to be done later**: **A — Cloudflare Pages on a domain of H's own** (the repo hooked up, no build, every merge deploys as today; `*.pages.dev` is DNS-poisoned in China so the domain is required; ~10 €/year and a card). Its side effects are all wanted: the shell and `sw.js` come from an origin reachable without a VPN, the mirror becomes the fallback rather than the only path, GitHub Pages' `max-age=600` and with it the v426 mixed-shell window disappear, and `assetlinks.json` becomes trivial for the Play Store, since the domain root *is* the site root and the separate `henglicam/henglicam.github.io` repo is no longer needed. **B — Supabase Storage as the second origin** (H's project answers without a VPN, a public bucket, an Action uploading the shell on every push; free, no domain, but no directory index — the URL ends in `/index.html` —, a second deploy path, and whether Storage serves HTML inline or as a download is **unmeasured**, a two-minute test in the dashboard). **Both are a second origin, so the IndexedDB is a second deck:** H's cards live under github.io and move by export/import, the share link changes, and github.io stays as the old origin. **The sandbox cannot measure reachability from China for either** — that is H's phone to say; the cheap pre-test before buying a domain is whether `cdnjs.cloudflare.com` loads on his phone without the VPN, since that is Cloudflare's own edge. Nothing is built and nothing may be built here without H's word: the domain purchase and the Cloudflare account are his, and only after they exist do the code changes (`APP_URL`, the share text, the mirror default, the purge workflow) have anything to point at. **VPN-off only: Qwen** (v173 — Bailian answered the phone without the VPN and refused through it).

- **The licences are in the app, not only in the repo (v425, H asked what law the web app already has to keep, then "OK, umsetzen"):** `vendor/LICENSES.txt` has been complete since the vendor files went in, and it was linked **nowhere** — neither `app.js` nor `index.html` nor `privacy.html` named it. Apache-2.0 (Tesseract, its core, both tessdata models, OpenCC), MPL-2.0 (Bergamot), MIT (pinyin-pro), CC BY-SA 4.0 (CC-CEDICT, and the derived `cedict.tsv.gz` is under it too) and the Arphic licence of the stroke medians all ask for the notice to be delivered **with the work**; a file that happens to sit in a public repo is a weak reading of that, and inside a TWA package it is weaker still. More → About now ends in a row **Open source licenses** — "The software and data the app is built on, and who made them." with **Open** (`#lic-open`), which opens `./vendor/LICENSES.txt` in a tab. No new file, no copy of the text to keep in step, and the path goes through the worker's own vendor route (v189), so it comes from the mirror behind the wall and is cached in `zt-ocr-v1` after the first look; it is deliberately **not** in the shell list, as `privacy.html` is not. Two keys in all nine non-English columns ("Open source licenses" and the sentence; "Open" was already there from the guide's row), 443 a column and 471 for Russian with its plural keys, no duplicate in any column. Suite `verify-lic` (the row last in More under the About row and inside the About group, its rounded bottom corners, the title, the sentence and the button, the file reachable at the relative path and naming Apache, CC BY-SA and MPL, the tap opening that address, the German three, no overflow at 390 px); checked by screenshot in light and dark; the static key check reports no key missing that was not missing before. **Two things it is not:** it does not make the licences available offline (an attribution notice has to ship with the distribution, not work without a network), and it is not a `WHATS_NEW` line — a learner notices the row and has no reason to care. **Then all six were actually verified against the upstream texts (same day, H: "Bist du sicher, dass das alles public und kostenlos ist?"), and every one permits commercial sale** — fetched and read: `mozilla/firefox-translations-models/LICENSE` and `browsermt/bergamot-translator/LICENSE` are both MPL-2.0 as claimed; the npm package `cedict-json`, which is where `cedict.tsv.gz` came from, declares `CC-BY-SA-4.0` (mdbg.net itself is blocked by the sandbox's proxy, so the notice is verified at the source actually used, not at MDBG); Make Me a Hanzi's `COPYING` puts `graphics.txt` — the file the stroke medians come from — under the Arphic Public License while its `dictionary.txt` is LGPL and is **not used here**; and the ARPHIC PUBLIC LICENSE (1999) text from SPDX's `license-list-data` settles the money question in its own words, "If you wish, you can charge for this service". **None of the six reaches the app's own code**: Apache-2.0 and MIT are permissive, MPL-2.0 is file-level and the files ship unmodified, CC BY-SA's ShareAlike binds the derived database and not a work merely aggregated with it, and the Arphic text says so explicitly ("mere aggregation of another work not based on the Font with the Font on a volume of a storage or distribution medium does not bring the other work under the scope of this License"). No upstream `NOTICE` file exists for any of the four Apache-licensed items (all four 404), so Apache-2.0 §4(d) asks for nothing further. **Two duties were unmet and are now met:** the Arphic licence asks that "you retain this license file (ARPHICPL.TXT) unaltered in all copies", and `LICENSES.txt` had pointed at the makemeahanzi repository for it — where that path 404s — so the text is bundled as **`vendor/ARPHICPL.TXT`**; and its §2 a) wants the modification and its date named, so `LICENSES.txt` now says what was dropped from `graphics.txt` and that it happened on 3 September 2026. Neither file is a shell asset or in `OCR_FILES`, so no version marker moved. **The standing constraint, and it matters for the Play Store: `strokes.txt.gz` and `cedict.tsv.gz` must stay freely available to everyone under their own licences even after the app is sold** — the Arphic §2 b) ("you must make such modifications Freely Available as a whole to all third parties under the terms of this License") and CC BY-SA's ShareAlike both say so, and today that is satisfied only because this repository is public. **Selling the app is fine; taking those two files private, or shipping them only inside a paid package, is not.** That is a direct limit on H's earlier "once online, I will kill the web version".

- **About says what leaves the phone, and that the AI can be wrong (v409, H: "Works Offline under about is too prominent and somehow misleading", then "Also add a disclaimer that the correct interpretations and translatios cannot be guaranteed"):** the row had said "**Works offline.** Cards and photos stay on this phone; anonymous usage counts go to the app's owner." plus "Only when the reading is weak, the framed area of a photo goes to Qwen." — and a sweep of the claim against the code found **the first sentence misleading, the second one false three ways**. *Works offline*: true of the shell and the deck, false of a fresh install, since the reader's eleven `OCR_FILES` (~12–14 MB) are not in the SW shell and the only button that pre-downloads them, More → Text recognition, sits **behind the owner's password gate** — a learner can never fetch them deliberately. *Anonymous usage counts go to the owner*: true but the wrong headline, since it omits the main outbound flow — `aiOn()`, `aiAutoOn()` and `viaRelay()` all default true, so a fresh install with **no key and no tap** sends every new card's text to DeepSeek through the relay. *Only when the reading is weak*: `picOnBad` (v302) fires on a `bad` text verdict at any reader score; *the framed area*: the v348/v393 re-ask grows the frame to the whole photo before it cuts, and on the camera path (v325) the learner never framed anything. So the row reads **"Cards and photos stay on this phone, and studying works without a connection. Making a new card uses the AI: the card's text goes to the provider, and anonymous usage counts go to the app's owner."** — the offline claim scoped to studying, the AI named as the ordinary case, not the exception — then **"When the reading is hard, a picture of the text — sometimes the whole photo — goes to {0}."** and, new, **"The AI can get a character, its pinyin or its meaning wrong. Check anything you rely on."** Three keys in place of two, in all nine non-English columns, each written against its own column's existing vocabulary and its v255 tone (`aboutText()`; 443 keys a column, ru 471). **The trap the translators found and the reason each column was written rather than translated once:** the old string's "only" had drifted into four columns as a quantifier the English never had — ja 匿名の利用回数**だけ**が, ko 사용 횟수**만**, ru уходят **только** обезличенные счётчики, vi **chỉ** vài số liệu — every one of them promising that the counts are the *sole* thing that leaves, which is exactly the false claim being removed; the new strings are checked mechanically for nur/seulement/solo/だけ/만/только/chỉ/เท่านั้น/hanya and carry none. **Cut on purpose:** a second clause saying the app's own texts in other languages are machine translations — true (CLAUDE.md records ja, ko, ru, vi, th and id as unchecked by a native speaker) but outside H's ask, and ambiguous in six of the nine columns, where "in other languages" gives the reader no anchor for *other than what*. Measured: the row at 390 px in English light, German dark and Thai light with no overflow; `verify-picture` reads the new text (and asserts the old "Works offline" is gone); the english, whatsnew, guide, admin, translate, kind, filter and cards suites pass; no duplicate key in any column; the static key check reports nothing new (its five hits — `kind:`, `{0} ({1})`, `opens`, `install`, `message` — are the v403 audit's open finding and the dynamic prefixes). `verify-whatsnew` no longer pins a version or a note's text: it derives both from `WHATS_NEW` at runtime, so the next release note does not break it. **What this does not fix, and is reported to H rather than built** (each needs its own "Go"): the AI row's "What is sent" sentence still says *flagged, doubtful or pending* cards while Check-up, Translate all and Tag all send **every** card, and the payload also carries `gloss` and `alt`; the Usage sharing row still says "once a day" while `sendReport(true)` posts again on every background transition with `REPORT_DIRTY`; the reader download stays behind the owner's password, so an offline-first install is impossible for a learner; offline the app still fires `signAskAI` on every reading (gated on `aiAutoOn()`, not `aiLive()`), costing two failed fetches and a needless "The AI could not be reached."; and with the reader files missing `failPending` says "Nothing could be read. Tap Crop to frame the text by hand.", blaming the photo for a missing download. Not yet field-checked.
- **A card no longer carries a line its own picture does not show (v410, H's shop sign 建国肉夹馍 / 砂, 2026-09-11: "Hier hat er den character fuer Claypot noch mit drin, obwohl ich ihn nachm Editieren explizit ausm Frame ausgeschlossen hab"):** Qwen answered two lines and two boxes, and its union `"box"` `[80,270,760,430]` is **byte for byte its own `boxes[0]`** — the model simply forgot line 2. `mainLines` leaves `out.box` alone when no fine print is dropped, so `pic.box` *was* line 1's box, the frame was placed on 建国肉夹馍, the card's 16:9 window ends 2.5 % of the photo above 砂, and the card's text carried 砂 with "clay pot" all the same. H's own rule since v324: only translate what is also shown in the thumbnail and in the learning card. (His "nachm Editieren" is not a hand edit — `cardFrame` in the v399 record is byte-identical to the AI-placed frame, so nothing moved it; the fault is at card creation.) **Where this runs is the whole design, and the first cut got it wrong — that failure is the entry's real content.** Put in `aiReadPicture`, beside `mainLines`, it filtered the text on **every** path while the frame follows the model's box on **one**; four independent skeptics broke it four ways, each reproduced end to end against a v409 baseline: a hand-drawn frame, a frame H merely **nudges** (`CROP.proposed` is deleted on the first pointerdown, so "most photos"), and the Edit form's Ask AI all place nothing at all, so the card showed both lines and taught one — H's own bug inverted; and on the intended path the card's picture is the **16:9 window** of v329, not the text frame, and the window still showed the line the text had lost. So the test is **`outsideWindow`**, called from inside `placeFromPicture` immediately after `frameOnText` has actually moved the frame, and it asks the only question H's rule asks: **is this line inside the picture this card will carry?** Each line box is mapped onto the photo by `photoFrameOf` and measured against `windowRect(placed)`; under `LINE_OUT` **0.15** of its own area the line leaves `zh`, `p`, `m` and `boxes`. A frame the box did not place is never filtered — the picture then shows everything. **The comparison is the model against itself, through the app's own geometry, and never against the pixels:** `snapBox` shrinks the box to the ink it found, so a poster whose snap trimmed would lose a real line. **The rebuild then had three defects of its own, two skeptics finding the first two independently:** `LINE_KEEP` was written `n<=0.5*lines.length`, and one survivor of two **is** more than half — so the rule could never fire on a two-line answer, which is the field defect's own shape (`<` now; measured inert end to end on the auto card, Save now and `picOnBad` before the fix, and the suite's DEFECT and NORULE runs came back byte-identical); `numPic` is called **before** `placeFromPicture`, so `out` was always empty in the `numbers:` record — the v384/v395/v405 shape, a record that does not say what happened (re-recorded after the placement on both paths); and with the first two fixed the rule **deleted the very line a v314 re-ask had just spent a second Qwen call to recover** (`verify-aiframe`'s `cutline` fell), so it stands down whenever `picSeen.base` is null, which is the regrow branch and only there. **Guards, every one of them earned by a reproduction:** the frame must have been placed (`cut` and `PLACED[id]`/`CROP.followed`), never a turned frame (the window is turned too and an upright overlap would be a guess), never `pic.apart` or a non-empty `pic.labels` (a panel's boxes are the split's, v358, and a drawn lattice, v380, would fire wholesale — measured, three of `oven-touch`'s six boxes score exactly 0), never unless every line box read on the union box's own `picScale` (`pic.oneScale`, the v379 trap), never unless **both** `p` and `m` split one part per line (or the card would keep the meaning of text that is gone — measured: a three-part `m` on two lines), never unless more than half the lines survive (a union covering one line of five is a broken answer, not a forgotten line, and there the old behaviour is the safer one), and once per answer. **Measured:** over 22 real picture answers captured at runtime from six suites the defect scores 0.000 and the lowest legitimate line 0.906; the window flip is between share **0.144 (dropped)** and **0.2001 (kept)**, driven end to end; the card's frame and the snap are **byte-identical** with the rule firing and stood down (`rect` and `snap` compared exactly, not to a tolerance). **The calibration caveat, and it is real:** of the 30 picture answers in the aiframe corpus 14 are single-line and 11 two-line, so only **two** have three or more lines *and* per-line boxes — the "zero false positives over 22 answers" rests on essentially one case, not 22. Suite `verify-framed` (the defect with its log line and `out:["砂"]` while `drop`/`dropB` stay empty, the saved card's text, pinyin and meaning, the frame's byte-equality against a stood-down run, an honest union keeping both lines, a panel standing down, one of three standing down, and the boundary walked in 4 px steps so the flip is a measured number); the aiframe, panel, picture, badpic, autocard, kind, english, savenow, twopass, recropai, edit and diag suites pass (english and recropai flake under eight parallel suites and pass alone). **Open, both named rather than fixed:** `oneScale` is measured against the *original* union scale while the v340 pixel reading may replace `pic.box` and leave `pic.boxes` on the grid reading — PLAUSIBLE, not reproduced, and the named test is an ARRI-shaped answer with three overshooting line boxes where the pixel snap wins; and `pic.box` is not recomputed after a drop, so the union still spans text the card no longer has (no live consumer today — the snap has run, `r.pic.box` is diagnostics, and `agreeBoxes` holds the pre-filter array by reference, which is also why v400 does not newly fire). Not yet field-checked — H's 建国肉夹馍 sign taken again is the check: 建国肉夹馍 alone on the card, and Diagnostics carrying `out:["砂"]`.
 **Closed as a special case, do not chase it again (2026-09-11, H's 来局棋牌社 / 来局 shop, at v415):** the card carried both lines while its picture showed only 来局 on the interior wall — "Hier ist wieder mehr text auf der karte als im Crop. karten text ist wie gewuenscht, Crop zu eng." **That card's record was already gone** (the v405 ring holds three readings and all three were other photos), so nothing could be diagnosed from the diagnostics he sent — the first thing to say when this shape comes back. The likely mechanism was named and not acted on: the frame follows the model's own union `box` as given, `pic.box` is never recomputed from the per-line boxes, and on his 建国肉夹馍 sign at v410 that union came back byte-identical to `boxes[0]`. Then **the photo settled it: it is two separate signs** — the banner 来局棋牌社 over the doorway and 来局 on the wall behind it, a doorway apart — so the model read both correctly and no single frame can hold them; H: "It wasn't actually one sign, but two individual ones. that might have caused the problem. And for me, that's a special case and therefore okay." **Two proposals died with it and must not be rebuilt unasked:** widening the frame to the union of the answer's line boxes (it re-breaks v410 — the 建国肉夹馍 crop would grow to take 砂 back in), and widening only when the missing line is *near* the placed frame, which **cannot work and the number says so**: v410's own record puts the 建国肉夹馍 window 2.5 % of the photo above 砂, so 砂 is near by any threshold that would also catch a banner over a doorway. What is left genuinely open, and is the `apart` question rather than the frame's: the model answered `apart:false` for two signs standing a doorway apart, where v357's rule says a wall of separate signs is `apart:true` — worth one line in `picSystem()` when a case comes back that is *not* filed as a special case.
- **The app tells its user that it updated, and what changed (v408, H: "von jetzt an bitte immer den user darueber benachrichtigen, wenn etwas geupdated wurde", then "Should also mention anything relevant for the users" — described in three lines, "Go"):** since v327 the app reloads itself at the next pause and says nothing, so nobody — H testing in the field least of all — could tell whether the page in hand was the version just shipped. Now `updateNote` runs 1.2 s after boot: setting **`seenVer`** remembers the version this phone last ran; when it is set and older than `APP_V`, a line slides up above the tab bar in the Undo line's own look and place (`#updated`, `.undo`, `role="status"`, gone by itself after `NEW_MS` 6 s, nothing to tap) — **"Updated — A photo of a control panel now makes one card per button, each with its own picture."** when a version since carries a note, **"Updated to v408."** when none does, and "More under About." appended when several notes were skipped; a fresh install writes the version down and shows nothing, since there is nothing it was updated from. **`WHATS_NEW`** in `app.js` maps a version to one English sentence, and More → About lists the last five under "What is new" (`whatsNewHTML`). **THE RULE, and it is the whole point:** every PR that changes something a learner would notice adds one line to `WHATS_NEW`, keyed by its version; a PR that does not — a matcher rule, a log that survives a restart, a closure moved above a gate — adds nothing, and its update says only that there was one. **Most versions get no note; that is correct, not an oversight** (of v400–v407 exactly two qualify: 402 and 407). The sentence is an English `t()` key like every other string, so it ships in English and its translation lands whenever it lands — `t()` falls back to English for a missing key, never to the key itself, so a friend's German phone shows the English sentence and nothing breaks; the four chrome strings ("Updated — {0}", "Updated to {0}.", "More under About.", "What is new") are in all nine non-English columns. Suite `verify-whatsnew` (a fresh install: no line, `seenVer` written; a phone from v401: the line with the v407 note and "More under About.", `role` status, the setting advanced, the line gone after 6.5 s; a phone from v405: the note without "More under About."; `WHATS_NEW` emptied: "Updated to v408."; About with the head and both versions; the German line and head); the english, ask, admin and reload suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's next update is the check: the line on the screen he was on, within a second or two of the reload. **And it never once showed a whole sentence, from v408 to v412 (v413, H's screenshot of "Updated to v412.": "Die updated to message sieht wirklich nicht gut aus", then "Und die Message macht so auch keinen Sinn. Ich hatte eigentlich gedacht, dass mit diesem Pop-up auch kurz gezeigt wird, was jetzt an geilem, neuen Scheiß da eigentlich mit dem Update hinzugekommen ist"):** he was right twice, and the measurement found a third thing neither of us had seen. `showUpdated` built the line with `className="undo"` — the Undo line's class, which is `display:flex` with `width:calc(100% - 32px)`, `padding:6px 6px 6px 16px` and, on its `.t`, **`white-space:nowrap; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`** — every one of those written for *short text beside a tint button*. With no button the consequences were: a 358 × 32 px slab whatever the text, 16 px of left padding against 6 px of right, and — the one that matters — **every note clipped with an ellipsis**. Measured at 390 px: v411 showed 336 px of the 653 px it needed (**51 %**), v410 59 %, v409 50 %, v407 **46 %**, the two-note case 42 %. So H's v411 update read "Updated — Pick several photos at once and they all become ca…", cut mid-word, and **the whole point of v408 — say what changed — had never reached the screen on any version**. The clipping is why the feature "macht keinen Sinn": it was not the wrong idea, it was silently truncated. `#updated` has its own rule since: `display:block`, `width:fit-content` so a short line hugs ("Updated." is 101 × 42 px, not a 358 px slab), `max-width:min(calc(100% - 32px),408px)` so a long one wraps at the card's width, even padding, `text-align:center` with `text-wrap:balance` so three lines come out even instead of leaving one word dangling, and `.t` back to `white-space:normal` with no ellipsis. **Two traps on the way, both found by measuring rather than reading:** `width:fit-content` first gave **195 px and 5–8 lines**, because `.undo` is `left:50%` with no `right`, so the shrink-to-fit *available* width is half the viewport and the `translateX(-50%)` only re-centres it visually — the fix is `left:0;right:0;margin-inline:auto` with `transform:none`; and that in turn needs its own `@keyframes noteup` (translateY only), since `undoup` hardcodes `translate(-50%,…)` and would have shoved a margin-centred box half its own width off during the 0.18 s. **The fallback is words now, not a build number:** `"Updated to {0}."` is gone from all nine columns and `"Updated."` replaces it — v225 took the version label off the header as "a developer's line, not a user's", and the fallback had quietly put it back; **and most versions get no note by the v408 rule, so the fallback is the common case and was the one H saw.** **The dwell is length-aware** (`newMs`: 3 000 ms + 55 ms a character, floor `NEW_MS` 6 000, ceiling 12 000) — 6 s was written for a line nobody could finish reading anyway; v411's note now gets 7.6 s. Measured over **140 cases** (10 languages × the no-note case, five notes and the two-note case, at 390 and 360 px): **0 clipped** where the old rule clipped every note, 0 overflowing the viewport, at most 3 lines for a single note and 4 for the rare two-note case. Suite `verify-whatsnew` (its fallback check reads `"Updated."`, its About check derives the last five from `WHATS_NEW` instead of naming v402, and its dwell is read from the page's own `newMs` — three assertions that would otherwise break on the next note); the english, ask and reload suites pass; checked by screenshot in light and dark. **The rule it stands for: a class written for one shape is not a free ride for another — `.undo` carries a button's padding, a button's width and a button's nowrap, and borrowing it whole cost this feature five versions of silence.** **Field-confirmed 2026-09-11** (H, the v413 update on the phone: "Looks good" — the note in full, over three balanced lines, where every version since v408 had cut it at about half).
- **Pulling the page down no longer reloads the app, and a reload the app did not ask for comes back to the same screen (v415, H: "nach unten swipen hat manchmal einen refresh mit zurueckspringen auf die Learn Seite zufolge. Koennen wir dieses zurueckspringen verhindern?"):** two faults, one behind the other. **(1) The pull-to-refresh guard was on the wrong element.** `overscroll-behavior-y:contain` has sat on `body` since v82, and `overscroll-behavior` is **not propagated from body to the viewport the way `overflow` is** — measured in the harness: `document.scrollingElement` is `html` and computed `auto` there, so Chrome's pull-to-refresh was never suppressed and a downward swipe at the top of any screen reloaded the page. It is on `html` now (body keeps its copy, which costs nothing). Chrome's own article used `body` and MDN repeats it, which is why this stood for three hundred versions — **and the english suite asserted the same wrong element**, so the harness confirmed a guard that never reached the scroller; it reads `document.scrollingElement` since. **(2) A reload the app did not ask for landed on Learn.** `resumeView` (v327) was written **only** by `reloadNow()`, so a pull-to-refresh — or a page MIUI discards for memory (the v316 hazard) — booted into the default mode. Now the screen is noted on every change of screen, and boot applies the note **only when the page really was reloaded**: `own:true` for the app's own reload, else `performance.getEntriesByType("navigation")[0].type==="reload"` — so a fresh open still starts on Learn, which is the v183 decision, while a reload and a discarded page come back where H was. **Why the note is written on render and not on unload, and it is measured rather than assumed:** a first cut wrote it in `pagehide`, and the harness showed the reload landing on Learn all the same — `setSetting` is an async IndexedDB put and the document is torn down before it commits. So `noteViewSoon` writes on every change of mode, open card or search (one small put per navigation inside the app, keyed so an unchanged screen writes nothing), and the scroll is refreshed when the app goes to the background and by `reloadNow`. `RELOADING` keeps the hide handler from overwriting the app's own `own:true` record. What it costs: one settings write per screen change, and a stale note living in the settings between sessions, which a fresh open deletes without applying. Suite `verify-pullrefresh` (the guard on `document.scrollingElement` and not only on body; the screen noted with its scroll when the app goes to the background; a browser reload coming back to Cards at scroll 600 with the navigation type `reload`; a note saying `more` **not** applied on a fresh `navigate`, which starts on Learn; the app's own `reloadNow` restoring as in v327). The reload suite's "the setting is consumed" check is now "the setting is current" — v415 changes that contract on purpose, and the new form still catches a double-apply; the english suite's version is read from `app.js` since, so it cannot go stale again (it had been pinned at v402), and it drives to Learn after its reload. **Eight suites reloaded from a tab and expected Learn** (english, whatsnew, ask, savenow, diag, order, tagall, translate) — every one of them now drives back to Learn after its reload, which is the honest record of the change rather than a weakening of it. Not yet field-checked — H's next downward swipe is the check: no refresh at all, and if one happens anyway, the same screen.

**The note waits until it is tapped away, and a switch under More turns it off (v416, H: "Was mich uebrigens an dem Update Pop-up gestoert hat, ist, dass es ziemlich schnell wieder weggeht. Koennen wir das nicht so machen, dass man das aktiv irgendwie wegklicken muss? Und damit es nicht nervt Koennen wir im menu ja ein haekchen fuer update notifications on/off setzen. Default on."):** the timer is gone — `NEW_MS` and the length-aware `newMs` of v413 with it. v413 spent a whole version on a note nobody could finish reading, and a dwell is a guess about reading speed whatever the arithmetic; the note now stands until the user is done with it. `#updated` is a flex row of the text and a **×** (`.x`, 34 px, `aria-label` through the **existing** `"Close"` key — a new `"Dismiss"` key was written first and the duplicate check caught it in all nine columns, the v371 trap), **the whole line takes the tap**, not only the ×, and `hideUpdated()` removes it. **The Undo line and the note share the one place above the tab bar**, so `showUndo` dismisses the note first: the user's own action wins over an announcement. **The switch** is a row **Update notes** at the head of the About group in More — the checkbox "Tell me what is new after an update.", setting `updateNote`, absent = **on** —, and `updateNote()` writes `seenVer` **whether or not the note is shown**, so switching it on again later does not produce a flood of skipped versions. Two keys in all nine columns (448 a column, ru 476). Measured at 390 px: the two-note line 358 × 77 px over three lines with the × clear of the text, "Updated." 135 × 60 px — it still hugs, the v413 rule. Suite `verify-whatsnew` (the note still there after 9 s with its ×, a tap on the line removing it, the switch off leaving no note while `seenVer` still advances, the row unchecked and its label, the switch back on) — and its text checks read `#updated .t` since, or the × rides along in the string. The english, ask, admin, order, reload, guide, cards, swipe and pullrefresh suites pass; checked by screenshot in light, German dark and with the short line. Not yet field-checked — H's next update is the check: a note that waits for him.

**Undo after Delete (v268, idea 3 of the improvement list, H: "Go 3"):** the card's Delete in the detail and the Edit form and the inbox photo's Delete act **at once, no sheet**, and a line slides up above the tab bar — "Deleted “学”" (a card without text: "Card deleted"; a photo: "Photo deleted") with a tint **Undo** — for `UNDO_MS` 5 s (`showUndo`, `#undo`, `.undo` on the card's surface with the hairline and a shadow, `role="status"`); a second deletion meanwhile joins it ("Deleted 2 cards", "Deleted 2 cards and 1 photo", the timer restarts), the line stays through tab changes, and goes when the time is up (`hideUndo`). **Undo** (`undoDelete`) puts everything back: the card at its old place in `S.custom` with its progress row (`delCustom` keeps card, progress and index on the item, IndexedDB is written again, the deleted counter goes back down — `bump("deleted",-1)`), a card deleted from the study back returns as the next card of the session, the photo into the inbox at its place with the copy `keepPhoto` made onto its cards dropped again (`delShot(id,true)` from the inbox row only). The deletion itself is real from the first moment — a reload after five seconds shows the card gone. Photos → Delete N, the import and Reset keep their sheet. Suite `verify-ask` (no sheet, the line's text, button and role above the tab bar, card and progress gone from IndexedDB, Undo bringing both back at the old index, two deletions joined and both restored, the line gone after 5.4 s with the card still gone across a reload, the study-back deletion continuing the session and Undo showing the card again, the photo's deletion with the card's copy made and Undo dropping it again); the line checked by screenshot in light, dark, German and Japanese; the cards, edit, english, detail, photostore and export suites pass. Field-confirmed 2026-09-06 (H: "Both look fine").
