now `translateRowHTML` draws the row from the state, `translateRefresh` re-queries the row by id after every batch, a tap during a run shows the progress, the button is disabled meanwhile, the finished line stays until the language is switched (`setLang` clears a finished run), Learn or Cards re-render when the run ends, and a run stops at the next batch when the language was switched meanwhile) (`aiCardPayload` with `translate:true` says "translate the meaning into German (it is in English now); keep zh and p unless clearly wrong"), takes only the meaning and its language from each answer — the text and the pinyin stay —, **stages every answer instead of writing the card** (v264, H: "make translation consistent and make sure that cards are not mixed in different languages if the translation was interrupted"): setting `translateStage` `{lang, m:{id:{m,from}}}` — `from` = the meaning the card had when it was asked, so a meaning typed meanwhile is not overwritten; an answer without a meaning is staged as `skip` so the run can end — and **the cards change together in one IndexedDB transaction** (`idbPutMany`, `applyStage`) only when every card has its answer; until then Learn and Cards show the old meanings, all in one language, with the pill on every card, the row says "Translating 20 of 43 … The cards change together when all are done.", an interruption keeps the stage and the resumed run asks only for the cards not staged yet (`inStage`), a switched language drops the stage (`setLang`, and the follow-up run of v263), `running` stays set until the cards and the settings are written; then "Done — 43 cards translated." and the button goes; a failed call shows "The AI could not be reached. 20 translated, 23 left. It goes on by itself when the AI can be reached again." and keeps the button; offline it says so. **An interrupted run goes on by itself** (v262, H: "Please continue translating after being interrupted"): the run is remembered in setting `translateRun` `{lang, at}` from its start until no card is left (`rememberTranslate`), and `resumeTranslate` picks it up again 2.5 s after boot, on `online` and on foreground (`visibilitychange`) — when the app's language is still the run's, cards are left, an AI is on and the phone is online; **a language switched during or between runs retargets the translation** (v263, H: "If the language is changed during translation then all the cards have to be translated into the new language" — until v262 the switch dropped the run): a running loop stops at its next batch and `translateAll` starts a fresh run for the new language at once, a waiting run is re-remembered with the new language and resumed by `setLang`; each batch stores the language it was asked in (`lang` captured at the request, not `LANG` at the answer), so a batch answered after the switch carries the old language and the follow-up run translates those cards again. So a restart, a lost connection or Android cutting the background page's requests no longer ends the translation, and every card ends in the language the app shows; the row shows the progress when More is open. Suite `verify-translate` (a failed run keeps the setting and the line names the resume, a reconnect resumes and finishes it, a reload with the setting resumes at boot without a tap, a switch while a run waits resumes it in the new language, a switch mid-run — two German batches answered, then French ones — ends with every card French and the French Done line; staged: after two batches no card has changed and the stage holds ten, a cut connection leaves every card in the old language with the stage and the run remembered, the reconnect asks only for the remaining cards — the call count says so — and at the end every card changes together with the stage and the run gone). The ai, addai, edit, busy, picture, savenow, recrop, aibad, aikept, aizh, admin and english suites pass (the aibad suite reads `aiSystem()` since). **Done in v258 (PR 5, H: "What is PR 5?" → described → "Go"): the pill for a meaning in another language** — a card whose `ml` differs from the app's language carries a grey pill with that language's own name ("English" on a German phone, "日本語"; `mlPill`, `langName`, `.pill.lang` in the plain pill look, title "The meaning is in another language than the app.") after the meaning on the back (Learn and the detail, `backHTML`) and on the pills line of the Cards list beside Traditional; it goes once the card is translated, by Translate all or an accepted AI check. Nothing else changes, no AI call. Suite `verify-translate` checks the list, the detail, the Learn back, the pill gone after a translation and a Japanese one; the back and the list checked by screenshot in German, light and dark; the english, cards, detail, link, trad and flag suites pass. The multi-language plan of v253 is complete with it. **Russian is the seventh language (v401, H: "Ergaenze russisch als sprache"):** English, German, French, Spanish, Japanese, Korean and now **Русский** — `LANGS`, `LANG_LOCALE` `ru-RU` and `LANG_NAME` `ru:"Russian"` (that last one is not cosmetic: `meaningLangName()` feeds the AI's prompt, so a language missing there gets an English meaning from the model). 444 keys, the German column's own, in "ты" throughout with the imperatives to match (Отметь, Нажми, Сделай) — the v255 tone rule, H's "Be relaxed. This is a fun app.", applied to a seventh column: no «вы», no «ваш», no «Пожалуйста», no formal -йте imperative anywhere in the column. **The seventh language forced two code changes the six before it never needed.** `nOf` had two forms and Russian has three — 1 карточка, 2–4 карточки, 5–20 карточек, by the last digit with the teens as the exception (11 карточек, 21 карточка, 111 карточек) —, so the rule lives in `PLURAL` (one entry, `ru`), the form is picked by `pForm` and the word by **`wordOf`**, which `nOf` is now built on; the third form is a Russian-only key, the plural key plus `"#many"` (28 of them, with one `"percent#few"` — `LATIN_UNITS["%"]` calls both its English forms "percent", so the plural key alone could not tell 1 процент from 2 процента), and a language with no `PLURAL` entry keeps the two forms of v253 unchanged. **The same rule had to reach the app's second, forgotten plural site**: `latinUnitMeaning` (v337) picked its own form with `+m[1]===1?u[0]:u[1]` — a private copy the static key check never looked at — and would have said "24 часов" beside a correct "24 карточки"; it calls `wordOf` now, so there is one plural rule and not two, and a decimal off a bottle (1.5L) takes the middle form, the genitive singular Russian wants there. And **`saneM` did not know Cyrillic**: its four-script whitelist threw away any answer with Han characters unless it also held Latin, kana or hangul, so a Russian meaning that quotes the characters — 健康 (здоровье) — was discarded and logged as "answered in Chinese"; Cyrillic is a fifth class now, two letters in a row as with Latin, and the comment names the trap, since an eighth language repeats it unless its script is added too. **Measured:** the Russian column carries all 444 of the German column's keys plus exactly 28 plural keys, 0 missing (the static key check reports no missing key in any column); no duplicate key in any of the seven columns, counted twice — a string-aware tokenizer over the source and an evaluation of the file agree (en 11, de/fr/es/ja/ko 444, ru 472), the v371 trap that cost the drawing pad its French "Annuler le trait"; 0 placeholders lost or reordered across all 472 entries and 0 edge-space mismatches; the plural rule correct at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 12, 14, 21, 22, 24, 25, 100, 101, 111, 121, 1002 for all 9 count words and all 18 unit words, and at six decimals; **the six existing languages byte-identical old against new over 7,380 outputs**, so nothing of v253 moved. Every screen walked at 390 px in Russian, light and dark — Learn front and back, Cards, the filter sheet, the detail, Camera, More locked and unlocked, Progress, the guide, the Add and Edit forms: **zero overflow anywhere**, and Russian is the first column that makes the admin log-in row fit (its right edge 370.3 of 390, where German's is 428.4 and has been since v284). Two slots were shortened against the ruler: `"Show"` in the Flagged-cards row is «Список», which brings that row from 390 px to 372 (`t("Show")` is used exactly once, while `t("Share")` is used four times and keeps «Поделиться»), and `"⚑ Review"` is «⚑ Метка», which gives the Cards row's status column 75.4 px instead of 103.7 and stops the pills colliding. **The four grade tiles were the tight slot** (until v421 made them three, which ended the problem): `Снова / Трудно / Хорошо / Легко` fitted at 390 px with 1 px of the card's 18 px inner padding eaten and nothing clipped (checked by screenshot, all four labels on one line); the row's floor was ru 391, de 373, fr 364, en 328, es 318, ja 280, ko 280, so Russian was the tightest of the seven and below 390 it overflowed as German did below 373. Measured again at v421 with three tiles: **0 clipped labels in all ten languages at 390 and 360 px.** Suites: english, guide, kind, translate, tagall, recheck, filter, pick, order, progress, badpic, cards and units all pass, and the two with a hardcoded six-language list gain `'ru'` in the same PR (`verify-kind.js`, whose set assertion goes from 6 to 7, and `verify-badpic.js`). What it costs: `lang.js` grows 167 KB → 212 KB, and it is a cached shell file, so every phone re-downloads it on this update (+5.2 % of the shell); nothing else — no font file (Cyrillic comes from the system stack), no new request, and a Russian phone sends exactly what a German one sends. **Japanese and Korean are mine and unchecked by a native speaker, and so is Russian** — the strings to have a Russian friend read first are the four grade words, `"New"` (one key serving both the deck-bar legend, where «Новые» is right, and a single card's status pill, where «Новая» would be — a known compromise that only a `"pill:New"` split would fix), `"Known"` → «Освоено», the header capsules Ждут / Сделано / Колода, «Админ» for the owner's row, and the six guide paragraphs. Not yet field-checked — a Russian phone opening the app is the check: the language chosen from `navigator.language` without a tap (measured: ru, ru-RU and ru-UA give Russian, uk, be and kk correctly give English), ru-RU dates, and the counts declined right on the first screen. **Three more languages, and the two things a script can break that a column cannot (v402, H: "Ergaenze russisch als sprache", then immediately "Ebenso Vietnamesisch, Thai, Indonesisch"; Russian landed as v401, these three as its own PR):** Vietnamese, Thai and Indonesian are the eighth, ninth and tenth columns — `["vi","Tiếng Việt"]`, `["th","ไทย"]`, `["id","Bahasa Indonesia"]`, with `vi-VN`/`th-TH`/`id-ID` and the English names for `meaningLangName()`. All three inflect for **no** number, so both members of every count word carry the same string, as Japanese and Korean do (`"card"` and `"cards"` are both `"{0} thẻ"`, `"การ์ด {0} ใบ"`, `"{0} kartu"`), and none of them needs an entry in the `PLURAL` table v401 built for Russian — the mechanism is untouched, and Russian's column legitimately carries 472 keys against the others' 444, so any check that asserts one key count now has to ignore `#few`/`#many`. **What the scripts forced, beyond translating:** (1) **`saneM` threw Thai meanings away and a quarter of Vietnamese ones.** The v401 comment said it — "an eighth language repeats it unless its script is named here too" — and the ninth did: 健康 (สุขภาพ) is Han with none of the four named scripts, so it was logged as "meaning answered in Chinese" and dropped. Vietnamese looked safe and was not: `\u00C0-\u024F` stops before Latin Extended Additional, where 34 of its tone-marked letters live, so 牛奶 (sữa), 米 (gạo), 一 (một), 红 (đỏ) held no two letters the test could see — measured over 118 everyday one-word meanings quoted beside their characters, **29 of 118 (24.6 %) dropped on v401, 0 on v402**. The `latin` class is widened to `\u1E00-\u1EFF` and `thai=/[\u0E00-\u0E7F]{2}/` joins the conjunction; two Thai characters in a row for the reason the Cyrillic test gives two, since the block holds ฿ and ๆ and one of those beside Chinese is decoration (measured: 健康 ฿ still dropped, 健康 (здоровье) still kept). (2) **The shared card tore Thai apart.** Thai writes without spaces, so a whole clause reaches `wrapText` as one word, and the fallback cut it into single code points glued back with a space: ผ ู ้ จ ั ด — every tone mark off its letter, on the PNG a user posts into WeChat. `textPieces` uses the browser's own word breaker, its grapheme clusters as the fallback, and joins with nothing; measured, the same meaning now wraps at a real word boundary, German/Vietnamese/Indonesian are byte-identical, and the Japanese break moves one character onto a word boundary. **In the DOM Chromium's ICU does the work already** — 123 Thai text nodes across the guide, More, Camera and Cards, 68 line starts at 390 px and 74 at 360 px, **zero beginning with a combining mark** — so nothing was needed there, and `word-break:break-all`, the one rule that would split Thai mid-syllable, appears nowhere and must not be added. (3) **Two CSS lines.** `.filter .fl` clips its rows, and Thai's two-level stacks (ทั้, ชื่) leave **+0.32 px** of top room at the page's 1.45 against +1.32 for Vietnamese and +3.3 to +5.1 for every other language — the tightest slot in the app, and an independent measurement put the same string at −1.00; `line-height:1.6` buys 1.28 px and costs 0.6 px on one row, which `min-height:48` absorbs. And `.stats b{text-transform:capitalize}` is gone: it title-cased every word of the header capsule, which is right for no language that needs two of them ("Jatuh Tempo", "Đến Hạn", and French's "À Faire" since v255) — the three labels are written in the case they should show, and Vietnamese's capsule reads "Đến hạn" instead of the one-word workaround. (4) **`langDefault` gained an alias:** Chromium does not normalise the legacy Indonesian code, so `in-ID` yielded `"in"` and an Indonesian phone opened in English; `if(l==="in") l="id"`. **The tone rule of v255 applied to each:** Vietnamese addresses the learner as **bạn**, relaxed, with the particles a Vietnamese app really uses ("vẽ lại nhé", "Đang vội à?", "Mới dùng à?"); Indonesian as **kamu**, everyday register, never Anda and never Silakan; Thai friendly and plain and **phrased so that no sentence-final politeness particle is needed**, since the app cannot know the user's gender — 0 occurrences of ครับ/ค่ะ/นะคะ/จ้ะ, 0 of กรุณา/โปรด, the pronoun dropped the way Thai apps drop it. **The file stays one file:** `lang.js` goes 212 → 326 KB raw, 62.2 → 95.1 KB gzip, and the whole shell 326 → 360 KB gzip (+10.5 %) — vi +10.9, th +11.6, id +9.9 KB gzip each, measured by building the file up one real column at a time. Boot is not the cost: median of nine loads to the first card, 166 → **153** ms at 1×, 545 → **464** at 4×, 711 → **671** at 6×, i.e. within noise. Per-language files would save ~94 KB a bump and were rejected for four reasons: they move a **shell** file onto the vendor-fetch path, which behind the wall answers with nothing rather than an error and needs the whole v189/v335 apparatus in front of the *first render*; a language never fetched is unavailable offline and falls back to English invisibly, so the switch would look like it did nothing; it contradicts the file's own "one more entry and one more column" instruction; and `app.js` is 61 % of the shell against `lang.js`'s 26 %. If the bytes bite, the deploy cadence is the cheaper lever. **What was checked:** 444 keys per column with no duplicate in any of the ten (parsed from the source, since the evaluated object has already lost them — the v371 lesson), no placeholder drift, every `t()` key and `nOf` word `app.js` asks for present, the tables in step with resolvable locales; detection for `vi-VN`, `th-TH`, `id-ID`, `in-ID` and the bare codes, with a stored setting beating the locale; a full-DOM overflow scan over eight screens × ten languages × 390 and 360 px against a v401 baseline built the same way — **zero new overflowing elements at 390 px, and the three new languages byte-identical to the baseline for every existing language**; the only new finding anywhere is Indonesian's admin login row at 360 px (7.9 px over), which joins a class German, French, Spanish and Russian already occupy and which is structural, not textual; the eleven required suites pass (translate's six console lines are its own dead-call case, identical on the baseline); 63 screenshots at 390 and 360 px in light and dark. **Judgement calls worth naming:** Thai dates come out in the Buddhist era (2569), which is correct Thai civil convention and reaches the SRS line, the inbox timestamps and the shared progress image — `th-TH-u-ca-gregory` would give 2026; and the Indonesian Meanings button says "Terjemahkan ke Bahasa Indonesia" rather than the literal "Terjemahkan semua kartu ke …", which overflows its own row at 427 px against 358, because `translateRowHTML` interpolates the app's own endonym and "Bahasa Indonesia" is the longest of the ten. **Not merged, measured and dropped:** a per-language `{0} hari lagi` for the Cards status column (costs 25 px of the meaning column and buys nothing once "due" is no longer "hari ini"). **The caveat:** Vietnamese, Thai and Indonesian are mine and unchecked by a native speaker, as Japanese and Korean are; the sandbox renders Thai in Loma, not the Xiaomi's Noto Sans Thai, so the filter row's headroom is measured in the wrong font. Not yet field-checked — H's next start with the phone set to one of the three is the check: the filter sheet's tone marks whole, a long Thai More sentence broken at word boundaries, a shared card with a Thai meaning legible, and the ten strings per language listed in the PR as the ones to show a native speaker first. **One meaning per language on the card (v265, idea 2 of the improvement list, described first, "Go"):** `ms` = `{en:"…", de:"…"}` holds every meaning a card got, by language — written wherever a meaning gets its language (`setMl` records `card.m` under it) —, `m` stays the meaning shown and `ml` its language. `syncMeanings()` at boot and in `setLang` gives every card the meaning it already has in the app's language, in one transaction (`idbPutMany`), so a switch back to a known language is instant and costs no AI call; a card without one keeps its meaning and the pill, and Translate all fills it. A typed meaning replaces only its own language (the others stay); a changed Chinese text drops the other languages' meanings (`applyCardUpdate`), since they described the old text; the offline model's meaning is recorded under `en`; the Cards search finds every language's meaning. Cards from before v265 get `ms` at the first start. Export and import carry `ms` like any field; an older app ignores it. Suite `verify-translate` (the switch back to English instant with no call, the three cards made in German keeping it with the pill and the row counting them, German back from `ms` on the next switch, a typed meaning replacing one language, a changed text dropping the others, the migration at boot); the english, cards, edit, addai, ai, export, admin, detail and link suites pass. A static check in the harness lists every `t()` key and count word of `app.js` that a column lacks (`node -e` over `lang.js`); at v254 the columns lack only the count words of the More screen and the owner's reports. The owner's tools stay English: Diagnostics, All users, the owner's Feedback row, the usage report, the Unlocked row, the AI setup form, Mirror, Text recognition, Offline translation, Reset, `privacy.html` (their count words go through `nOf` and would follow a switched language — H uses English). Japanese and Korean are mine and unchecked by a native speaker; not yet field-checked on the phone.

### The flow (AI-first — "nobody wants to see OCR if not necessary")
1. **Camera:** `<input type="file" capture="environment">` (Take photo) or `<input type="file" multiple>` (**From album** — several at once, all land in the inbox, the first opens in crop mode; `addPhoto` per file) — or **a screenshot shared to the app from another app** (v163, H: "a fast and easy function to translate screenshots": the manifest's `share_target` posts the files to `./share`, the worker's `shareIn` parks them in the cache `zt-share` and answers with a redirect to `./?share=1`, the page's `takeShared` moves them into the inbox through `importPhotos` — the same path as the album, the first in crop mode; the installed app only, a browser tab has no share target; Chrome picks the new manifest up on a later launch, so the entry in the share sheet may take a day or a re-install — not yet field-checked) (a "Done, no card" link beside Cancel that also deleted the photo, v163–v167, went in v168 — H: "What's the difference between Cancel and Done, no card?" … "Cancel only"; Cancel keeps the photo, the inbox's Delete removes it) → the photo is normalized (EXIF baked in, max 1600 px) and stored in `inbox`. A pulsing "Processing photo …" placeholder appears at once; the inbox re-renders on `visibilitychange`; pull-to-refresh is off (`overscroll-behavior-y: contain`).
**A photo becomes a card by itself (v325, H, 2026-09-08: "Develop concept where no frame is seen during the first scan at all. Just the magic wobbling over the image. And then the result is the finished card. But if I want to edit something and go to edit mode, then I get a frame which I can adjust." — described first, then "the result can be the finished card, plus an option to save and accept or to edit", then "It can be saved by itself. Is that recommended?" → yes, with the reasons; "Go"):** a photo that opens by itself — taken, the first from the album, shared — shows **no frame and no preview**. The photo stands full width with a soft band of light sweeping across it (`.shotwrap .scan`, the kind of the v288 sweep, which went because the frame then carried the dashes; a faint veil under reduced motion) — **the band moves by transform alone since v332** (H at v331: "Der Bildscanning-Effekt hakt oben links. Muss flüssig laufen"): until v331 the sweep animated `left`, a layout property the main thread draws, so it froze whenever the reader's copies and flood fills held the thread, and the skewed band's top corner popped in at the top left on every loop; now `translateX` from −150 % to 250 % of the band's width with `will-change:transform`, linear, so the compositor keeps it moving while the page works and the band starts and ends well outside the box. Measured in the harness: the transform changes between two frames while a synthetic 200 ms main-thread stall runs; not yet field-checked — the next photo is the check: the light gliding evenly while the app reads and the bar "Reading the text …", **Cancel** at the right of the row. The card exists from the first moment: `proposeFrame`'s hidden branch calls `saveNow(id,true)` — the placeholder with the proposal as `reading.rect`, `reading.auto`, and `AUTO[id]`, `PENDING[id]`, `QSCARD[id]` set **before the cut is made**, so the quick look's placement meanwhile goes to `PLACED` and no frame is ever drawn (a first cut read `CROP.followed` before the awaits and lost the placement). The reading runs as for a Save-now card — **the quick look and the close look place for a waiting card whose frame is the app's** (`READ_APP[id]&&!PLACED[id]`; until v324 they ran only while a crop frame stood, so a Save-now card never got the quick look's frame), the AI's box as before —, and `finishPending` fills it: the placed frame as `frame`, its cut as `img`, no note, and **the finished card in the photo's place** (`resultHTML`: the front's photo box and text box, the back with pinyin, the speaker, the meaning, the parts row and the linked row, the flag box when flagged; a tap on the photo box shows the whole picture and back) with **Edit** and **Delete card** in the row (`data-resedit`, `data-resdel`), the AI suggestion box under it when one comes. **The row is the card detail's own since v344** (H's screenshot of three finished cards: "Please polish, especially edit and delete", then "Looks a little squeezed?"): until v343 it was the photo row's `.meta` — the photo's timestamp in the monospace font at the left, a small soft Edit pill and "Delete card" as plain tint text two sizes larger, the three of them touching the parts row above; now the finished card carries `.detailacts`, the same two-column grid of equal 15 px buttons the detail's Edit / Flag / Share / Delete card sit in (`.btn` and `.btn.danger`), with the detail's 16 px above them and a little more room around the result (`.shot:has(.result)` 12/14 px). The photo's timestamp is gone from that row — it belongs to a photo, and a photo row keeps it beside Crop and Delete. Nothing else changes; Edit still opens the form with the frame, Delete card still acts at once with Undo. The autocard suite reads the buttons from `.shot .acts button, .shot .detailacts button` since; the english, savenow and recropai suites pass; checked by screenshot in light, dark and German. Not yet field-checked. **Flagged only when the reading is doubtful**: `mt.suspect`, a bad AI answer, or a weak reader score the AI check did not confirm — note "the reading looks unsure — check text, pinyin and meaning" (six languages); a Save-now card keeps its v245 flag. **Edit** opens the Edit form from the camera (`S.editFrom="camera"`, `S.editOpenFrame`) with Crop again already open — the photo with the frame the card was cut with, adjustable, no reading until it moves (v244) —; Back, Save changes and Delete return to the Camera tab and the result. **Delete card** acts at once with Undo (v268); the photo stays with Crop and Delete, Undo brings the result back. **Cancel** while it reads (`cancelAuto`) drops the placeholder (`dropAuto`: the card, the byPhoto count, the thumbnail) and keeps the photo with Crop. **Nothing readable, or a failed reading, makes no card** (`failPending`'s auto branch): the placeholder goes and the row says "Nothing could be read. Tap Crop to frame the text by hand." A restart while it reads: `resumePending` reads the card again and restores `AUTO` and `QSCARD`, so the result shows in the row when done. **From album with several photos: they all become cards, one after the other (v411, H: "Geht background processing in der Android app?" — answered no, then "Go for background processing", then "Maybe we should also mention somewhere that the app has to be open to process the images, but please don't make it sound stupid. Make it sound somehow acceptable."):** until v410 `importPhotos` opened the **first** photo of an album and left the other nine in the inbox with a Crop button, untouched until each was tapped by hand — which is what H's question was really about. **The background itself is not available and never will be:** the web has no API for sustained background compute, Chrome throttles a hidden page's timers to about one task a second and then a minute, then freezes the page, then discards it, and MIUI is harder still; a Service Worker cannot host the reader (Tesseract spawns its own workers, and a worker cannot spawn one); and **a TWA changes none of that, since it is the same Chrome renderer** — the Play wrapper only removes the browser chrome. What the app can do is work through a batch while it is open, and that is v411. `AUTOQ` holds the photo ids; `importPhotos` queues everything after the first (`autoQueueAdd(added.slice(1))`), and `autoNext()` starts the next one whenever the last finished — called at the end of `finishPending`, at both exits of `failPending`, from `cancelAuto`, and at boot after `resumePending`. **One at a time**, since the reader's pool is shared: a frame standing (`CROP`) or any card still waiting for its reading (`PENDING`) holds the queue, so the hand always has the floor. **Only an explicit import is queued**, never the inbox at large — H's holds 237 photos, and that would be 237 AI calls. A photo is taken off the queue **before** it is read, so one that fails is tried once and not for ever; a photo already gone, already a card or already reading is dropped silently. The queue survives a restart in setting `autoQueue` and is restored at boot, and a reading that never ends would hold it for the session, so the foreground hook calls `autoNext` too (beside `resumeTranslate`, `resumeTagAll` and `resumeRecheck`). `proposeFrame` works without a layer for this (`AUTO_LW` 440, the layer width H's own records show for the Camera tab, standing in when the queue runs off the Camera tab; a photo that IS on screen keeps its real layer, so nothing about the existing paths moves). **What the user sees, and it is the one thing H asked to be said well (the wording is v412's, below):** under the Inbox head, while the batch runs, `.batchline` reads **"2 photos to go, while the app is open."** — the count only of photos still in the inbox, **one** key in ten languages (`"{0} to go, while the app is open."` with `nOf(n,"photo")`, which every column already had), and the guide's first section gains "From album takes several photos at once — they all become cards, one after the other, while the app is open." Measured in the harness (suite `verify-batch`): three photos from the album — the first in hand, two queued, the line saying so, never more than one reading at once, three cards and the line gone at the end, one AI call each; the queue in the setting and picked up after a reload without a tap; Cancel on the running photo dropping that one and the batch going on (`1/1/0 → 0/1/1 → 0/0/2`); two photos put into the inbox by hand queueing nothing. The english, guide, autocard, savenow, cards, ask, picture, framed, whatsnew and translate suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's next album pick is the check: the line under Inbox, and the cards appearing one after the other while he watches. **What it cannot do:** run while the app is away — that is the part no version can fix. **One sentence, one key, and the pronoun that was wrong at one photo (v412, H on v411's line: "Sounds too long and a little clumpsy. Any better suggestions?"):** he was right, and the measurement says why. Rendered in the real `.batchline`, the one-line budget is **37 English characters at 360 px**; v411's line was 92 and wrapped to **three**. Measured over the app's own 142 real translation pairs, German, French and Spanish run 1.14× English at the median and **1.39× at the 90th percentile**, so a line that stays one line everywhere has an English budget of about 27–33 characters — and the count phrase eats 8 of them. **The clumsy half was the resume promise, and it is dropped on purpose:** the line proves it by existing — leave, come back, it reads "1 photo to go" and carries on — so the clause was spent on a fear the user has not had yet, and a reassurance offered before the worry exists manufactures the worry. The promise stays in the guide, where it is read once. Five copywriters and three judges (user, copy editor, localisation) produced fifteen candidates; two judges converged on this line and the third's winner, the house busy-voice "Working through {0} while the app is open.", was **dropped on measurement — it wraps in 12 of 30 language × count combinations at 360 px, English included**. The shipped line is one line in **all 30** (10 languages × 1, 2 and 12 photos) at both 390 and 360 px, widest 320 px of 350. **And the exercise found a real bug in v411 that nobody was looking for: the line was ungrammatical at n=1 in seven of nine columns.** `"They finish …"` is a pronoun whose referent lives in the *other* key, the formatted count phrase, and `pForm(1)` renders that singular — so DE read "Noch 1 Foto. **Sie werden** fertig … **machen** … **sie aufgehört haben**", FR "**Elles se terminent**", ES "**Quedan** 1 foto. **Se terminan**" (the count key itself wrong too), RU "**Они обрабатываются** … **продолжат**", VI "**Chúng**", ID "**Semuanya**", TH "**ทั้งหมด**" — *they / all of them*, for one photo. Only Japanese and Korean survived, because they drop pronouns; **n=1 is the state every batch passes through on its way to finishing, so it is the most-seen state, not an edge case**, and six of those columns have no native checker. **The rule it stands for, and it is general: a pronoun or a count-agreeing verb must never cross a key boundary.** The fused one-key shape is immune by construction, and each column is written verbless or agreement-free so it is right at every count — "Noch {0}", "Encore {0}", "{0} más" (not "Quedan {0}"), "Осталось {0}", "Còn {0}", "Sisa {0}", 「アプリを開いている間に、あと{0}。」, "{0} 남았어요. 앱이 열려 있는 동안 진행돼요.", "เหลือ{0} จะทำต่อตอนเปิดแอปอยู่"; six of the nine reuse wording already in `lang.js` from the guide's own From-album sentence, so the terminology matches for free. Two dead keys leave all nine columns and one arrives (445 → 444 a column, ru 472). **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — a wording polish of a line shipped one version earlier is exactly the case the v408 rule says gets none. Suite `verify-batch` reads the rendered line; the english, guide and translate suites pass, the static key check reports nothing new and no duplicate key in any column. Checked by screenshot. **Measured and dropped, do not bring back unasked:** "2 photos to go, while you're here." — the shortest and warmest line in the pool, and false: the batch keeps running on the Learn and Cards tabs, so "here" teaches the wrong boundary, and in JA/KO/TH "here" hardens into *on this screen*. **What stays where it was:** Crop (the hand's frame with the preview, Save now and Save card), Crop again, the tap outside the frame and the marching dashes — in those views; the flow below describes them. **A photo of a user interface or of several separate labels, one card per element (v357–v358, H's rice cooker panel — eleven buttons, 低卡饭 柴火饭 快煮 粗粮饭 汤/粥, 时 分, 保温/取消 预约 开始 功能: "I want that if such a picture comes, you automatically detect the different words on it and make single flash cards for each of them"; described in three lines, "Go" — then, on v357's test: "No. It doesn't work like that. I think you have to find out if the image is a user interface and then put a card for each and every single element of it", and then: "Also for all kinds of signs and labels"):** measured on that photo first — the reader reads garbage from it (说, 队定还, 下昌。。功双, every pass at 0), so the picture goes to the AI as any weak reading does, and the answer already carries every label with its own pinyin, its own meaning (v300) and its own box (v312): eleven cards' worth of data in the one call the app already makes. What the pixels alone cannot do: a clustering of the photo's ink found 8 of the 11 labels and lost the whole left half to one brightness threshold, so the split follows the model, not geometry. **The model is asked one question — do these texts stand apart? — and lists them** (`picSystem()`'s `"apart"` and `"labels":[{zh,p,m,box},…]`, `aiReadPicture`'s `apart`/`labels`): true for a user interface (the control panel of an appliance, a remote, a keypad, a lift panel, a vending machine, a ticket machine, a cash machine, **a screenshot of a phone app**) **and for several signs, labels, buttons, menu items or packages standing next to each other** — a menu board, a shelf of price labels, a wall of notices, a building directory, a bus stop board, **a row of shopfronts**, the care instructions on a clothing label, **the section headings on a package** (配料表, 净含量, 保质期), **the field labels of a form or a receipt** (发票, 金额, 日期), **the rows of a timetable or a price list** (v359, H: "Brand names, signs, logos, user interfaces. What else can you think of?" → a list of candidates; v361, H: "implement all as suggested, but no Icons and logos with no text and no Menu prices") —, whose Chinese texts each name their own button, setting, item or thing, so that a learner would learn them one by one; false when the lines belong to one text (a poster's title and its credits, a sign's two lines, a brand above a product name, a label's name and its ingredients); **a price or an amount is never an element of its own, but it stays in the text of the item it belongs to** (v361, H: "no Menu prices" — a menu board gives one card per dish, not one for 38元; v363, H: "if they're part of the meaning then they must be included. Remember the 24H rule" — v336's number with its unit: 宫保鸡丁 38元 keeps its price as 24H存包 keeps its hours and 净含量380ml its millilitres, and only a price standing on its own gets no card). **A phone app's screen is one of them, and its labels are tagged App (v367, H's six screenshots of Meituan, Taobao and Xianyu — the home screen's icon grid, an account page, a tab bar: "Bitte nehme auch die funktionen der wichtigsten chinesischen Apps mit auf (screenshots). Die koennen wir speziell trainieren."):** `picSystem()`'s `apart` list names the cases — a super app's grid of function icons (外卖, 团购, 酒店民宿, 闪购), the rows of an account page (我的订单, 待付款, 待收货, 退款/售后), a tab bar (首页, 视频, 购物车, 我的), the tab strip over a list (关注, 推荐, 新发), the blocks of a wallet or an order page —, and **App** is the ninth kind of v364 (`KINDS`, "kind:App" in six columns: App, Appli, アプリ, 앱), so a screenshot's labels all carry the tag and the filter sheet studies them as a group. **A label's box has its own floor** (`LABEL_MIN` 0.005 beside `PIC_MIN` 0.02 in `picBox`/`picScale`, both taking it as an argument): the v293 rule that a box must cover a fiftieth of the picture is right for a poster's text block and wrong for one label of a 2520-pixel-tall screenshot — 外卖 is 30 pixels tall, 1.2 %, so every label was dropped and H's home screen made one card of all fifteen. Measured on H's own screenshot (1080×2520, Qwen's answer mocked with the grid's fifteen labels): **fifteen cards, each with its own text, pinyin and meaning, each frame on its own label** and each tagged App. What it cannot do: a small label in a tall screenshot is a few pixels tall in the 800-pixel picture the AI sees — an account page's fine print may come back wrong or not at all. Suite `verify-panel` (`app`: H's Meituan home screen with the fifteen labels — at least twelve cards, every one tagged App with its own picture and a frame under 6 % of the photo's height, the head line "15 cards from this photo"); the kind, english, picture, aiframe, autocard and guide suites pass; checked by screenshot. Not yet field-checked — H's next screenshot shared to the app is the check. **Rejected with it: a card for an icon or a logo with no text** (v359 described it in three lines — the picture the icon, the text the Chinese name of what it means, flagged because the model names it rather than reads it; H, v361: "no Icons and logos with no text"). Do not bring either back unasked. the labels come **one entry per element, all of them, in reading order**, the small label under a bigger one (长按童锁 under 洗衣液) included — on an interface nothing is fine print —, an element printed on two lines (加速 above 省时) as one entry with one rectangle, and an element that reads 汤/粥 with the slash kept in its own entry. The joined `"p"` and `"m"` cannot be split on `" / "` — `pySpaced("汤/粥")` is "tāng / zhōu" and its meaning "soup / congee", so two of H's eleven labels each add a part and the joined strings come back as 13 pinyin and 12 meanings for 11 lines, which is exactly the photo the feature exists for; each entry keeps its own. The labels are read from the raw answer, past the v312 fine-print filter, so a sub-label is not dropped on the way. **The app checks only what it can check better than the model** (in `cropSign`'s box branch, `SPLIT[id]`): `SPLIT_MIN` 2 to `SPLIT_MAX` 30 elements (H's washing machine carries 23, his dishwasher's lower panel only two — 加速省时 beside 轻载模式), every box read on the same scale (`picScale`: `picBox` reads numbers as fractions, as the picture's pixels or on the 0–1000 grid on its own, so a mixed answer would put some labels somewhere else entirely) — **the labels are read the way most of them are read (v379, H's washing machine at v378: "Waschmaschine hat nicht funktioniert", and the log named the gate — "the AI calls these 19 texts separate labels, but their boxes are not all on the same scale — one card"):** the model's grid put the panel's last column at x 770–830 of an 800 px picture, so that one box alone came out over the picture's width and `picBox` took it for the 0–1000 grid while the other eighteen were pixels. One column overshooting the edge by a little says nothing about the answer's scale, so the majority decides now (`picBox` takes a `force`, the tally is counted before the labels are built, ties go to the union box's own reading, and a box read on the majority's scale is clamped to the picture as any box is — clamped **before** the size test, since a box forced onto another scale may lie wholly outside the picture and what is left of it must still be a box). It works both ways: an answer that is really on the 0–1000 grid with one small box that happens to fit under the picture's size reads that one as the grid too. A box that is nonsense on every scale is dropped and the other labels keep their cards (v360's rule), where until v378 the whole panel fell back to one card. Diagnostics says "18 px, 1 grid — the labels are all read as px" when they differed, no box covering the whole picture, the automatic-card path only (`PENDING[id]&&!RECROP[id]&&READ_APP[id]` — a frame drawn by hand still makes one card), an upright frame (a tilted panel keeps one card) and not the v340 pixel reading of the box (`altWon`: `boxes` are never rescaled with it). **What v357 asked and v358 does not:** whether two boxes stood side by side in a row band and whether any box was taller than twice its width — H's correction: a panel whose buttons sit in one column would have failed both, and the geometry was the app's invention, not a judgement the pixels can make. The price: a poster whose model wrongly answers `ui:true` is split into its lines; the question decides, and the model is the one that can see the picture. Each box is then snapped on its own (`snapBox` with n=1 and that label's character count, its `beyond` bands ignored — a neighbouring label is not this label's cut-off line), gets `FRAME_ROOM` and is mapped onto the photo by `photoFrameOf` — `frameOnText`'s own upright mapping without its side effects, with the minimum measured in the copy's pixels (`SPLIT_PX` 16) and the frame grown around its centre to `CROP_MIN` 8.5 layer pixels, since a button 35 px tall in a 1600 px photo is under 8 px on a 338 px layer and is a good card picture all the same. **`splitCards` in `finishPending`** builds each element with the existing builder — a one-line copy of the reading (`res`, `mean`, `full`, `nmt`, `cardImg` cleared, `ai` narrowed to that label) through `readingCard`, so every card gets its parts row, its meaning language and its metadata exactly as a card of its own would — the placeholder becomes the first element's card, the rest are saved beside it with their own 16:9 window (v329) and their own `frame`, so Crop again starts on that label; ids are made unique against the deck and each other (`cardId` appends `Date.now()`, identical inside one loop), and **all the cards are written in one transaction** (`idbPutMany`, v264's rule — half of them saved while the placeholder still carries its `reading` would be read again at the next start and doubled). The photo's row lists them (`QSMORE[id]`, the head line "11 cards from this photo" in six languages, each card with the detail's Edit and Delete card, a hairline between); Delete removes one and the v268 Undo line brings it back. Anything that does not pass the check makes one card as before, with a Diagnostics line saying why. **Every test that keeps one card says so, and a straightened panel splits too (v374, H's washing machine at v373 — the rice cooker's cards were right and the washer made one card of all 24 labels: "Aber die waschmachine hat er immer noch nicht geschafft"; the diagnostics arrived after a reload and ended at “Asking the AI about the picture …”):** two faults, both about not being able to see. **(1) The reading's later lines lived in memory.** `readingStatus` saves the log 0.8 s after each step (v267), but the frame's, the snap's and the split's own lines were pushed straight into `READLOG` — so a reload (an update, the v373 brightening pass, the app reopened) left a diagnostics text that stops at the AI's question and never says what happened after it. Every one of those 25 places goes through **`logRead(text)`** since, which pushes, trims and saves like `readingStatus`. **(2) Half the split's tests were silent.** `pic.labels` were only split on the automatic-card path, with the app's own frame, no pixel reading of the box, an upright base and a straightening under 1.5° — and when one of those failed, nothing was logged at all; the same for the last gate in `finishPending` (the frames cut, but the picture answer not used as the reading). Both say their reason now (“the AI calls these 24 texts separate labels, but the frame was turned by hand — one card”, “the labels have their frames, but the picture answer was not used as the reading — one card”), and `aiReadPicture` logs the answer's shape as it comes: “the AI's answer: 24 lines, apart yes, 24 labels (24 usable), 0 boxes, meaning 241 characters”. **And the tilt test is gone:** `photoFrameOf` maps a label's rectangle back through the straightening angle exactly as it maps the union frame, so a panel the reader straightened splits like any other — the tilt costs each label the little room its bounding box adds, not its card. A frame the **hand** turned still keeps one card (that angle is the user's), and so does a re-crop, a hand-drawn frame and the v340 pixel reading. Measured in the harness on H's washing machine with 23 labels: at 0° 23 cards as before, and with the straightening forced to 4° and 9° **23 cards** where v373 made **one, silently** (verified by running the same probe on the stashed v373 code). What this does not settle: H's own washer reading was not straightened (its log carries no “straightened by” line), so the tilt is not what stopped it — the cause is still unknown, and the next attempt's log is what will say. Suite `verify-panel` (the washer at 4°: 23 cards and the split's line in the log); the autocard, diag and aiframe suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's washing machine taken again is the check, and its Diagnostics now name the gate that stopped the split. **The labels are placed row by row, in the order the model read them (v376, H's washing machine at v375 — the split worked and every card showed a neighbour's label: "beim 2. What the model does get right is the **reading order and the topology** — which label stands in which row, and in which column of it —, so that is what is used now (`labelPlan`): every label's own scan nominates one run per row of ink near it (`labelScan`, v359's machinery with its local cut, looking `LB_FAR` 4 box heights up and down instead of `LB_UP` 1.6, and letting a row be `LB_TALL` 2.2 box heights tall, since a panel's row of labels carries its fine print); the nominations of all the labels are clustered into the picture's own rows (`labelClusters`); the answer's boxes are grouped into rows (`labelRows`); the rows are laid onto the clusters **in order** by a small dynamic program, so a cluster may be skipped — the icon rows are; and inside a cluster the row's labels are laid onto its runs in order (`alignRow`, again a dynamic program: each run used once, a label that finds none costs `LB_MISS`), so **no two labels can take the same run**. Then `labelRect` runs again, **pinned** to that row and that run — the region is the run with a little room, the row nearest it wins outright, and a row another label was placed on is never taken as this label's second line, while a spare row of ink standing under `LB_PAR` two or more of a row's labels is a row of its own (a panel's icons) and not their second line either, so 保温 above 取消 still joins. A label the plan could not give a run of its own keeps the answer's box but is held to its row. Nothing lines up — fewer clusters than rows, or under `LB_KEEP` half the labels placed — and the plan is dropped: every label is placed on its own as before, and the log says so.
