Suite `verify-stop` (the washer with the answer at 1.5 s: the stop, one pass instead of 44, the card 洗衣机 with its picture, one picture call and no text check, an empty error log; the answer at 25 s: no stop, every pass; a bad answer: no stop, every pass, no card — one picture call, since the washer's frame is the whole photo already and a bad answer has nothing to regrow; the −8° 邪不压正: the answer used, no stop; a clean sign: nothing sent early; Cancel during the stopped reading: nothing left); **run unchanged on a v441 root the same suite's stop case fails** — no `N.stop`, 44 passes, the reading 7.1 s against 6.3 s here with one pass —, so it tests the app and not the clock (the v419/v439 rule). The aiframe suite passes with `bottleStop` beside its cases, and the panel, savenow, badpic, early and provisional suites pass; `verify-picture` and `verify-autocard` fail byte-identically on the v441 root (the harness's own service-worker line and the v417 `.card .glyph` timeout). One `WHATS_NEW` line (a hard photo becomes a card as soon as the AI has answered) and one `TO_TEST` line. **Open, named:** the A/B's v442 run overlapped the `r.passesDone` edit by a few minutes — the guard changes a log line and nothing the measurement reads, so the numbers stand, but it was not re-run. Not yet field-checked — H's next panel is the check: the card seconds after Qwen's answer, and Diagnostics carrying `N.stop` with "the reading stopped at … — N passes read".
- **A merged label is measured by its head, and a cut-off label at the photo's edge gets no card (v443, H's washing machine in three close-ups at v442, 2026-09-12: "Ein paar Karten sind noch immer nicht richtig gelesen. Sie zeigen nicht den richtigen Ausschnitt, sondern einfach das gesamte Bild beziehungsweise der Text passt nicht zum Bild."):** three readings, and his diagnostics carried all three (the v405 ring), so the three photos were not needed for the diagnosis. **Readings 1 and 2 — the right and the left block, 10 cards each, 9 with their own crop, and one card of each with the whole panel: 漂洗 and 柔顺剂.** Both are plain two-character labels standing between two labels the model merged with their 长按 sub-line — 漂洗 between 时间长按远程 and 温度长按联网, 柔顺剂 between 洗衣液长按童锁 and +烘干长按单烘 — and the v389 ordered fill, which exists for exactly this gap, measures a candidate's width per character against the row's: the row's per-character width is the placed run's width over the label's character count, and a merged label is **six or seven characters on a run two or three characters wide** (its sub-line stands under the head at half size), so the row's reference was a third of the true character width and the plain neighbour measured 2.9× (漂洗) and 2.2× (柔顺剂) against `RL_WIDE`'s 1.8 — read straight out of H's own `found.rects` and the labels' texts, no photo needed. The v407 head match found the merged label its run and then handed the fill a count the run never had. `nHead(j)` — the head before 长按 (`labelHead`), else the whole label — is the count now in the ordered fill, in the half-reading pass and for the candidates; by it 漂洗 measures 0.96 and 柔顺剂 0.73 of the row. And a run that read the whole merged label (`hitCore` on the full text, e.g. 时间长按远各, +烘干长按单妊) holds two lines, so `linesOf` counts its height as two for the row's line height (`median` takes the upper of two, so one two-line run had set the bar for the whole row). **Reading 3 — the dial, six labels, none placed, six cards with the whole photo.** Three of them are right: 左筒, 右筒 and 下筒 are the dial's own words, the reader cannot read them along the ring (v387), and the whole photo of a dial close-up is the dial — H's own v392 rule. The other three were wrong in the way he named: the model listed 羽绒, 血清洗 (a misreading of 血渍洗) and 时间长按远程 from the sliver of the next block at the photo's right edge — every one of their boxes ends at x=800 of 800 —, the reader found none of them, and each got the whole dial with its text half outside the picture. **The v312 rule asks the model to leave out a line the picture's edge cuts; a box on the edge with no run of its own is that line.** So a label the reader could not place whose box touches the picture's edge (within 0.02, the v313 threshold) on a side where the proposal is the photo's own edge (the v315 test on `seenBase`) is left out of the split — in the whole-picture branch (v380) only, see below — "羽绒, 血清洗, 时间长按远程 stand at the picture's edge, in a picture whose labels the reader could not find — cut off by the photo, no cards for them", `N.edgeOut` in the record. Never on a proposal that ends inside the photo (there is more beyond it, v313's case), never a label the reader placed. What it costs, named: a real label at a whole-panel photo's edge that the reader fails to name — 智洗烘 in the last column of H's wide shot, if the reader misses it — gets no card where it got the whole panel; H's field runs named that column, and a card with the whole panel is the picture he rejected at v382. **Measured on the washer fixture (H's wide shot, the drawn lattice of v380) on both trees:** with H's merged label shapes — 洗衣液长按童锁, +烘干长按单烘, 时间长按远程, 温度长按联网 — the reader names 14, the half reading places 2, and the row's order places **柔顺剂 on v443 and nothing on v442** (`ordered` 1 against 0): 17 of 19 cards on their own label against 16, **none on a neighbour's** on either tree; 漂洗 is placed on both there (its run reads on the wide shot), so the fixture proves one of the two field misses and the other stands on the arithmetic above. The original wash case stood at 17 of 19 and 0 wrong on both trees — until the refute round below took one of them back on purpose (16 on v443, 0 wrong) —, and every other case of the suite is unchanged. **The first cut of the edge rule ran in the reader branch as well, and the fixture caught it at once:** it dropped 混合 — a real label whose drawn box touches the *left* edge of the wide shot (the lattice is clamped at 0) and which the reader misses there — and the wash case fell to 18 cards on the fix and 18 on what was meant to be the baseline, which turned out to be the same server (the suite's page URL carried a hardcoded port; it takes `PORT` and `ROOT` since, so the two trees really are two trees). Hence the rule lives in the whole-picture branch only. Suite `verify-panel` gains `merged` (above) and `edgeWhole` (three labels of round-pixel boxes on the dial that nothing in the picture reads as, and 蒸汽 on the picture's right edge: the reader finds 0, the three keep the whole picture, 蒸汽 gets no card, the log line and `N.edgeOut` say so — four cards on v442, three on v443); a first version of that fixture put its boxes on multiples of eight, the app rightly refused to call them a drawing, and the reader path never ran — a fixture has to have the answer's own shape, which on H's dial answer is round pixels. The aiframe suite passes with no page error. **Then three skeptics were set on the change before it shipped, and two of them broke it (the refute of v443, a workflow of three independent readers and a judge, each with the code of both trees and H's records):** **(A) The head-based width handed a neighbour's button through the ordered fill.** The whole-label count had refused every real-width run on a merged row — the label's own and its neighbour's alike — and the fill of v389 accepted a gap with a placed label on **one** side only (`(L||R)`, since v391). So when the model **omits a row's last label** — ordinary, H's answers for this panel carried 20, 21 and 25 labels on three consecutive runs — that label's own run stands free at the row's end on a column another row vouches for (羊毛's), the unread label before it has no column of its own (大件 and 内裤 are H's documented misses, v386 and v407), and the fill hands 漂洗 温度's button at a width ratio of 1.03. Measured in a probe of the placement core extracted verbatim from both trees: 漂洗←温度 on the first cut of v443 and 漂洗←— on v442, 柔顺剂←+烘干 the same way on the left block — and **the hole pre-exists on a plain row** (时间 listed without its 长按 line: 漂洗←温度 on v442 too), which is exactly what v396 named: "do not bring an order-based fill for a row's ends back without a test for the omitted label". **The gap must be closed on both sides now** (`L&&R`, v389's own sentence): a row's first or last label the reader cannot read keeps the whole picture, the honest v380 answer, and a pixel cannot tell an unread label's own run from its omitted neighbour's there. What it costs, measured: on H's wide shot (the `wash` fixture) 洗衣液, the first label of its row, had been placed by the one-sided fill on every run since v391 and keeps the panel now — 17 → 16 of 19 with their own crop, 0 wrong, the reader's own counts identical across six runs; H's two close-ups are untouched, since there 洗衣液长按童锁 is placed by its head reading. Named, not built: a gap bounded on both sides can still slide when the model omits a label *inside* it and the unread label's whole column is unplaced — the same shape moved inward, identical on v442, and no fixture or field record shows it. **(B) The edge rule's own hole:** with three of four labels at the edge the drop left one, under `SPLIT_MIN`, no split was set, and the one-card path built its text from **every line of the answer** — the card would have carried the very lines the log called left out, under the whole dial: H's complaint in one card. The drop applies only while `SPLIT_MIN` labels remain; fewer, and every label keeps the whole picture as at v442. Two more from the same reader: the rule stands down on a straightened copy (`seenAngle`), whose edge is not the photo's along the rows — every panel so far was under 1.5°, so this is a guard, not a fix —, and the log line no longer claims the reader "found it nowhere" (vacuous when the reader found nothing at all, wrong when `readLabels` threw); it says the picture's labels could not be found, which is the branch's own condition. **(C) `linesOf` read the wrong reading:** it asked the stored best reading whether it held the sub-line, and a clean head reading (1.0) outranks a whole-label one (0.83) as the stored best, so a run that read both lines on one copy and the head alone on another counted as one line and the row's height stayed the two-line run's; it asks every reading of the run since, and `found.two` records how many placed runs held two lines (the v399 rule). Suite `verify-panel` gains three cases from the round: `omitted` (the merged answer without 温度, 大件 and 内裤, the reader blinded to those three — **on the tree without the both-sides rule 漂洗's card lands on 温度's button at 84–92 % across, with it 漂洗 keeps the whole panel**, skeptic A's probe driven through the whole app; on v442 the width still refuses, since the hole needs the head-based width to open), `twoLine` (a tall run's head reading alternated with the whole merged text, as two of a run's four readings would be: `found.two` 2 and 漂洗 placed by the order on its own button, where v442 keeps the panel — the pre-fix tree also places it, its one-line run passing the two-line height's floor at 0.61 against 0.6, by a hundredth, so that half of the change is held by the record and the arithmetic rather than by a placement that flips) and `edgeFew` (four labels, three on the edge: four whole-picture cards, no drop, no log line). **And a v442 suite case was measured to be timing-fragile and given its margin:** `verify-early`'s `bad` case and `verify-provisional`'s `pana6` case let the picture mock answer at 12 s so that the reading — pana6, 10–13 s on this box — ends first and the late branch (`picOnBad` taking the early answer, v441's gate) is what runs; under a parallel suite the reading took longer than 12 s, the answer landed inside it and the case measured the v442 stop instead, failing for a reason that was the clock's, not the app's (the v439/v419 shape). Both answer at 20 s now, under `AI_TIMEOUT_MS`, and both suites pass with it (run beside the aiframe suite, which passes on the final tree too). No `WHATS_NEW` line — a placement rule, the v408 rule. **And v442 saved nothing on these three photos, which is worth writing down:** Qwen answered in 24.4, 25.1 and 15.9 s — the picture call landed at the very end of the reading (`early.ahead` 24.6 and 25.5 s, the stop at "the whole frame" with 40–42 passes read) or not before it (the dial photo was straightened by 2°, over `SKEW_STOP`, 50 passes). The saving of v442 is the reader's time past Qwen's answer, and on this evening Qwen took as long as the reader. Not yet field-checked — H's washing machine taken again in the same three close-ups is the check: 漂洗 and 柔顺剂 with their own buttons, and the dial photo with three cards, not six.
- **A row's first label is placed again, and a trailing gap stays refused (v444, H's washing machine in three close-ups at v443, 2026-09-13: "Falsch gecropped", ten card screenshots and two Diagnostics dumps):** the ring of v405 carried all four readings, so every one of the eight wrong crops was diagnosed without the photos — and they are **three separate faults on three separate paths**, not one. **Three of them are v443's own regression, and it was predicted in writing.** 洗衣液长按童锁 and 柔顺剂 (the bottom row `[洗衣液长按童锁, 柔顺剂, +烘干长按单烘]`, only +烘干 placed) and 血渍洗 (the row `[血渍洗, 内裤]`, only 内裤 placed) are every one of them **the first label of its row**, so `L` is null and v443's `L&&R` can never fire: the guard refused exactly the labels the v389 ordered fill exists for, and the log said "no run of the picture reads as it — the whole picture". v443's own entry had measured the cost on the wash fixture (own 17 → 16) and shipped anyway on the judge's "F1 is simpler"; the field charged three cards for it the same evening. **The rule it stands for: a guard measured to cost a card on the fixture costs cards in the field, and "simpler" is not a reason to accept that when the alternative was measured to be safe too.** **The first cut of the repair was `(L||R)` — a placed label on either side — and a skeptic broke it before it shipped, which is the entry's real content.** With both ends open, the defect v443 existed to close comes back at the **trailing** end: when the model omits a row's last label — ordinary, H's answers for this panel carried 20, 21 and 25 labels on three consecutive runs — that label's own run stands free at the row's end on a column another row vouches for, and the unread label before it takes the neighbour's button. Measured on H's own `wash.jpg` through the app's own `labelRunsOf`, with the placement core extracted verbatim from both trees: **漂洗←温度 and 血渍洗←内裤 on `(L||R)`, 漂洗←— and 血渍洗←— on v443.** So the gate is **`R&&…`**: a gap is filled only where a placed label stands *after* it — a row's leading gap is allowed (H's three cards), a trailing gap is refused (the omitted label). Measured: it closes all four reproductions, keeps the field fix, and the panel suite is ALL OK with the wash fixture at **17 of 19 on their own label, 0 wrong**. **And the second guard is empirical, not principled, which is said here rather than hidden.** (Quantified at v447 by an independent refutation run over H's own `wash.jpg` through the app's own `labelRunsOf`: on row 0, **42 of the 68 runs overlapping the row band — 62 % — fall outside the `RL_HGT` window and are invisible to `g0`**, and on row 2, 12 of 34; all 268 run heights are min 8 / p25 10 / median 16 / max 45 against label runs of 25–33. That run also confirmed the shipped `R&&` gate is the safe form — it was its own recommended stopgap — while the `(L||R)` candidate this version rejected does carry a neighbour's button whenever the unread label's own run is a sliver or an icon-swallower.) `g0` counts the band's candidates standing in the gap *before* the columns filter them, so a run nobody vouches for still makes the order ambiguous — but `cand0` keeps the `RL_HGT` height test, so it is **not** "every run of the band", as the first comment claimed: measured on H's photo, **42 of the 68 runs overlapping row 0 fall outside that window and are invisible to the count** (all 268 run heights: min 8, p25 10, median 16, max 45, against label runs of 25–33). - **The owner's relay (v191, H: "Why would a friend enter a key of their own?" → "Go with the relay"):** a phone without a key for a provider sends its OpenAI-style requests to H's Supabase edge function `ai-relay` (`relayUrl()` = `SHARE_URL + /functions/v1/ai-relay`, `RELAY_PROVIDERS` = deepseek and qwen, `viaRelay(pv)`, `relayFetch`, setting `aiRelay` absent = on): body `{provider, body}`, headers `apikey` and `Authorization: Bearer` with the publishable key and `x-install` with the installation id; the function adds H's provider key from its secrets, counts the call in the table `relay_usage` through the SQL function `relay_bump` (per phone and per day) and refuses with 429 above the per-phone cap, which is **per provider** since 2026-09-14, or `CAP_ALL` calls a day (the numbers, and why they are what they are, in the cap paragraph at the end of this entry) ("the daily limit of the owner's relay is reached — try again tomorrow"; 404/503 = "the owner's relay is not set up"), then returns the provider's JSON unchanged with CORS headers. **The phone's own key always wins**; `aiOn()` and `pictureProvider()` count a relay provider as available, so a fresh install has DeepSeek text checks and Qwen pictures from the first card. The three transports (`aiAsk`, `aiCharAlternatives`, `aiReadPicture`) each carry the relay branch; the status line says "…, through the app owner's relay", the form's provider line "no key on this phone — the owner's relay is used.", the What-is-sent line and `privacy.html` describe the relay (it forwards and keeps only a count; H's key never reaches the phone). The code lives in the repo: `supabase/functions/ai-relay/index.ts` (Deno, deployed by H from the dashboard's editor with "Verify JWT" off and the secrets `DEEPSEEK_KEY`, `QWEN_KEY` and `OWNER_INSTALL`) and `supabase/relay.sql` (the table and the counter function, run once in the SQL Editor); neither is in the shell. **Field-confirmed the same evening:** H deployed the function from the iPad (the dashboard's editor, the name and Deploy button in the footer below the code, the JWT switch under the Settings tab as "Verify JWT with legacy secret"), the first call answered 400 "unknown provider" until the secrets were in (the function says that for a missing key too), then 焦香蜜汁肠 came back through the relay from H's phone without any key ("Looks like it worked"). Remove key on the last key had switched the automatic check off (the v172 rule for a phone without AI) while the relay still read pictures — since v192 the check goes off only when no AI is left. **The Qwen endpoint follows the key's own prefix (2026-09-14, H after a day of relay errors: "Go, make the relay pick by key prefix"):** Aliyun's console hands out two Qwen credentials side by side on two different endpoints — **`sk-ws-…`, pay-as-you-go (按量付费), on `dashscope.aliyuncs.com`**, and **`sk-sp-…`, a Token Plan subscription (套餐), on `token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com`** — and each is rejected by the other's endpoint with **`401 Incorrect API key provided`**, which reads like a dead key and is not one. That is what H's phone reported all morning: yesterday's `403 Free quota exhausted` on the old pay-as-you-go key, then a Lite 套餐 bought to fix it, its `sk-sp-` key pasted into `QWEN_KEY`, and every picture call 401ing against the pay-as-you-go address. `qwenUrl(key)` picks the address from the prefix, so the two can no longer fall out of step — including next month, when the 套餐 lapses and the account goes back to pay-as-you-go. `QWEN_PLAN_URL` overrides the Token Plan address from the secrets, so a console that spells its path differently needs no code change. **And both keys are `.trim()`ed**, since a newline picked up while pasting into the secrets form on a phone goes straight into the `Bearer` header and produces the same 401 — a whitespace-only key now also counts as absent, so the function answers its own "unknown provider" instead of sending a broken header. **The two things the 401 had already proved, worth keeping as a diagnosis rule:** a wrong or missing secret *name* answers `400 unknown provider`, so a 401 says the secret is there and non-empty; and the 401 body is Aliyun's own text, so the request reached Aliyun and nothing is blocked between Supabase and Dashscope. **`APP_V` was not bumped** — `supabase/` is not in the worker's shell list and no phone fetches it, so a version bump would cost every phone a shell re-download for a file it never reads. **The per-phone cap is per provider, and the owner's phone is exempt (2026-09-14, H after his rice cooker made one card on a freshly topped-up account: "Aber hab ich heute echt schon 200 calls gemacht???", then "Sollten wir das cap nicht allgemein hochsetzen?", then "Go, bau es"):** he had, and the number was guarding the wrong thing. **Every relay call counted against one cap of 200, and the two providers cost nothing alike:** the text check goes to **DeepSeek** (`textProvider()`, ~500 tokens on a separate **pay-as-you-go** account at well under ¥0.01) and the picture to **Qwen** (~2,000 tokens off a fixed weekly **prepaid** Token Plan quota), so one hard photo is two counted calls and a Check-up over his ~270-card deck is **55** of them (`RECHECK_BATCH` 5) — and since `current_date` is Postgres's own, on Supabase's UTC, the day resets at **08:00 Beijing**, so a morning session sits in one bucket that began four hours earlier. **Measured from his own Bailian console the same morning, and it is what settles the numbers:** 29,000 tokens is **0.3 %** of the 7-day quota, so ~10M tokens a week, ~1.4M a day, **~700 picture calls a day** before the money is the constraint — while `CAP_ALL` **10000**, if those were pictures, is 20M tokens, **twice the whole week's quota in a single day**, so the global cap stood above the thing it was supposed to guard and guarded nothing. His morning spent its 200 on text checks and refusals with **99.7 % of the quota unused**. **The cap lives on the provider now** (`PROVIDERS[name].cap` — qwen **80**, deepseek **400** — so a provider cannot be added without one, and a missing one fails closed, which is the right way for a budget guard to fail), and **no schema change was needed**: `relay_usage` is keyed `(install, day)`, so counting under `<install>:<provider>` gives each provider its own row and its own count while `relay_bump`'s own sum over the day stays a true total across everything. `CAP_ALL` is **6000** — a backstop against a runaway or abuse, **not** a budget guard, since the Token Plan is prepaid and cannot be overspent and DeepSeek at 8,000 calls is about ¥2; **2000 is deliberately not used again**, being the number v409 had to raise because it locked the whole class out on their first day. **The owner's phone is not capped per provider** (it is the one that tests the app) but is never past `CAP_ALL`, and **its installation id lives in the secrets as `OWNER_INSTALL` and not in this public file** — the relay has "Verify JWT" off and the publishable key is in the app, so anyone who read the id here could claim the exemption by setting `x-install`; unset means nobody is exempt, which is the safe default and also the **v199 fallback** (a secret that silently does not take costs H the exemption and nothing else). **And the deploy unblocks a capped phone by itself, before the exemption applies at all:** the composite key starts every phone on a fresh row at its next call. **Named, not changed:** the counter still bumps **before** the cap is checked, so a refused call is counted too and a capped phone's number keeps climbing while nothing works — it is per day, and the deploy resets it. **`APP_V` was not bumped** (the qwenUrl precedent above) and no app string changed: a phone can now hit the Qwen cap while DeepSeek still answers, and "the daily limit of the owner's relay is reached — try again tomorrow" is true of that too. Ten branches of the cap decision were checked as a pure function (the owner forwarding at 5,000 and still stopped by `CAP_ALL`, a classmate at 80/81 qwen and 400/401 deepseek, the owner's id with no secret set falling back to the ordinary cap, a malformed id, an unknown provider). Not yet field-checked — the sandbox cannot reach supabase.co (the v170 rule), so **H deploying it and taking the rice cooker again is the check**, with `select install, calls from relay_usage where day = current_date` naming the two rows. The sandbox cannot reach supabase.co, the relay is mocked in the harness.
- **Every AI request is tried twice (v201, H switched apps during "Checking pinyin and meaning …" and came back to "no connection (offline, or this provider refuses calls from a browser — try another provider)": Android cuts a page's requests when it goes to the background, and the text named a provider problem the user could do nothing about):** the three transports and the relay fetch through `aiFetch` — a request that fails is sent once more, after the page is back in the foreground when it went to the background meanwhile (`HIDDEN_AT` from `visibilitychange`, `whenVisible`), else after `AI_RETRY_MS` 1.5 s; the bar keeps moving meanwhile. A second failure is `AI_NET_ERR` "The AI could not be reached" everywhere — the Read preview adds ". Tap Ask AI to try again." and keeps the Ask AI button (`aiErrText`, which also turns a provider's lowercase answer into "The AI check failed: …"), the Edit form ". Tap the button to try again.", the picker and the Add form say it as before; the detail ("Failed to fetch (tried again after the app came back to the foreground)" / "(tried twice) — offline, or this provider refuses calls from a browser" / "— the API may be blocked without a VPN" for Claude) lives in the AI log only. Not yet field-checked.
- **A try that does not answer is dropped after 25 seconds (v331, H after the auto card's long reading: "he was reading quite long. why?" — described, "Go"):** `aiFetch` sends every try through `timedFetch`, an `AbortController` that aborts after `AI_TIMEOUT_MS` 25 s (a `let`, so the harness shortens it); the aborted try counts as a failure like a dead one — the v201 retry follows (after the return to the foreground when the app went to the background meanwhile, else after 1.5 s), and a second hang gives `AI_NET_ERR` with the Ask AI button as before; the AI log's detail reads "no connection: no answer within 25 s (tried twice) — the connection hangs, or the provider is slow" (`aiAsk`; the picker's and the picture's transports carry the same message without the suffix). Until v330 a hanging connection held the reading for as long as the browser waits, a minute or more, before the retry even started. What it costs: an answer that would have come after 25 s is thrown away and asked for again — Qwen's picture answers take 3–10 s on H's phone ("→ 200 in 10.1 s" in Diagnostics), so 25 leaves room; a relay that answers at 30 s costs a second call and then fails. Suite `verify-bgretry` (the timeout at 1.2 s: two hanging tries end in the sentence and the Ask AI button after about 4 s with the log's hang line; a first try that hangs and a second that answers fills the fields with two calls); the english, ai and picture suites pass. Not yet field-checked — the next reading whose AI call hangs is the check: the reader's result after half a minute instead of the bar standing.
- **Request:** OpenAI-style `POST {base}/chat/completions` with `Authorization: Bearer` (system + user message, temperature 0), or `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` for Claude (`anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access`). Payload per card: hanzi, pinyin, meaning, note, why (flagged / uncertain reading / pending), gloss, alt (the other readings, v96) — **never photos**. Reply = JSON array `[{c,zh,zht,p,m,note,ok,bad}]` (`zht` only for `script:"traditional"`). Cost ≈ 400 input + 100 output tokens per card, well under ¥0.01 at DeepSeek; a hundred cards a day ≈ ¥0.10–0.20.
- **Where it acts:** in the Read preview before saving (result shown in green, Save stores it verified); after saving as a suggestion stored `ai:{zh,p,m,note,ok,at,model}` with **Accept** (applies pinyin/meaning, fixes the text in place via `applyCardUpdate`, clears flag and `suspect`, `mt.src:"llm",verified:true`) or **Dismiss** — on the study back, in the card detail, under the photo, and via the **"N AI suggestions waiting — Accept all"** bar on the Cards tab; in the **Edit form** ("Ask AI to check text, pinyin and meaning" fills the fields in place, stored on Save). **Ask AI about N cards** in More sends the whole queue (`aiQueue()` = flagged + uncertain + pending) in one request; the auto run (`aiAuto`, `aiAutoSoon` 1.5 s after a save, and on `online`) does the same for pending/uncertain cards.

### Offline translation (T2, opt-in)
Firefox Translations `zh-Hans→en` v2.0a2 (Mozilla, MPL-2.0; model 44 MB + shortlist 4.7 MB + vocab 0.7 MB gzipped = 50 MB) in the Bergamot WASM engine (`vendor/nmt/translator-worker.js` + `bergamot-translator-worker.{js,wasm}`, npm `@browsermt/bergamot-translator` 0.4.9, no SharedArrayBuffer). Fetched by the **GitHub Action "Fetch zh→en translation model"** (workflow_dispatch) from **Mozilla Remote Settings** (the source Firefox uses; the Git LFS objects on GitHub are gone, 410; the build sandbox cannot reach Mozilla) — it writes `nmt-model.json` (sizes, sha256), bumps both version markers and pushes branch `nmt-model`; Actions may not open PRs here, so the PR is opened by hand. Enable under More → Translation (size prompt; files cached in `zt-ocr-v1`), setting `nmt`; used **only without a connection** once the AI is set up. The preview's translation is kept on the reading (`sg.nmt`, the lines it was made for) and Save reuses it for the same lines (v194, H: the Save button read "Translating …" — until v193 the model ran a second time at Save; the label stays for the rare case that the lines changed after the preview; a re-render of the preview no longer translates the same lines again either). Suite `verify-nmtsave` (a mocked model: one run in the preview, none at Save, the card carries the preview's meaning). `signMeaning(lines)` → `{m, src: phrasebook|nmt|gloss, pending}`; "Translate pending" in More completes gloss-only cards. Verified on the build machine (~40 ms per sentence after load), **not yet timed on the Xiaomi** — the More row shows "loaded in N s, last translation N s" (`NMT.loadMs`, `NMT.lastMs`) for that field test.

### Learning and the library
- **Learn:** SM-2 light; progress rows are `{c, interval, ease, due, reps, fails, last}` (`last` = day of the last review); every review day is appended to setting `days` (max 400) for the **streak**; `learnStats()` → cards learned / reviewed this week / streak, shown on the All-clear screen and in More → Progress — `fails` counts consecutive "again" (hard keeps it, good/easy reset it) and at `LEECH_FAILS` = 4 the card is **flagged automatically** ("failed N times in a row — check text, meaning and photo"): a leech is usually a bad card, not a bad memory. Front = photo (crop) above the text box, **both boxes the same shape on every card** (v223–v231, from H's two screenshots of a square 養樂多 beside a wide 嘉悦芭蕾: "Warum sind manche Hanzi felder quadratisch und andere rechteckig? Quadratisch nimmt zuviel vertikalen raum in anspruch. Bitte consistency!", then the design review that followed). **The card's picture is a 16:9 window around the text (v329, H: "Bitte analysiere alle bisherigen Fotos und sag mir, ob das 16:9 Format Sinn macht oder du einen besseren Vorschlag hast" — measured on the 21 real photos of the harness and this session: one-line signs and labels run 2.3–6.8:1, posters, plates and two-line signs 0.9–1.6:1, about half and half, almost nothing near 16:9 itself, so the tight crop filled the box's height or width only half and the rest was the blurred fill; a different ratio would move a tenth from one half to the other; described, "Go"):** `windowRect(rect)` takes the text frame (the layer rect, its angle) and widens it to `FRAME_RATIO` in the direction it lacks — a one-line sign gets the sign's surroundings above and below, a poster title the poster left and right —, never smaller than the frame, the same centre, shifted to stay inside the photo and clamped to the photo's size (an upright window; a turned one keeps its centre and `cropBlob` fills what lies outside the photo, v185); `windowCut(id,rect)` cuts it from the photo record, null when the photo is gone. Every save takes it: `saveSign` (the preview's Save card, from `CROP.rect`), `finishPending` (the placed frame or the saved rect, for the card made by itself and Save now), `saveNow`'s placeholder, the Edit form's Save changes (the hand-off's rect and the re-cropped frame, through the v247 window's coordinates as `photoFrame` does) and Image only from the inbox (`cropOk`); the reading's own cut (`sg.cardImg`) stays the fallback when the photo is gone (a card resumed from its crop alone). **The card's `frame` stays the text's frame** — Crop again starts from it, the AI's placement and the snap are untouched; only `img` is the window, so the text keeps its size and place in the box (it spans the same edge as before) and the surroundings fill the rest instead of the blur. Cards from before v329 keep their tight picture with the blurred fill until they are edited. What it costs: neighbouring text shows in the picture without being on the card (the pinyin under a street sign, the small line above a title). Measured in the harness: the synthetic poster's card 664×373 px for a frame of 664×125 (as wide as the frame, 16:9 tall), 邪不压正's turned frame 664×420 → the window 747×420 at −8°. The aiframe, autoframe and autocard suites compare the saved picture with `windowRect`'s width since (until v328 with the frame's); the savenow, recrop, english and picture suites pass. Not yet field-checked — the next card is the check: the box filled with the photo, the text as large as before. **A dark card picture gets its light back (v372, H's rice-cooker labels: "Some Cards really look bad because their part of the image was in the shade, etc. Can you enhance the visual quality of those cropped images?" — described in three lines, "Go for the brightening", then "Move the brightening button into the admin area. And make brightening a default process for all new Cards."):** **every card picture** goes through `cardJpeg` — the one boundary where a picture becomes a card's `img` (the finished card, Save now, Crop again's hand-off, the split panel's labels, Image only, the Add form's chosen picture; nine call sites that all encoded through `jpegOf` before) —, and there `brightenBlob` measures it and stretches it when it needs it. **Almost everything the reader and the AI see is untouched**: every reading cuts its own copy through `cropBlob`, which never brightens — with two exceptions found in v401 and not yet closed. `resumePending`'s third branch (`app.js:5050`, `opts={blob:d.img}` — a card with a pending reading whose photo is gone) and `picOnBad`'s Edit-form call (`app.js:2318`, `recropImg||d.img`) both hand the reader or the vision model the card's own **brightened and sharpened** picture. Measured at v401 on the real native-size crops through the real `cropSign`: of the seven treated, **three read differently and all three worse** — 绿皮书 from a correct 绿皮书 to 继反十｜月中日全国十, 保温取消 from 保湿｜取消 to 取消, 语翼中文 from 吃苦中文 to 还国语字二才了下｜?光加了入 — while the three untreated crops are byte-identical and read identically. The reader branch is narrow (`keepPhoto` normally leaves `fullPhoto(d)` set, so branch 2 is taken) and no card of H's is known to have been harmed, but the claim that the pipeline is insulated is false and no further brightening may be built on it. **The measure is the highlight end, not the median** (`brightLut`): the 1st and 99th percentile of the luminance (`BR_CLIP` 0.01, sampled at up to `BR_SAMPLE` 200 000 pixels), and a picture is left alone when its brightest pixels reach `BR_HI` 200 **and** its span is at least `BR_SPAN` 120. A straight stretch of that span to black and white follows — **no gamma**: a poster on a dark wall is not underexposed, and lifting its midtones would wash it out (the first cut used the median and a gamma, and 绿皮书, 流浪地球, the scooter badge and the Nongfu bottle all came out grey). The gain is capped (`BR_GAIN` 40, so at most 6×) and a span under `BR_MIN` 24 is noise and is left alone. **The stretch is per channel, which is a white balance (v375, H: "kannst du beim brightening noch einen Weissabgleich machen, damit alle bilder aus einem batch gleich aussehen?"):** the labels cut from one panel each carried their own share of the light's colour, so the seven rice-cooker cards came out in seven different tints — one cream, one grey, one yellow — though they are one photo. Each channel's own 1st and 99th percentile go to black and white, so whatever the light did to the picture is taken out and the sibling cards match by themselves; no batch, no shared measurement, each picture balanced on its own. It runs **only where the three channels are of a kind** — the widest span at most `BR_WB` 2.5 times the narrowest: a crop that is one colour through and through (red text on a red button, the green 绿皮书 cut with its spans 182/88/62) has no white in it to balance against, and stretching its empty channels would drain the colour, so it keeps the one luminance curve of v372. The gain cap is the luminance span's and the same factor goes on all three, or the cap would tilt the balance. Measured on the harness's real photos: all seven rice-cooker labels come out neutral and matching where they were cream, grey and yellow before; the green cut is byte for byte what v373 made of it; 流浪地球, the scooter badge, the Nongfu bottle, the parking sign, the street sign, the ARRI poster and the washing-machine panel are still left alone; a synthetic grey panel under a warm light ends at rgb ends **247/243/241 since v398** (255/252/249 until then — the shoulder maps the 99th percentile to `BR_KNEE` rather than to white) and red on red at 255/32/27 — the red kept. Not yet field-checked. **The top end rolls off instead of clipping (v396, H: "when brightening, avoid clipping highlights"):** the stretch mapped the 99th percentile straight to white, so the brightest hundredth — a lamp on a glossy panel, the glare on a bottle — came out as one flat sheet of 255 with its shape gone. The straight part of the curve ends at `BR_KNEE` 246 now and everything above it is compressed into the last nine levels, ending at the picture's own brightest pixel: the highlights still reach white but keep their order and their detail. Below the black end nothing changes — a card picture wants its dark ground dark. Measured on the curve: with the ends at 30 and 180 the inputs 180, 218 and 255 map to 246, 251 and 255, where before everything from 180 up was 255. It **settles within two passes** (v398, measured over 217 points, seven black points × every span the gate admits): a stretched picture usually measures as "leave alone" the next time, but a span of 24–32 needs a second pass on v395 and v398 alike, and v398 adds span exactly 32 to that set (246 × 32/40 = 197 falls under `BR_HI` 200 where 255 × 32/40 = 204 clears it). H's seven stretched crops run from span 63 to 144, and no path applies the curve twice to one picture. Measured on the harness's real photos: all seven rice-cooker labels come out readable (低卡饭 from a dark grey plate with darker characters to black on light grey, 保温/取消 the same), the green 绿皮书 cut and the tilted poster get a mild lift that only sharpens them (gain 2.1 and 2.4), and 流浪地球, the scooter badge 九号, the Nongfu bottle, the parking sign, the street sign, the ARRI poster, the whole washing-machine panel and all twenty of its label cuts are left exactly as they are — a black panel with white text has its highlights. **The white balance is tightened, and the deck is cut again (v398, H: "I'm really unsure about the brightening/image enhancement option … crops may look unnatural and not like the original image", then, after looking at 26 of his own crops rendered three ways: "Go with your recommendation and update all existing crops in my app"):** the evidence came first — 26 crops cut from H's own photos, each put through the app's real code untouched / as v397 makes it / as a proposal made it, published as a page he could tap through. **It showed the feature is far narrower than either of us thought: only 7 of 26 are brightened at all.** Every white-on-black appliance panel is already left alone, because the white strokes and lit icons carry the highlight. Of the seven that are lifted, exactly one is genuinely ugly — 绿皮书, a blue backlit lightbox that the per-channel stretch turns swamp-green with dirty cream characters — and the ugliness is the **white balance**, not the brightening. **So `BR_WB` is 2.5 → 1.5.** The channel-span ratios of the seven stretched crops are 1.026, 1.032, 1.042, 1.087, 1.138, 1.149 and **2.206**; the bar sits in an empty gap that the JPEG cut moves by at most 0.045. 绿皮书 loses the balance and comes back clean, and 语翼中文 keeps it, so the warm-light correction H preferred there survives — better than the panel-siblings-only scoping first proposed, which would have lost it. No crop gains or loses treatment; only which of the two curves it gets. **And the gate was still measuring the wrong quantity — the black points, not the spans (v418, H's 福 card, 2026-09-11, a pink paper-cut on a grey wall coming back as a red one on a green wall: "Oh no! Die Farbkorrektur ist hier ja schrecklich!!!!! Absolutes no go!!!"):** reproduced from his own two screenshots — the whole-photo view gives the input, the card gives the output — and the app's own `brightLut` run over that crop returns the wall as **(112,172,132)** where H's card shows (116,176,130), a match within four levels on every channel, and the field as red where the photo is pink. The cause is not the amount of correction but **which crops are allowed it**: the three channel spans on that crop are 122/145/114, a ratio of **1.272**, comfortably inside `BR_WB` 1.5 — while the three **black points** are 97/50/85, **47 levels apart**, because a saturated red object covers most of the frame and drags green's own 1st percentile far below red's. Mapping each channel to its own black point then *rotates the hue* instead of removing a cast, which is the opposite of a white balance. **The span ratio cannot be tuned out of this, and that is the measured point:** over the 105 real crops in the harness it puts the near 邪不压正 poster at 1.254 and this failure at 1.272 — 0.018 apart, no gap to put a bar in — while the **black-point spread** separates them with room: 1–14 on every panel label the white balance exists for (the rice cooker 3, the washer 2 and 14, the QR sign 8, the near poster 1), 22 on the parking sign, 26 on an inverted test image, and **47 here, 48 on the green lightbox cut**. `BR_LO` **30** sits in that gap, and both tests must now pass (`BR_WB` stays as the looser second guard). **Measured end to end, v417 against v418 over all 105 crops through the app's own code in the browser: 104 byte-identical, exactly one changes — H's 福, from the per-channel curve to the luminance one, wall (102,182,129) → (145,142,129) against the photo's (152,151,146).** So the fix reaches the failure and nothing else. **The deck is cut again, once more** (`RECUT_V` 2, the `recutPass` setting holding a version instead of a flag): a picture the v398 curve made has that white balance baked in and cannot be undone in place, so every eligible card is re-cut from its photo as at v398 — same guards, same drop-on-change rules, no undo, and a card without a frame or a photo keeps its look. **What this does not fix, and H should see it before it is changed:** even with the balance off, the luminance stretch still pushes this crop — its pink (189,152,176) comes out (236,144,198), more saturated than the photo — because the crop clears the "light and lively" bar on its highlight (200, exactly at `BR_HI`) but misses it on span (112 against `BR_SPAN` 120) by eight levels. Widening that bar would change which crops are treated across the whole deck, which is the v398 kind of decision, so it is reported rather than built. **And the pass says what it reached (v419, H: "Zeig mir den Zähler in den Diagnostics"):** the counts were thrown away when the pass ended, so nothing said how much of the deck it had touched — which is the one thing H needs while checking the new curve over many cards. `recutPass` stays the version number the gate reads and a second setting **`recutStat`** carries the result (`{v,at,deck,eligible,written,skipped,dropped}`), so the gate's logic is untouched. Diagnostics' settings line reads `re-cut` through **`recutLine()`** in five states: `not yet`; `v2 running, 84 of 248 cards cut so far` while it works; `v2 done 2026-09-11 · 241 of 266 cards cut again · 7 could not be cut · 1 changed while the pass ran · 18 without a frame or photo, never tried` when it is over (each clause only when it is not zero); and `v1 done, no count kept` for a phone whose last pass predates this. **The last clause is the one that matters:** a card with no stored `frame` (anything from before v244), a card whose photo is gone, and a card whose fresh cut does not match what is stored are never re-cut and never will be — they keep their old picture for good, and until now that group was invisible. Owner's, English, no key in any language. **And the check of it found that the brightening suite had been testing a frozen build since v398:** `DC-verify-bright` serves `…/v398/settle/shadow`, a copy of the repo at v398, so it could not see any change after it — it passed on v417, v418 and v419 alike **without ever running them**, which is the v384 trap one level out (the harness green on data the build never produced) and it was reported to H as verification before it was caught. Pointed at the live repo it needed the v415 reload patch as well, being the ninth suite to reload from a tab and expect Learn; it then passes on v419 with every v398 assertion intact and drives the whole re-cut path end to end — seeded deck of 21, 15 eligible, 12 written, 2 that could not be cut, 1 taken out from under the pass, 6 never tried, and the line reading all four clauses. **The rule: a suite that freezes a copy of the build under test stops being a test the moment the build moves; if a shadow root is needed for one measurement, it does not get to stand in for the suite.** The swipe, english, diag and numsring suites pass. **`SH_AMOUNT` is 0.8 → 0.4** (halo energy down 56–65 %, about half the legibility gain kept; the band 1.06–1.14 is asserted in the suite so a rise back to 0.8 fails rather than passes). **A proposal that was measured and dropped:** triggering on legibility (Otsu ink-vs-ground separation) instead of on brightness. On a poster whose ground is a gradient the measurement splits the gradient, not the ink, so it fired on H's ARRI poster — separation 44.5 — and made a soft pale-blue poster neon. It would have cost ARRI to win back 等候区. Do not bring it back without a test for a non-flat ground. **The deck is cut again, once (`recutPass`, setting `recutPass`, its own — `brightPass` is untouched; it runs after the brightening pass, never beside it):** the pictures already on the phone were made by the old curve, and that cannot be undone in place — an old white balance is baked into the stored crop and the unsharp mask is not idempotent, so running the new curve over a stored crop would double-sharpen and keep the cast. So each eligible card is **cut again from its photo at the same rectangle** and treated fresh. **Which rectangle is decided by measurement, not by a field**: an ordinary card's picture is the 16:9 window around the text frame (v329), a split-panel label's is the label's own frame at the photo's pixels (v362), and nothing on the card says which — so both cuts are computed and the one whose size matches the stored picture is taken. **Every doubt resolves to skip.** A card qualifies only with a picture, a stored `frame`, a photo still on the phone (`fullPhoto`), no waiting `reading`, four finite in-range frame numbers, a size match within 2 px or 1 %, and a fresh cut correlating at least `RC_CORR` 0.8 with the picture the card has (`greyThumb`/`corrOf`, a normalised correlation a change of brightness does not move; measured over 120 real frames: min 0.9215, 5th percentile 0.997, against 0.28–0.59 for a cut moved a quarter of its width — the bar sits in the gap). **What three skeptics found and what fixed it:** a cut sat in the write queue for a median 439 ms and up to 1.2 s, so a card H re-cropped meanwhile got the **stale region** written over it (measured: correlation 0.0068 between the card's final picture and its own frame), Remove image was undone, and `corrOf` returned 1 for a flat picture — turning the last guard inside out. Each queued row now carries the card state it was cut from and is **dropped, not forced**, if the card moved on; a flat new picture is rejected; the frame is validated before anything is cut; and a card still waiting for its reading is skipped (`recutCard` returns a blob for every eligible card, unlike `brightenBlob`, so without that guard a Save-now card was written with its pre-placement cut on its post-placement frame — reproduced 6/6). **What it costs, and the entry must say so rather than read as pure benefit:** every card picture the app now makes has a little **less ink/ground separation** — measured down on all 19 of the 26 crops the app changes, by 0.5 % to 8.3 %, and up on none. That is the price of the smaller halo and the rolled-off highlight; invisible at native size on the ones rendered, but real and uniform. The unsharp mask still puts clipped pixels back after the curve has rolled the highlight off (1.16 % → 4.24 % on the dishwasher's 加速), so the curve no longer clips and the finished picture still does a little — though less than v397's on every one of the 19. 绿皮书 is the one crop that changes character rather than degree: the single luminance curve makes its blue about twice as saturated as the photo's. **There is no undo**, as with the v373 pass, and **a partly re-cut deck is the expected outcome**: a card from before v244 with no `frame`, a card whose photo is gone, a card cut in the Edit form's window — all keep their old look forever. About 95 ms a card, 18.6 s for 189, spread out and interruptible. Suite `verify-bright` (the knee bar `pctWhite<=10`, measured 4.8 % against 65.8 % on v397; the sharpening band; five v398 probes — the eligible card re-cut with memory and IndexedDB agreeing, a size-mismatched frame untouched, a broken frame untouched, a card waiting for its reading untouched and still carrying `reading`, a photo-less card untouched, and the race, where a card taken out from under a queued cut keeps the user's picture); the english, cards, reload, savenow, panel and autocard suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's deck after one start is the check. **The pictures already on the phone are done by the app itself, once (v373, H: "Run the brightening over my deck now and remove the manual option completely. I thought i have to run it from the app and wanted to remove it afterwards."):** the deck lives in the phone's IndexedDB, so nobody can run it from outside — `brightenPass` starts 2.5 s after boot beside the other resumed work, walks the deck, measures every card picture and writes back the ones that were dark or flat, in chunks of `BR_BATCH` 10 (`idbPutMany`, each row rebuilt from the card **as it stands at the write**, so an edit meanwhile is not overwritten), dropping each list thumbnail; the Cards or Learn screen is drawn again at the end when anything changed. **No row, no button, no question, nothing to see.** It waits while a photo is being framed or read (`reloadBusy`, `READING`) and breathes `BR_PAUSE` 60 ms between cards, so a deck of 167 takes about half a minute of wall time and none of it is felt; the idle reload of v327 waits for it. The setting `brightPass` is written **only when the pass has been through the whole deck**, and the curve is idempotent, so an interrupted or failed pass simply runs again at the next start and re-measures what it already did. It runs on every phone, once. The owner's row of v372 — “Card pictures” with its button and its question — is gone with it; do not bring a manual button back unasked. What it costs: a decode per card picture at the first start after the update (a few milliseconds each, spread out), and one JPEG generation on each picture that is brightened. There is no undo — the pass is the app's own decision, as the line-break repair of v338 is. What it costs: a decode and a measurement per card picture at save (a few milliseconds; a picture that needs nothing is not re-encoded at all), and one more JPEG generation on a picture that is brightened. **And the picture is sharpened at the cut (v378, H's "Go" on the offer after "Any other image improvements you suggest?"):** a photo is stored at 1 600 px, so one rice-cooker label is 184 px wide in it while the card shows it at about 322 CSS pixels — two to three times its own size on the phone —, and that softness is in the pixels, where the brightening cannot reach. An unsharp mask puts the edge back (`sharpen`): the picture blurred with `SH_PASS` two 1-2-1 passes (a radius of about one pixel), the difference added back at `SH_AMOUNT` 0.8, and a difference under `SH_MIN` 3 left alone — that is the JPEG's own grain, and a panel's flat surface must not become crunchy. It runs **only on a picture under `SH_W` 800 px wide**, one the card enlarges; a big crop already has more pixels than the box and is left as it is. The stretch runs first and the sharpening after it, so the threshold reads the picture as the card will show it. Measured on the rice-cooker labels enlarged three times: 0.8 is the last amount without a light halo around the strokes (1.4 haloes and lifts the grain), and two blur passes read far better than one, since the softness spans three or four pixels; the 773 px 绿皮书 cut at its own size comes out a touch crisper with no halo, and the whole photos over 800 px are untouched. What it costs: 9–17 ms on a label cut, 42 ms on a poster cut. **It is not idempotent** — sharpening twice is visible —, so it happens only where a picture is cut fresh from the photo (`cardJpeg`, `brightenBlob(blob,true)`), never in the deck pass of v373 (`brightenBlob(d.img)`, no flag): the cards already on the phone keep their look until they are cut again. Not yet field-checked. Suite `verify-bright` (`brightLut` on three synthetic pictures — the shade stretched, a lively one and a poster on a dark wall left alone; the white balance on a warm-lit grey panel and on red on red; the unsharp mask raising a soft picture's edge energy by a fifth, a 900 px one left alone, and the cut's path sharper than the deck pass's on the same blob; no row and no button anywhere, unlocked and on More; the pass running by itself at the next start with no sheet and nothing on screen, one of three cards brightened and the other two's bytes unchanged; the stretched picture across a reload and no second pass; a card saved through the Add form carrying a brightened picture); the english, admin, savenow, autocard, cards, reload and order suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's next photo in the shade is the check, and one run over the deck for the cards that are already there. **A library for the brightening, and why the arithmetic went in instead of one (v401, H: "Bezueglich brightening und allgemeine Bildoptimierung: gibts da vielleicht eine oeffentliche library, die wir nuetzen koennen?"):** thirteen packages were downloaded from npm and run in the harness, not read about — OpenCV.js in four builds, wasm-vips, Photon, image-js, jimp, sharp, two OpenCV subsets, and three smaller ones. **The answer is no, and the reason is not the mirror's cap:** `@techstark/opencv-js` 4.5.3-release.3 is 8,054,069 bytes (2.61 MB gzipped, Apache-2.0, no NOTICE file to propagate) and would fit, but it costs **3.6 s of the phone's CPU on every load** — measured over four fresh loads at 4× throttle from the phone's own cache, with no speed-up between them, because the wasm is 7.47 MB of base64 inside the JS and Chrome never code-caches it; and that embedding is exactly what makes the file loadable from a blob URL, which v335 requires of every vendor script, so the two constraints cannot both be met. At the cadence of these days — 39, 35 and 29 shipped versions on three consecutive days, each a forced v327 reload — that is about two minutes of H's phone a day. Beside it: +76 to +89 MB resident (measured per process tree, not the 128 MB `HEAPU8` length) next to up to four Tesseract workers, and a friend's first-card download from 4.69 to 7.17 MB. **And it would buy nothing.** The app's own `otsuThr` is already bit-identical to `cv.threshold(…OTSU)` on all 26 of H's crops; a hand-written `adaptiveThreshold` agrees with OpenCV's on 94.4–99.95 % of pixels and a hand-written CLAHE to 0.28–4.0 grey levels of 255; whole `snapBox` with `cv.connectedComponentsWithStats` doing the labelling is **0.87× — slower** (the labelling core is 3.36× faster and the JS↔WASM copy eats it), the deskew 0.56×, the brightening histogram 0.27×, and only the unsharp mask is faster at 1.32×. On H's washing machine the entire replaceable pixel-JS is 2.21 s of a 33.1 s reading against 71.9 s of pooled Tesseract the library cannot touch, and the biggest apparent target — `toBW` at 6783 ms over 544 calls — is 6203 ms of `canvas.toBlob`, the JPEG the reader has demanded since v73. **The algorithms were then written and measured on their own, and they lose too.** CLAHE on the card picture is better on **0** of the seven crops the curve stretches, the same on three and worse on four (ground grain +19 %), and ungated it moves all 19 left-alone crops, *lowers* ink/ground separation on five appliance panels — now the commonest card since v357 — and re-creates the v398 ARRI failure as tile mottling in the blue gradient; the reason is that these crops do not have uneven light but insufficient light, and the illumination-field range of the seven is 37–79 while 等候区, the one card the build really fails, has the **smallest of all 26 at 26.2**. Sauvola as an extra reader copy takes exact reads from 12/26 to 11/26 and turns ⑥烤鱼 into 加吉鱼; as a fourth `snapBox` candidate the v347-style guard blocks it on all six real failure fixtures while it moves 流浪地球 by 0.6 points; replacing `snapBox`'s global Otsu outright breaks nine aiframe checks including 邪不压正 near and far, the lamp photo and the tilted 绿皮书, because the component count goes 74 → 320 and every selection rule since v287 was tuned against the current population. Only in `readLabels` does it pay, and invisibly: the washer's labels named *by reading* go 16 → 18 while placed stays 18 of 19 and wrong stays 0, for 50 % more reader passes. **What did work is in no library**: `groundTexture`, twenty-two lines asking whether the ground the characters stand on is speckled or smooth, which lets 等候区 — worn yellow paint on granite, span 138 and highlight 213, both clear of the bars — through the "light and lively" gate and lifts its separation 50.2 → 84.8. It is **not merged**: measured with genuine downscaling, seven of the twenty-five other crops cross `BR_TEX` 0.04 (wash-wazi 0.0283 → 0.0569 at half size, robust across three resampling filters), and a wrongly stretched panel label is worse than a dim 等候区. It needs a scale term first, and then it is H's call, since the stretched stone is more legible and less natural and that is the word he used at v398. **Measured and dropped, do not attempt again without the named test:** wasm-vips (needs `SharedArrayBuffer` and COOP/COEP, which GitHub Pages cannot set — measured hanging 40 s); image-js (391 KB, MIT, and all fifteen of its thresholds are global where every failure since v306 demands a local one); Photon (2 MB of Instagram filters); the paddle and onfido OpenCV subsets (1.3–7.3 MB exposing one to six functions, none of them CLAHE, adaptiveThreshold or connectedComponents); a custom OpenCV build (needs emsdk, still ~128 MB of heap, and an unauditable binary in a public repo); bgustreadimg-wasm (BUSL-1.1); a polynomial background model (fits the content, not the light — wash-wendu 183.8 → 140.3); SWT for the plate rule and MSER for the fused mat (both implemented: the plate's outline stroke ratio overlaps the characters', and none of MSER's 251 candidates is stable). **One rule falls out of the delivery measurements and should be kept whatever is vendored later:** `OCR_FILES` is overloaded as both "what the reader needs" and "what to pre-download", and `warmReader` sets `READER_WARMED` before its `ocrCached()<OCR_FILES.length` check, so a single non-reader entry silently kills the v290 Camera-tab warm-up for every existing user until the new file arrives — measured against a control, worker "made" → "NOT made" — while `app.js:6015` still hardcodes "(14 MB, once)". **Nothing is field-checked here because nothing shipped**; what needs H is whether 等候区 bothers him at all, and whether the brighter stone reads as better or as unnatural.
