Roughly 3 MB for 70 crops, 15–30 MB with the whole photos; WeChat takes files up to 100 MB. Field-confirmed (H's 70 cards, 19.5 MB through WeChat, the photos on the other phone: "OK works"). **An older app imports such a file without a word and without the photos** — the first try landed on a phone still at v165; the receiving app must be at v166 or later (More → About), then the same file imported again restores them. Since v167 the import ends with one sentence on what it did — "Imported 70 cards and 53 progress entries, 68 with photos.", "(N could not be read)" when a photo failed to decode, "The file carries no photos; the photos on this phone were kept." for a text-only file — so a silent loss cannot happen again. The Export row shows **"Last export: N days ago"** (setting `lastExport`), red after 30 days or when never exported — the cards exist only on this phone. **Photos** row: inbox count, and a **Delete N** button for photos older than 30 days that already became a card (cards carry `shot:<inbox id>`; the cards keep their crop, and the whole photo is copied onto them just before the deletion — v214, `keepPhoto`). **Reset** wipes cards, progress and photos. **Diagnostics** (v93, H: "crop draws, nothing happens afterwards" could not be reproduced in Chromium — the phone has to tell): the last 20 uncaught errors and unhandled rejections (`ERRLOG`, `logErr`, persisted in setting `errlog`), the steps of the last reading with their times (`READLOG`) and its competing passes (`LAST_READ.passes`), the last three **drawings** (`DRAWLOG`, v140 — the strokes as drawn, rounded to pixels of the 720 px pad, and what the model answered; H: "I feel no improvement" after v139, and the synthetic strokes of the harness are not a finger — the phone's own strokes are the only field data), the last three **AI exchanges** — request payload and raw reply, never the key (`AILOG`, `logAi`, v97: the phone is the only place DeepSeek can be watched from; it once returned the Chinese text as the meaning and waved 二和玖 through) —, plus page/script version, online state, AI provider (never the key; since v267 with "(text deepseek)" when the text goes elsewhere than the active provider), service-worker presence and user agent — **the reading log keeps its steps since v285** (H's diagnostics of the SF Express card, 2026-09-07: forty lines of "recognizing … 61%" and nothing else — the reader's progress lines had pushed every step and the proposed-frame line out of the 40-entry log, and `cropSign` had wiped the proposal line at the reading's start anyway): a progress line now overwrites the previous progress line (`readingStatus`), and the frame's own lines — "frame proposed by the app: …" and "the old crop found in the photo …", marked `pre` — stay at the head of the new reading's log; the diag suite expects the proposal first, "cutting out the frame …" second and no two progress lines in a row; the autoframe, twopass, recrop and english suites pass — **the last reading's steps and passes survive a restart since v267** (setting `readlog`, written by `saveReadLog` 0.8 s after each step and after the competition, restored at boot into `READLOG`/`LAST_READ` — H's first diagnostics after the v266 update said "Last reading (0 steps)": the update's reload had emptied the in-memory log; the diag suite reloads and finds the steps) — **The AI exchanges survive a restart too since v384** (H's washing machine, 2026-09-09, after five versions tuned against his answer rebuilt from the reading log: "We are trying the same thing again and again, and it doesn't seem to work." — right, and the reason was in his own diagnostics, which said `AI exchanges (0, newest last):` twelve minutes after the reading. `AILOG` lived in memory alone, so the v327 idle reload, an update, or simply reopening the app wiped the model's raw answer between the photo and the sharing; the reading log has been persisted since v267 and the error log since v93, and only this one was not. Every version since v379 was therefore fitted to the box numbers as the reading log prints them — **rounded to whole percent**, which on a label box about 7.5 % wide is a tenth of a box on each edge, wider than the `LB_TMPL` tolerance the drawing test measures — so the harness passed and the phone failed each time, on data that was never the phone's. Now `logAi` writes setting `ailog` 0.8 s after each entry (`saveAiLog`, the reading log's own debounce) and boot restores it, so Qwen's own JSON with its own box numbers reaches the next session. Device only: the daily usage row carries `reportErrors()` and never this, and the picture entry has carried `[picture 800×442 JPEG, 24 KB]` in place of the base64 since v173. **The rule it stands for: when the harness and the phone disagree, the harness is wrong and that is what gets fixed first — no heuristic is tuned against numbers the phone did not actually send.** **And the whole answer is kept, not its first 1500 characters (v395, H's washing machine at v394 — 25 labels, 15 of them placed by the reader and none on a neighbour's button, and the answer that made them could not be rebuilt): `logAi` cut every reply at 1500 characters, which a panel's answer passes inside its third label, so the log showed 混合, 快速, 单脱水 and then stopped mid-word. The same fault as v384 one level down — the log persists but says too little — and it blocks every further fix, since the harness can only be fitted to the raw answer. `AI_LOG_RES` is 6000 characters now (about forty labels); three entries in the setting are some 18 KB, and the picture entry still carries `[picture 800×442 JPEG, 24 KB]` in place of the base64. The panel suite reads `AILOG` after the washer case and parses its twenty labels back out of it.** Suite `verify-diag` (an exchange logged with a raw reply, a reload, the reply still in `AILOG` and in `diagText()` with its box numbers, and absent from `reportData()`); the english, ai and picture suites pass.) **The reading's own numbers, beside its sentences (v399, H, 2026-09-10: "Fehlt dir denn noch irgendwas in diagnostics? … Ich werde dann in Zukunft einfach lauter Bilder knipsen und Karten generieren und dir Screenshots von den Karten schicken, von denen ich denke, dass da was nicht korrekt ist. Plus die Diagnostiks."):** every line of the reading log rounds what it prints to whole percent, and on a label box 7.5 % of the picture wide a whole percent is a tenth of a box on each edge — wider than the tenth `templateBoxes` tolerates and 25 times the 0.3 px `roundGrid` needs. **v379, v380, v381, v382 and v383 were five versions fitted to those rounded numbers**, every one green in the harness and wrong on the phone; v384 found the AI log empty, v395 found the reply cut at 1500 characters, v390's row band is still my own reconstruction, v393 had to rebuild the rice cooker from a screenshot, v396's `picW` "cannot be exercised here", and v386 and v398 needed H's own photo and his own verbatim answer. The same defect each time: **the phone recorded a sentence where the harness needed a number, or recorded nothing at all.** So every value the frame chain decides on is written down as the code uses it (`NUMS`, restored at boot with the steps like v267/v384, printed by `diagText()` as one `numbers:` line): the photo's and the layer's own pixels, the ink rows' rectangle, the straightening angle unrounded, `Hink`, `frameH`, `maxLines`, `effScore` and whether it fell under `WEAK_READ`, the quick look's and the winning pass's **per-character** confidences and boxes (`textLike` wants three boxes at `SURE_BOX` averaging `PLACE_CF`, which a rounded mean can never show), the picture answer as the code reads it — `picW`/`picH`, the box, its pixel reading, every label's box at **four decimals** with its scale, the dropped fine print and its boxes —, a fingerprint of `picSystem()` (5 656 characters, changed at v361, v363, v367 and v377, and no answer has ever named the words that asked it), the snap's box, its blob count, its `beyond` bands **and `null` when it found nothing** (H's ARRI poster: `snapBox` returns null and `cropSign`'s `if(snap)` has no `else` — measured, **5 of 40** AI-box readings said nothing at all), the drawing test's own inputs, the run search's bands and runs with each label's rectangle and the run that named it, every `frameOnText` call with what it was given and what it gave back **including its refusals** (v346 tripped over the silent "nothing to move"), the window and the card's frame, and the cards the reading made. **One record per reading, keyed by the photo, filed by `numsFile`** — a single global was measured to fail on H's own workflow: photo B taken while A's picture call was out left A's eleven cards with no record and B's record carrying A's eleven labels. Diagnostics' head line gains the cores, the memory, the readers actually started, how full the storage is (`setSetting` swallows every write error, so a phone at its quota stops persisting and says nothing — the v384 mode with no signal) and the settings that change how a photo is read; **every card made from now on carries `v`, the build that made it.** Measured: an ordinary sign 1 927 bytes, H's 19-label washing machine 6 082 (about 190 a label, so `SPLIT_MAX` 30 fits whole and `NUMS_MAX` never fires), the diagnostics text 6 829 → 8 980 and 10 956 → 17 262; the write 0.8 ms at the median and 5.6 at the worst on a four-core desktop. And it is **checkable, not merely stored**: the placement arithmetic is `frameGeom` now, so a fresh browser given only the diagnostics text lands on the sign's frame to the pixel (0.0–0.1 photo px of 1328×1000) and on all **19 of 19** of the panel's. What it costs: 2–6 KB of diagnostics, a longer paste, and nothing the learner sees — no row, no control, no key in any language (Diagnostics is the owner's, English). What it cannot do: replay the pixels. `snapBox`, `readLabels`, `textRegion`, `deskewBlob` and the reader are recorded by their **outputs**, so a wrong snap replays as the same wrong snap — v386's lesson stands, and the record names the `shot` and the cards so the right photo can be asked for. **Deliberately not built:** a suspect list from the app's own confidence — measured, `sg.weak` fires on 11 of 16 real readings while **6 of its 7** on the regression photos are correct and the one known-wrong text is called strong, `mt.suspect` fires **0 of 65**, and a card built from a picture answer is `verified:true` whatever the crop shows, which is why all nineteen washing-machine cards read clean. **Rejected and not merged (do not bring back unasked):** the one-tap "Send this card's story" bundle as built — its picture was written to IndexedDB by `setSetting` (structured clone keeps a Blob), **121 279 bytes** per picture reading of H's own photo, surviving the inbox's Delete, its cards' deletion and "Start over → Delete everything", on a friend's phone too with no row and no switch; and its record kept the *first* answer of a re-asked reading while re-cutting the *second* call's picture. The bundle's idea — one tap sends a card's whole story with the picture the AI saw and, for the reader path, the frame at its own pixels (2 of 19 frames reproduce without it, 19 of 19 with it) — is worth building once the picture is never stored, and it is a control the user can see, so it waits for H's "Go". Not yet field-checked — H's next photo is the check: does Diagnostics carry a `numbers:` line, and can the next fix be built from it without asking for the photo? **Three readings in the shared text, not one (v405, H on the same diagnostics that carried the rice cooker: "Why doesn't the washing machine work?"):** the answer was in that dump and it was not a placement failure at all — **Qwen answered three labels, 左筒 / 右筒 / 下筒, "the three drums of a triple-drum washing machine", for a panel that carries about twenty-five**, and every mechanism downstream did its job on the three it was given. The picture held the panel (the reader's garbage carries 剂量用 from 柔顺剂 and 全金和羽 from 羽绒, which the dial does not); the model's box `[230,100,650,540]` is 38 % of the picture and dead centre, so the v393 re-ask correctly did not fire — it wants under `PIC_SMALL` and against an edge, and a big confident box that is simply wrong about scope looks nothing like a tiny one at the border; `roundGrid` correctly called the three round-pixel boxes a drawing (all three labels are two characters, so v381's width rule cannot fire). Three cards, no buttons. **What made that diagnosis nearly impossible is what this version fixes.** `NUMSOF` holds `NUMS_LIVE` six records, but `numsFile` promoted exactly one into `LAST_READ.nums`, and that one is what `diagText` prints and `saveReadLog` persists — so a session of three photos kept the **last** photo's numbers and threw the other two away; the washer's record existed a minute before H shared and the rice cooker had overwritten it. That defeats H's own way of working ("Ich werde dann in Zukunft einfach lauter Bilder knipsen und Karten generieren und dir Screenshots von den Karten schicken, von denen ich denke, dass da was nicht korrekt ist. Plus die Diagnostiks"), since the card that came out wrong is almost never from the last photo taken — the same shape as v384 (`AILOG` in memory alone) and v395 (the reply cut at 1500 characters), one level up. `LAST_READ.ring` keeps the last `NUMS_KEEP` **three** filed records, **by identity**: one reading files twice, at the end of `cropSign` and again once `splitCards` has named its cards, and both times it is the same object, which the ring then updates in place rather than taking a second slot. Diagnostics prints the newest as the `numbers:` line it always did and the other two under **"Earlier readings (2, newest last)"**, each with its shot id and card count so a screenshot of a wrong card can be matched to a record; the setting carries the ring (`numsRing`), the newest at `NUMS_MAX` 12 000 characters and the older two at `NUMS_OLD` 6 000 — a 19-label panel measures 6.1 KB whole, so an older panel survives intact and the whole text costs at most 12 KB more. A phone still holding a v404 setting has its one record under `nums` and is read back as a ring of one. Measured in the harness: three readings filed give three `numbers:` lines and the head, a re-file takes no second slot, a fourth photo pushes the oldest out, all three survive a reload, the v404 setting migrates, and three worst-case records make a 20.5 KB diagnostics text with the older two trimmed. Suite `verify-numsring`; the diag, english, panel and savenow suites pass. **What it does not do:** say why the model read three labels of twenty-five. The one input the app controls is the reader's guesses, and four of the washer's six contain 下筒 or 下简 — the only real word in all that garbage — while the rice cooker's six guesses 22 seconds later held no real word at all and it listed twelve labels; whether those guesses anchored the model cannot be tested here, since the sandbox cannot reach Qwen. Not yet field-checked — H's next session of several photos is the check: does the diagnostics carry the wrong card's own numbers, and not only the last photo's? **Measured and dropped, do not attempt again without the named test:** nothing — the alternative considered was one record per photo with no cap, which puts an unbounded paste in front of H.

**The app asks whether the picture agrees with what the model said it saw (v400, H, 2026-09-10: "Du würdest eine falsch gecroppte Karte doch selber erkennen, wenn Du den Crop noch mal prüfen würdest. Also ich meine die App."):** his 长安铃木 badge had the right text, pinyin and meaning under a picture of bare red paint, and **nothing in the app noticed** — no weak reading, no bad verdict, no refused split; `readingCard` sets no doubt for `mt.src=="llm"`, so a card built from a picture answer is `verified:true` whatever the crop shows. Four ways to see it were built and scored on a labelled corpus of 57 good, 21 borderline and 98 bad card pictures cut from H's own photos, and **three were broken by the skeptics**. Now `cropDisagrees` asks one question at save time (`finishPending` for a single card, `splitCards` for each label of a panel): does the card's own frame lie outside **everything** the answer named? `PICSEEN[id]` keeps the picture the AI read and the frame it was cut from — set after the v314/v318/v348 re-ask has settled `picSeen`, or a check would map the second answer's boxes through the first proposal —, every box of the answer is mapped onto the photo by `photoFrameOf`, and the frame must clear their union by more than `AGREE_GAP` 0.15 of the union's own width or height. **Not label by label**: measured on H's washing machine, a *correct* card overlaps its own label box at IoU 0.00–0.31 and 8 of 20 not at all — the model draws a lattice and drifts it (v380), boxes the buttons instead of the labels (v359), or reads its bright block and guesses its dim one (v385) —, so a per-label check fires on most correct cards; per-label drift moves boxes *inside* the union and does not move the union, so v385's error shape costs nothing (0 false alarms with the dim block displaced by three label widths). **The action is the review flag, not a new picture**: "the picture may not show this text — check the photo" in six languages, and Crop again fixes it in one tap. The wide-frame fallback was measured and rejected — it is v380, the picture H turned down in the field at v382 ("Die Bild crops sind noch falsch"), usable in **0 of 75** cases (6.1 CSS px a character against 69.1 for a good card), and on a neighbour's crop widening does not remove the neighbour, it adds the right label beside the wrong one. Measured: **0 false alarms on 54 good, 21 borderline and 13 adversarially built correct crops** — 0 of 88 —, the worst correct card at 0.027 (H's rice cooker, whose answer boxes the buttons a label-height below the characters, v359) against the lowest bad at 0.166, a 5.5× margin; 14 of 94 bad crops caught, among them two cards of H's own v398 dishwasher run that came out as bare chrome trim and that nothing noticed; 0.075 ms a card. Nothing fires on the honest whole-frame fallback of v380/v392 — 0 of 21 — which matters, since that is the picture such a card already has. **What it cannot see:** a neighbour's label (0 of 35 — the neighbour is inside the union) and a sliced character (0 of 32, even at 75 % of a label's width), so H still spots those; and it abstains entirely when the reading was strong enough that no picture went to the AI, about two cards in five. `null` is "cannot say", never agreement. **Measured and not merged (do not bring back unasked):** the ink test — no threshold catches the badge (0.032) without condemning H's own 拉 door plate (0.022), and its stroke-run window is empty whenever the character height is under 2.5, so the vertical escalator sign scores exactly 0; reading the crop back with the reader — 40 % of *correct* crops go unconfirmed and it costs 24.4 s on a 20-card panel, sound only as a confirmer (0 of 98 wrongly confirmed), never as a detector; the free bookkeeping — 53 of 53 (photo, text) groups give a correct crop and its displaced twin identical state, a measured ceiling of 6 of 98 at zero false alarms; a per-label agreement check; re-asking the AI (v382–v385 measured that: three calls, 132 s, a worse answer); and a silent picture change of any kind. Suites: autocard, panel, aiframe, savenow, picture, badpic, kind and english pass. **The 长安铃木 entry of the corpus is a reconstruction from H's screenshots, not the phone's bytes, and was excluded from the threshold** (the v384 rule); signal D fires on it at 0.333 and stays silent on the correct window at 0.000, which is illustrative only. Not yet field-checked — the badge taken again on v400 is the check, and v399's record now carries `seenBase`, `seen`, `seenAng` and `pic`, which is exactly the state this reads. **Show** expands the text in place (`.diag`), **Share** sends it as a `.txt` via the share sheet (`shareDiag`; a third share-sheet dance on purpose, the two others keep their own texts), and **Copy** puts the same text on the clipboard (v292, H: "offer the option to share/copy diagnostics and user data and feedback directly from the app" — so it can be pasted straight into a chat): `copyText(text,st)` through `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, the row's line says "Copied.", or "Copy is not available here — tap Show and select the text." when the clipboard refuses; the same button on **All users** (`#users-copy`, the cached rows, else one fetch) and the owner's **Feedback** (`#fb-copy`); the three rows carry Show, Share and Copy under their text (`.fieldacts`, as the Progress row) since a third button beside the sentence squeezed it. Suites diag (the copied text equals `diagText()`, the line, the three buttons, the refusal's sentence), users and feedback (the copied text equals the shown report, no second fetch) pass; the rows checked by screenshot. Not yet field-checked.

**What the app claims it can read, and what a photo has confirmed — in the app, not in this file (v434, H after the untested menu board of v433: "OK, diese liste bitte unter admin anlegen"):** the offer had been a block here; H put it **under Advanced settings instead, and that is the better place** — the list is a checklist he carries out of the door, and a paragraph in a repo file is no use on the street. More → Diagnostics → **Field tests** with Show and Copy (`fieldText`, `fieldKinds`, `fieldNote`; owner's, English, no key in any language, hidden when locked). **Two halves, and the split is the whole point.** The first is **counted from the phone's own deck** and cannot go stale: one line per `KINDS` entry with the cards carrying that tag and how many of their photos produced more than one card (a split), plus the untagged rest — a kind at 0 is a kind this phone has never made. It matches **every language's** word for a kind (`L10N[col]["kind:"+k]` over all ten columns), since a language switch leaves the old tags as they are (v364) — measured: an `Appliance` deck with one card tagged the German `Gerät` counts 4, not 3. The second half is **`picSystem()`'s own promise list, which no tag can measure** — a timetable and a shelf of price labels are both `apart` cases that end up tagged Transport or Product, so the deck cannot say whether either was ever photographed — in three groups: **confirmed by a photo** (poster, shop sign, product label, door plate, sticker, appliance panel), **tried, the fix after it unconfirmed** (street sign, car badge, carton and calligraphy, vending machine, phone app screen, and the menu board's one failed try), and **never tried** — twelve cases, the list to work through: dish list, shelf of price labels, wall of notices, building directory, bus stop board, row of shopfronts, care label, package headings, form or receipt, timetable or price list, remote/keypad/lift panel, ticket machine/cash machine. **That half is kept by hand in `app.js` against this file's field-confirmed record**, and a case moves up only when H says on the phone that it works. **Why it exists:** at v433 the empty deck advertised menu boards that no photo had ever read, and only H's own memory caught it — the app now carries the answer where it is checked rather than in a file only I read. Measured: the row's line "7 of 9 kinds never made on this phone, 12 cases never photographed at all", the report's widest line **45 columns** against the `.diag` box's 46 at 390 px (the v250 rule) with **0 lines over**, no box overflow, Show toggling both ways, the row absent when locked, and no page error but the harness's own service-worker line. **No `WHATS_NEW` line** — an owner's row a learner never sees. The english, admin, order and kind suites pass; the diag suite's `copied.same` failed once and passed on the re-run, the known v432 flake. Checked by screenshot in light and dark. **And the row is the general list, not only the photo cases (v435, H: "Bitte allgemeine „noch zu testen“ Liste"):** v434 was too narrow — he wants everything built and not yet confirmed on the phone. The row is **Still to test** since, and its first section is `TO_TEST`, **grouped by what H does rather than by version**: *Take any photo* (17), *Take one of these again* (15, each naming the photo — the washer, the rice cooker, 建国肉夹馍, the ARRI poster, 邪不压正 from across the room …), *In the app* (33) and *After an update* (5), newest first inside each. **The folding is the work, not the transcription.** This file's roadmap carries **136** pending entries, and a list of 136 is not a checklist: v379–v392, v406 and v407 are all *one* thing H can do — the washing machine taken again — and are one line. The oldest, **66 of them (v59–v152), are counted and not listed** on purpose: per-character correction, the deskew, the picker, the linked cards are in daily use and have simply never been confirmed in words, which is not the same as untested. So the row reads "70 checks waiting on the phone. 7 of 9 photo kinds never made here, 12 cases never tried." **THE RULE, the owner's twin of `WHATS_NEW` (v408): a PR that ships something only the phone can judge adds its line to `TO_TEST`, and the line goes when H says it works** — the same discipline, one list for the learner and one for the owner. **The `.diag` box holds 45 columns at 390 px, not 46** (measured: 358 px wide, 14 px of padding a side, a 12 px monospace character 7.2 px), so the budget for an entry's text is 35 columns after the `    v431  ` prefix; 28 entries were shortened against that ruler and **0 lines wrap** — the first cut let 20 wrap, and a wrapped line restarts at column 0 and breaks the list's alignment, which a screenshot showed and the column count had not. Checked by screenshot in light and dark; the english, admin, order and kind suites pass. Not yet field-checked — H's next look under Advanced settings is the check: are the twelve the right twelve, does the folded list match what he thinks is open, and does the deck half tell him anything he did not know?

### Field lessons that shaped the UI (keep)
- **Flow and UI:** four free corners on the crop frame with a perspective warp of the cut were built in v127 (H: characters photographed from the side are not recognised) and taken out again in v128 on H's request ("No, I don't want this. Leave it as it was.") — the frame is a rectangle with resizing corners; do not bring the quadrilateral back unasked · No tab switching for the AI (v31/v32) · button always visible, never replaced by the auto result (v32) · one action after framing (v39) · plain words instead of jargon and `·` shorthand (v25/v39) · three top-bar pills overflow at 390 px, so Deck only shows off the Learn tab (v25) · Chrome/Android does not repaint after the camera until touched (v34) · the card text keeps the photo's lines, a horizontal word is one line (v42) · reading starts by itself after the frame is released, no Read tap (v47) · the crop frame stays on the photo until Save (v50) · after grading the next card must start at the top of the screen (v53) · two taps on the front: photo = whole picture, character = answer (v55) · the static HTML must already match the first render (Deck pill hidden in index.html), otherwise the top bar jumps at load (v57) · `html` needs the page background, a `color-scheme` and an inline fallback in index.html, otherwise a line in the wrong colour flashes above the page at load (v58, kept for light and dark in v82).
- **Storage, deploys and network:** Android shares `.txt` but not `.json` (v3) · a cached 404 poisoned the dictionary once (SW caches only OK responses) · status text written into a DOM node captured before a re-render disappears silently — keep status in state and re-query (v47) · the inbox re-render previews only the inbox's readings — the Edit form's text state survives a tab tap, and previewing it before the pinyin library is loaded threw "pinyinPro is not defined" into every reading (v108) · github.io is unreliable from China, jsDelivr is not (v48/v49) · the reader's files must be reachable without the VPN too, hence the mirror fallback for `vendor/` (v56) · the worker's fallbacks help only a page the worker controls — a page with "SW no" fetched every reader file from github.io and hung for good; the page needs the same origin-then-mirror rule of its own, a way to ask an active worker to take it over, and a stall that ends a load (v335) · **one version number per deploy, not per feature — three PRs under one number leave the last two undeployed (v426, H at v425: "ich sehe keine sterne", and About said v425):** v425 went out three times in 25 minutes (the licences row, the Arphic text, the star), each PR bumping `APP_V`, the label and `zt-vN` to the same 425. The browser installs a new worker only when `sw.js` differs **byte for byte**, so the first deploy created the cache `zt-v425` and the two after it changed nothing — the phone kept serving the first deploy's `app.js` and `styles.css`. And every safety net agreed with it: the boot self-check compares `APP_V` to the label and both said 425, the mirror compares its `PWA vN` to the page's and both said 425, and About showed 425. **A feature can be absent from a phone whose every version marker is correct**, which is why "H is probably not updated yet" was the wrong first answer — the right question is whether that number was used twice. The number is a deploy counter; a second PR on the same day takes the next one even when the first is minutes old · a new worker must fetch the shell past the browser's HTTP cache, or rapid deploys leave the old app under a new cache name (v71) · the script carries its own version and checks it against the page's label at boot, so a mixed shell repairs itself (v72) · "the frame draws, nothing happens afterwards" on v92 was not reproducible in Chromium and vanished with the v93 update (VPN on) — cause never seen, most likely a mixed shell from the mirror, which caches each file on its own; first ask for More → Diagnostics before touching the reader (v93) · a reading that a corner drag superseded must abandon, or two results and two AI requests land on the same frame (v117) · the error log persists across updates, so an error in Diagnostics may come from an older script — compare the stack's line numbers with the current file before chasing it (v117) · an older app imports a file with fields it does not know without a word — every new export field needs the import to say what it did (v166–v167, the photos lost on a phone at v165) · Chrome's voice list says nothing about whether the phone can speak — the Xiaomi lists no voices and speaks Chinese (v165) · a tap on a layer that lets the page scroll must be read from the click event, not from pointerup — iOS Safari sends pointercancel there (v206, H's iPhone; the frame's own handles carry touch-action none and are unaffected) · an installed app keeps its old manifest for days; a new share entry needs a re-install through "Install app", and a home-screen shortcut never gets one (v167) · an app that holds one API key loses it the moment another provider is chosen — H's DeepSeek key had to survive the Qwen setup, hence one account per provider with the old key migrated (v172) · Android's share sheet appends the url field to the shared text, so the text must not carry the link itself, or WeChat shows it twice (v215) · a Blob put into two IndexedDB stores is stored twice — the inbox photo copied onto the card as `imgFull` doubled every phone's photo bytes until v214; keep one copy and a reference, copy only when the original goes · a long-running action must keep its state outside the row it was started from — a tab change re-renders the screen, the old row's status goes nowhere and a "running" guard swallows the next tap (v257, Translate all: "changed page, pressed again and no reaction"; the same rule as v47's status text in state). · **`git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` uses the LOCAL ref, and a merge made through the API does not update it — always `git fetch origin main` first, or the next version is built on top of the one before last (v458 and v459 were each caught by the version marker in the serving root, which is the only reason it was noticed)**
- **The reader:** a tilted frame is straightened before reading — Tesseract fails beyond a few degrees (v59) · Tesseract's per-symbol boxes are not to be trusted for Chinese: the heights are right, the horizontal ends drift, stop early on the last character or lose it altogether — take the line's ends from the image columns (v69/v75) · **what the reader sees must be a JPEG** — this Tesseract build misreads large canvas PNGs and WebPs (same pixels: JPEG 0.95 → the full line at 99 %, PNG → one character); intermediates stay PNG so only the last step is lossy — two JPEG generations in a row lost the line too (`READ_JPEG`, `deskewBlob` always hands back a JPEG, `jpegOf` re-encodes card images to JPEG 0.85 at save) · the reader is chaotic on large text: the same clean crop reads perfectly at one scale and as garbage at another, so read at several scales and let the readings compete (v73) · light text on a strong colour defeats the reader's own thresholding — a binarised copy reads it (v77) · shading (a curved bottle) defeats every brightness threshold, a chromaticity copy does not care (v95) · the score must not reward a soup of short lines, and a band only one pass saw or that is tiny beside the others is decoration (v95) · the AI must be allowed to say "unreadable" — asked only to correct, it invents (v95) · a traditional logo needs the traditional model, the simplified one can only approximate (v96) · confidence must weigh more than character count, and a text several passes agree on beats a lone near-equal score (v96) · the AI sees every competing reading, not just the winner (v96) · the AI may fix what was read weakly or what another reading offers, never a character every pass read clearly — asked for a sign, it answers with a common phrase (减展单车 → 共享单车, v143) · when the readings circle around one dictionary word, the dictionary decides before the AI is asked — the AI refused 养浴多 / 次乐多 / 开乐多 twice (v99) · every gate must judge by the same score as the competition, or a long soup of fragments switches the fallbacks off (v100) · the ink height must ignore solid decoration, or the text looks like fragments (v100) · a single line whose characters are as tall as the frame's ink is the text, however short — the fragment penalties are for soups beside real text, not for a lone 推 that ten passes agree on (v116) · a white character on a black plate has no chromaticity, so the chromaticity copies read noise there — they must lose, not be skipped (v116) · a frame one text height tall cannot hold two lines — a second "line" in it is decoration, and the pass must lose score for it, not be rewritten (v137) · bold outlined characters fill a tight frame's rows almost solid — the ink height must let dense rows ride inside a text band, or a one-line sticker reads as a twelve-line soup (v144) · whatever fills the corners of a rotated crop lands in every copy and in the ink height — it must be the crop's own dominant colour, not an edge pixel, not a median, not the border (v138) · six stroke edges per text row is the rule that keeps stripes out; four was tried for big characters and lost 业主直租 through a changed ink height (v138). · **the stroke medians do not read photos** (tried after v142, H: "can the stroke analysis also improve the word recognition in the photo?"): a shape re-ranker was measured in the harness — at every character position the candidates (the reading, the other passes, the dictionary, the true character) were compared with the binarised, thinned photo glyph at `charBox` by symmetric chamfer distance, truncated chamfer and the overlap of the medians drawn at the photo's stroke width, with a small shift-and-scale search. On 56 positions of 14 images the best measure kept 29 right characters, broke 24 and fixed 1; even on the clean print signs it broke 5 of 22, and the clean 台 of a bold banner lost to 后, 富 and 特. The medians are one 楷 style, the signs are bold, rounded and brush fonts, and the glyph box carries the neighbours, a logo oval or speckled stone. Both of H's actual failures (美团 read as 人美加, 减震单车 as 减震单生;) were wrong in length, where a per-position re-ranker cannot act at all. Not built; the matcher stays in the drawing sheet, where the strokes are real. · **A rounded bold display font can be a model limit — check the clean copy before touching the reader** (v169, H's 奈斯餐吧: gold rounded characters on a shaded blue panel, first framed loosely under the Latin "NESTO", then tightly around the four characters; H: "Why can't he figure this out?", "Still nonsense"): the loose frame reads two-line soups on the phone and in the harness — the Latin letters as a Chinese line (和人叨时) above the text as garbage — and the tight frame gives 广包看中 on the phone, 本了了 in the harness (a blob of the colour copy at 95 %). The deskew is right (the text sits at −9.5° in the frame, the straightened black-and-white copy is a clean, perfectly legible 奈斯餐吧), and the model still reads that clean copy as 夫斯均肥 / 雯斯豆妈 / 索斯餐妈 / 去斯餐凤 at six sizes from 80 to 370 px: 斯 always, 餐 half the time, 奈 and 吧 never; thinning the strokes makes it worse, the traditional reader gives 泰新宴吧 / 素箕窒旋. So no copy, size or angle helps — the model does not know this font's 奈 and 吧. The AI then invented "Guangbao Kanzhong (possibly a shop or brand name)" for 广包看中 instead of calling it bad. What would read it: a vision model that sees the crop — ruled out by H's own rule that photos never leave the phone, so it is H's decision, not a reader change. Not built.
- **Fixing a character and drawing:** one misread character is fixed by tapping it, not by retyping the line; the AI is asked first, the dictionary is the fallback (v61) · candidates first, drawing as the second level when the right character is missing; the photo character stays in view while drawing, because the system keyboard's handwriting pad hid it (v62) · the Tesseract worker has **one** logger: progress goes to `_ocrLog`, the handler of the running job, never to the status closure of whoever created the worker — the pad's reading once wrote "recognizing … 100%" into the photo's box and wiped the editor (v63) · action rows in the picker are flex (`.ckacts`), not the auto-fit grid, which broke the pad's buttons (v63) · the picker is two levels only, suggestions then drawing; no type field in it (v64) · the word-picking overlay (pinyin boxes on the photo, selection bar) went unused once the AI-first preview existed — removed with its Split into words button (v91) · inserting a character through the picker (+ before / + after, a trailing + on the strip) did not convince H in v91 and was removed in v92 — asked for again in v119 together with a Remove that can be found: a red button in the action row, not a text link at the right edge · the drawing pad is a full-screen sheet with a Done button — an inline pad below the fold went unseen, and reading after each stroke felt like being cut off (v65) · an automatic crop is a guess — let the hand correct it (drag/pinch on the photo square) (v70) · small black-on-white pad images are indifferent to PNG/JPEG (measured) (v73).

## Hard constraints (learned in the field — do not violate)
1. **No external dependencies / CDNs.** Must run offline and behind the GFW. System CJK fonts only. Libraries and data go into `vendor/` (licenses in `vendor/LICENSES.txt`).
2. **All paths relative** (`./…`). The app lives under a subpath (`/zeichentrainer/`).
3. **Persistence only via IndexedDB** (do not use localStorage/sessionStorage). `navigator.storage.persist()` is requested — Xiaomi/MIUI aggressively evicts storage of non-installed sites. The SW must **never cache non-OK responses** — a 404 cached during a deploy window poisoned the dictionary permanently once; `loadDict` additionally heals such entries.
4. **Phone-only deploys:** H uses GitHub only in the phone browser. Ship changes as small, clearly described PRs. As few files as possible; generate/commit binaries (icons, vendor data) in the repo, never ask H to upload them.
5. **Privacy rule:** Confidential text (real contracts, suppliers, company internals) must **never** end up in the public deck or repo. General vocabulary only. H's provider keys live in the Supabase function's secrets, never in the code (v191). Photos and card images stay on the device — the one exception (v173): the straightened framed area, at most 800 px, goes to a picture-capable AI provider when the reading is weak and H's switch is on, see the AI section; the daily usage row (v170) carries counts only.
6. **Files leave the device only via the share sheet:** programmatic blob downloads (`<a download>`) are silently blocked by Android/MIUI. Use `navigator.share` with a file — and Chrome/Android only shares whitelisted types (`.txt`/`.csv`/images/PDF yes, **`.json` no**), hence the `.json.txt` extension with `text/plain`.

## Design (iOS-style since v82, on H's request: "orient on a modern Apple app")
The lacquerware look (INK/BONE/VERM/JADE) was replaced in v82 by the treatment of a current iOS app. Light and dark follow the phone (`prefers-color-scheme`; `color-scheme: light dark`, two `theme-color` metas, inline fallback background in index.html so nothing flashes at load). The seal red stays as the tint, the big characters keep the serif.
- Tokens in `styles.css` (light / dark): `--bg` #F2F2F7 / #000 · `--card` #FFF / #1C1C1E · `--card2` #F2F2F7 / #2C2C2E · `--fill` #E9E9EE / #3A3A3C · `--label` #000 / #FFF · `--label2` #6E6E73 / #A1A1A6 · `--label3` #AEAEB2 / #6E6E73 · `--sep` hairline · `--tint` #C8372D / #E0483E (+ `--tint-soft`) · `--ok` #2FA36B / #3DBE7A (+ `--ok-soft`, for AI and verified) · `--bar` translucent bars · `--shadow` (light only). Radii: cards 16 (`--rc`), buttons and inputs 12/10 (`--r`).
- Fonts: UI = Apple system stack (`-apple-system`, SF Pro, PingFang SC, then Roboto/system-ui on Android); Hanzi = `'Songti SC','STSong','Noto Serif CJK SC','Source Han Serif SC','SimSun',serif` for the big characters, strips and rows; `--mono` only for timestamps and Diagnostics (the version label is hidden since v225). Pinyin is set in the UI font, semibold.
- Components: large title `识字` in the sticky, blurred top bar (no version label beside it since v225; the version sits in More → About) with stat capsules (Due/Done on Learn, Deck elsewhere — three overflow at 390 px) · translucent bottom tab bar, active tab in the tint · the study card and the done screen are white/dark cards with radius 16 · the **田字格 reticle** stays the signature element (since v223 one shape for every word card: the wide box at the card's width, 150 px tall per photo line, on `--card2`, hairline lines and corner ticks, dashed tint crosshair only for single characters; font fitted to the longest photo line — `frontLines`/`frontBox`; base font by character count 1→150px, 2→104, 3→74, 4–8→58, 9–12→44, 13+→34, capped at 72 px so the box keeps its height — the 260 px square for up to three characters went on H's "Bitte consistency!") · lists (Cards, More) are inset grouped rows with hairline separators and rounded ends · buttons: `.btn.primary` filled tint with white text, `.btn` tinted soft, `.btn.danger` red on soft, `.del` plain tint text, the three grades as tiles in the traffic light's colours (`--tint-soft`/`--warn-soft`/`--ok-soft` with the matching strong label, v421) · inputs are white/dark fields with a hairline inset, tint ring on focus · chips are `--fill` capsules, active = filled tint · the character strip buttons (`.ck`) are white/dark tiles with a hairline; low confidence = tint ring, AI candidate = green ring, chosen = filled tint (`.signed .ck.on` — the surface rule once outranked it and the chosen character showed white on white) · the reading bar (`.reading .bar`) is a 4 px `--fill` track with a tint segment sliding across.
- The script draws nothing in fixed colours: inline SVG uses `style="stroke:var(--…)"`, canvases read the tokens at paint time (`cssVar`) — the drawing pad's strokes are `--label`, its grid `--sep`, the photo view's padding `--fill`.
- The crop frame is independent of the theme: white dashed edge with a dark outline and white handles, nothing dimmed — it must stay visible on any photo colour.
- Readability rules kept from the old design: body 17 px, hints and labels 13–14 px in `--label2`, meanings 18 px, touch targets ≥ 44 px, inputs ≥ 16 px (no zoom), safe-area padding top and bottom, plain words instead of jargon.

## Didactics / SRS
- Loop: photo + character/word → tap to reveal → pinyin (+ pronunciation), meaning. No example sentences (H's decision), and no context word since v424.
- SM-2 light. The learner sees three grades since v421 — **Hard** (red), **Medium** (amber), **Easy** (green) — which map onto the scheduler's `again`, `good` and `easy`; the fourth grade `hard` (a small interval bump) is no longer reachable from the screen and stays in `schedule()` for the progress rows that carry it. `again` re-queues the card within the same session, behind the cards still to come — and when the session holds none, the next cards of the same filter are pulled forward so it never comes straight back (v428).
- Session = due cards + max. 8 new ones — **except a starred session, which holds every starred card** (v429: a star is a hand-picked list, not a category, so the cap and the due date do not withhold what the learner chose; the due and new ones lead, the rest follow by due date). "Pull forward" pulls future cards when nothing is due. **Card order** (v153, H: "provide choices for the order in which the flash cards are shown", described first and built on "Go"): More → Learning → "Card order" with the chips Oldest first (the old order: due cards by due date, new ones by creation), Newest first (both groups by creation, newest first) and Random (a fresh shuffle per session); due cards always come before new ones, the up to eight new cards are picked in that order, a tap rebuilds the session at once (setting `learnOrder`, `LEARN_ORDERS`, `orderCards` in `buildQueue`).

## Deck format
No built-in deck; all cards live in IndexedDB `custom`. Schema:
```
{ id:"坚果", c:"坚果", p:"jiānguǒ", m:"nuts", t:"Custom", at:1756800000000,   // id: the key (text while free, else 坚果#<at>) · t: Custom | Sign · at: creation time
  tags:["Chinese class","HSK 3"],     // optional: H's own labels (v133) — the Cards filter and the Learn filter
  seg:["坚果","\n","供应"],           // optional: word boundaries + photo line breaks for the front
  lb:"photo"|"auto",                    // where the line breaks came from (auto = estimated from the crop's shape)
  w:"…", wp:"…", wm:"…",              // dead since v424: the context word of the old built-in deck. Nothing creates, shows, edits or searches it any more; the fields are left on a card that has them rather than deleted, and export and import carry them like any other field
  shot:"shot_1756800000000",           // inbox photo the card came from (photo cleanup)
  mt:{ src:"llm"|"dict"|"phrasebook"|"nmt"|"gloss", verified:true|false, pending:false, suspect:"reason" },
  flag:true, flagNote:"…",            // review flag — the app's word for "this card looks wrong"
  star:true,                             // the learner's own mark (v425), set by the star on the card row or in the detail; no note, no meaning to the app
  alts:["养兴多","义乐多"],               // optional: the other readings of the photo (v96), for the AI check
  trad:"養樂多",                          // optional: the text as it stands on the photo, in traditional characters (v101); shown on the front, c stays simplified
  ml:"de",                               // the language of the meaning (v256) — absent = English: the dictionary, the phrasebook, the offline model and every card before v256
  ms:{ en:"nuts", de:"Nüsse" },          // every meaning the card got, by language (v265) — the app shows the one for its language when the card has it; a changed text keeps only the current one
  ai:{ zh, p, m, note, ok, bad, at, model }, // a waiting AI suggestion (bad: the AI calls the text OCR garbage)
  frame:{ x:0.02, y:0.52, w:0.96, h:0.46, a:0 }, // the frame the crop was cut with, as fractions of the photo (v244) — Crop again starts from it; cards before v244 have none and get the app's proposal
  reading:{ rect, at, failed },             // a card saved before its reading was done (v237, id reading#<at>): the frame it was saved with; c is empty until the reading fills it, failed = why it never did
  page:"page#1756800000000",                // v453: this card is one text of a page card; the list shows the page, Learn groups the page's texts, an item whose page is gone is an ordinary card again
  from:"page#1756800000000", fromT:"Midea — wash programmes", of:"page#1756800000000:快速" // v487/v503: a flashcard generated from a multicard's text — the multicard's id, its title as it stood (a fallback once the multicard is gone), and since v503 the id of the text itself; no img, no shot, no frame
}
A **page card** (v453) is `{ id:"page#<at>", kind:"page", t:"Page", c:<title>, name:{name,what,place}, ml, at, shot, items:[ids of its texts], tags:[the kind], mt:{src:"llm",verified:true}, v }` — no img (its picture is the photo through shot/imgFull), no progress row, never sent to the AI, not in the Deck count (v504); export and import carry it like any card.
```
Sign cards add `kind:"sign"`, `segs` (per line) and `gloss` (`[{w,p,m}]`, feeds the parts row); word cards from the Read path carry `gloss` too; any card saved from a photo carries `img` (crop) and `shot` (the inbox photo's id); **the whole photo is stored once** (v214, H's "Go" on the v213 audit's storage finding): `imgFull` exists only when the inbox photo is gone — `fullPhoto(d)` = `imgFull`, else the inbox photo through `shot` (the front toggle, the detail, the list thumbnail of a card without a crop — not repeated on the back, H); `saveSign` stores no copy while the inbox photo exists, `delShot` (the inbox's Delete, Photos → Delete N) first copies the photo into every card that references it (`keepPhoto`), `dedupePhotos` at boot drops the copy from cards of v213 and earlier whose inbox photo is still there (and the import drops it the same way), the export takes the whole photo from `fullPhoto`, so files stay the same, `photoBytes` counts it once, and the Edit form's Remove image drops `shot` too (until v213 the front still showed the inbox photo after the removal); saves about half of a phone's photo bytes (field-confirmed 2026-09-05, H: "Look both good" on v214 and the About line) — blobs, local only; in the export only with the "Include photos" checkbox, as `imgB64`/`imgFullB64` (v166).
Rules: **Pinyin only verified, with correct tones — never guess.** Meanings in English, or in the app's language from the AI (`ml`, v256). Dictionary/phrasebook prefills are `verified:false` until a human or the AI checked them; when unsure, flag instead of inventing.
New words come from photos (menus, signs, packaging).

## Play Store
The app goes to Google Play as a **Trusted Web Activity** — a thin Android wrapper (PWABuilder/Bubblewrap) that opens the live GitHub Pages URL full screen; the web app itself does not change, and taking the public site down would break every installed copy. H registers a **personal** Play Console account. H is a **German citizen resident in China** (corrected 2026-09-10 — earlier notes wrongly said a Chinese ID): Google takes a government photo ID from any country, so the German passport is the identity document, and it is the **address proof** that decides which country the account belongs to. That country lives in the payments profile and **cannot be changed afterwards** — a wrong one needs a whole new profile, so it is decided once. China is the honest choice, since that is where H lives and has a real address proof (residence permit, rental contract); a German profile would need an address H genuinely holds. Practical: the one-time fee needs a Visa/Mastercard, and the whole flow runs over the VPN. A personal account created now must pass a **closed test with at least 12 testers opted in for 14 continuous days** before it may publish to production. Google Play does not distribute to users in mainland China at all; the Chinese stores would need a 软著 and a Chinese company and are out of scope. **The commercial side — price, model, the launch case — is deliberately not in this file: the repo is public** (H, 2026-09-10). One consequence to respect: the paid/free choice is **irreversible on Play** (paid can become free, never the other way), it is settled outside this file, and it must be confirmed with H before the listing is created.
- **Done:** `privacy.html` in the repo root — Play requires a public privacy-policy URL (`https://henglicam.github.io/zeichentrainer/privacy.html`), and it describes the on-device storage, the daily usage counts and their switch, the owner's relay, the framed area sent to a picture provider, and feedback. It is not in the SW shell, so it needs no version bump. The manifest is TWA-ready (maskable icon, standalone, scope).
- **Decided rules:** the signing keystore never goes into the public repo — the package is built on H's side (pwabuilder.com from the phone) and the key stays there. `assetlinks.json` must live at the **origin root**, `henglicam.github.io/.well-known/assetlinks.json`, i.e. in a separate one-time repo `henglicam/henglicam.github.io`; a `.well-known` under the project path does not work for asset links. It carries the SHA-256 of the **Play App Signing** key, which exists only after the first upload — until then the wrapper shows a browser bar over the page, which is fine for testing.
- **What law applies today, and what triggers what (assessed 2026-09-11 on H's question "Welches Recht muss ich schon jetzt mit der Web App eigentlich einhalten?" — an assessment, not legal advice):** **German Impressumspflicht (§ 5 DDG)** binds *Diensteanbieter niedergelassen in Deutschland* and *geschäftsmäßige* services; H lives in China, the site is on GitHub Pages, the app is free — so today probably not. It bites the moment money flows **or** the Play listing exists, since Google displays and verifies every developer's name and address anyway. Nothing to publish before then: H's Beijing address does not belong on a public page one day earlier than it must. **GDPR** needs an EU establishment or the targeting of people *in* the EU; mere reachability is not targeting, so today probably outside — but the one thing that would be an opt-in question under it, and is an opt-out one today, is that **the online AI review is on by default** (`aiAutoOn()` is true unless the user unticks it, and `viaRelay()` means it works with no key), so a new user's card text goes to a provider in China from the first card, and photographed signs carry names, numbers and addresses. `privacy.html` says so honestly since v403; honest and lawful are not the same thing. **PIPL** covers processing of personal information of people in China, defines it widely enough to reach a random installation id, and wants a *separate* consent for sending it abroad — which the daily usage row to Supabase is. The APP备案 filing is for apps distributed in China and needs a Chinese business licence, so it stays out of reach and out of scope. **The open-source licences were the only duty already unmet**, and v425 closed it. **The open question is not a privacy one:** whether a foreigner in China on an employer-tied work permit may take side income at all — one hour with a Beijing advisor before the first payout, together with the PIPL questions.
- **Data Safety, before the first release (v397+):** the Console's Data Safety form is a separate declaration from `privacy.html` and must match what the code actually does, or the listing is a takedown risk. Since the usage reports and the relay the app does collect: a random installation id with the daily counts (on by default, switchable under More → Usage sharing), the same id with feedback, and AI calls routed through the owner's relay for phones without a key. Declare the collection and its purpose, that it is switchable, and that it travels over HTTPS; the id is random and carries no identity, which is what makes the declaration simple — but it must still be declared.
- **Still to do:** H creates the Play Console account → TWA package via pwabuilder.com from H's phone → first upload to a closed track → H pastes the Play App Signing SHA-256 from the Console → `assetlinks.json` content for the root repo → recruit the 12 testers and keep them opted in for 14 days → Data Safety form, store listing (screenshots and texts prepared by Claude) → production.

It passed because `READLOG` still held the **previous** case's "Asking the AI" line at the moment Playwright first polled, so the stand-up happened before the reading even started. v439 shifted the timing by a few hundred milliseconds and the case fell. **It was not assumed to be a flake: the same timing was forced on a v438 tree by clearing `READLOG` before the photo, and v438 fails identically** — so the app was never the cause. The case now clears `READLOG` first and stands `textLike` up on the reading's own `quick look:` line, which is deterministic and before `sureAngle`; **it passes on both the v438 and the v439 tree**, which is the proof that it tests the app and not the clock. The lesson is v419's one level down: a green check is only worth what its mechanism is, and the way to tell is to make the *old* tree fail. Layout is checked by screenshot at 390×844; anything derived from the reader's geometry is checked against the image itself (v69: a contact sheet of all character crops of the test sign, straight and tilted, exposed the drifting symbol boxes).

## Working with H — the how-to rules (v128, agreed after the four-corner episode)
**What H sends.** One request per message: a sentence, and a screenshot when it is about a screen. When the reader is wrong, More → Diagnostics → Share with it — the phone is the only place the reader can be watched from. "Leave it as it was" means: revert to the previous behaviour, no discussion.

**What Claude does with a request.**
1. **Restate before building.** One sentence: what changes for H on the phone. Two readings that lead to different work → one question, not five. Otherwise no questions.
2. **Size gate.** Wording, layout, a rule in the reader, a bug: build at once. **Anything that changes how H handles the app** (a new gesture, a new field or control, a new screen, a changed flow) is described first in three lines — what H does, what H sees, what it costs — and waits for "go". A "go" is for that description; if the built thing feels different, H says so and it is reverted in the same session.
3. **Only the ask.** No "while I'm at it" changes. Consistency passes, cleanups and refactors only when H asks for them.
4. **Field first.** A reader change is judged by the phone, not by the harness. Every claim about the phone is either seen on the phone (screenshot, diagnostics) or marked "not yet field-checked".
5. **One request, one PR, one version.** Every PR: the three version markers bumped, the suites that touch the change run, CLAUDE.md updated in the same PR, merged by Claude, branch reset onto main. A revert is a PR like any other, with its own version.
6. **CLAUDE.md is the memory.** Decisions, rejected features and field lessons go in with the reason; "Zieh CLAUDE.md nach" means consolidate into the current state, not a version log. What H rejected is not brought back unasked.
7. **Report short, in English.** What changed, what was verified and where, what is open. Honesty over confidence: "I don't know" beats a guess; limits are named.
8. **Wording and design.** Sentence case, plain words, no jargon (no "OCR"), no "·" shorthand; iOS-style tokens; pinyin in the UI font; the rules in Design and Hard constraints are not up for interpretation.
9. **Tone (H, v255): relaxed.** "This is a fun app. No formal, boring translations within the app. Customers are passionate language learners. Same for the design and layout." — every language addresses the learner as a friend (du, tu, tú, 해요체), no formal register, no stiff notices; design and layout stay light the same way.
- Build-first. Physical reality beats spec.
- On every change: confirm the app still runs with no network dependencies and relative paths.
